author: TGEU
title: The Trans Leaders Academy 2026-27 kicks off
content:
We are delighted to introduce the inspiring

Trans Leaders Academy

 Cohort 2026–27. Over the coming year, the 16 leaders will take part in virtual and in-person trainings and peer exchange sessions.


To further strengthen their practice, they will also have the opportunity to join the Spring

Leadership Kitchen Series

,

 a six-month coaching space made possible through a partnership between TGEU and

Spring

. Through the coaching, they will have space to reflect, share and grow in leadership while connecting with a wider community of global change-makers from diverse social and ecological justice movements.


We are excited to welcome this group and to witness their leadership journeys as they reflect, share and grow in community.


Meet the Trans Leaders Academy 2026–2027 cohort:


Alia Lehner (she/her)

 was born and raised in Austria. She is the State Secretary and Queer Representative of the Young Generation (JG) Upper Austria, and the State Secretary and Transgender Spokesperson of the SoHo Upper Austria.

Change-making  leadership vision:

To build an inclusive, courageous, and intersectional movement where trans people are empowered to lead, shape political decisions, and create lasting social change.


Beatriz Carmo Flores (she/her)

 is an activist and community organiser based in Portugal. As a Coordinator at GRIT, the trans reflection and intervention group of ILGA Portugal, she supports and strengthens community organising, from peer-support spaces to public advocacy.

Change-making vision:

To build collective power through community care, so that trans communities can lead the change for human rights while impacting positively each other’s lives and thrive together.


Evi Gümüssoy (they/them)

 is from Turkey and works on the TIN* & Refugees team at the TransInterQueer (TrIQ) organisation in Berlin.

Change-making leadership vision:

To transform these shared lived experiences into collective power by building community-rooted support networks that protect our sustainability, mental well-being, and joy.


Jononi Zulaikho (she/her)

 is a poet and artist actively contributing to Colored Qollective through translation and creating and holding space for trans and queer communities.

Change-making leadership vision:

To hear and see one another, speak openly about our differences and the privileges that shape our experiences, while remembering that, despite our differences, we remain connected in different ways and are part of a larger whole.


Mak Maslać (he/him)

 is a writer, editor and cultural worker based in Zagreb, Croatia. He is the editor-in-chief of VoxFeminae, a queer feminist online magazine focused on culture and societal phenomena, where he also writes on queer and feminist topics, literature and popular culture.

Change-making leadership vision:

To create and protect spaces for more open, critical and nuanced conversations about culture, queerness, sexuality and BDSM through writing, publishing and community work.


Maui Angela Miranda


(she/her)

 is a writer, editor and cultural worker based in Zagreb, Croatia. He is the editor-in-chief of VoxFeminae, a queer feminist online magazine focused on culture and societal phenomena, where he also writes on queer and feminist topics, literature and popular culture.

Change-making leadership vision:

To create sustainable systems of care that center racialized trans migrants. I aim to cultivate “care-full” spaces where trans individuals can heal from systemic racism while building collective resilience and joy.


Miia Kovanen (she/her)

 is from Tampere, Finland. In this project, she represents Transfeminiinit Ry / Transfeminines NGO. She works in the organisation under the title of a volunteer social assistant. She is also a member of the feminist organisation Naisasialiitto Unioni / The Finnish Women’s Association Unioni.

Change-making leadership vision:

To take on this new role given to her. Indeed, she has only been in the sphere of advocacy for a relatively short while. Her journey has necessitated rapid personal development, which she aims to continue in these new responsibilities.

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: ADHD, a Unicorn in the Psychiatric (Be)wilderness
content:
A

ttention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder was invented in America and appeared in the American Psychiatric Association’s 1980 DSM-III diagnosis manual. But what is it?


At an NIH 1998 consensus conference, the chairman asked a leading ADHD expert, Mark Vonnegut, but he couldn’t explain what ADHD is:

1,2

 “They cannot sit still … they are difficult and they aggravate their parents … the diagnosis is a mess … I think, you know, we, uhm, I, I do, I think, part of the problem is that the profession keeps changing the diagnoses.”


Today, ADHD is a contagious, fashionable diagnosis.

3

 When youngsters look up descriptions of people who say they “have” ADHD on social media, they may be convinced they “have” it too and may even self-diagnose.


The diagnostic criteria for ADHD are so vague that when I lecture and ask people to try the adult ADHD test

4,5

 on themselves, it never fails that one quarter to half the audience test positive. Dr Iona Heath, Former President of the UK Royal College of General Practitioners, said in August that “if you want the diagnosis, you will be able to get it.”

6

 Many people are proud of their diagnosis and a British comedian said he needed to try the test five times before he passed.


Those who are too quiet can get the diagnosis of “predominantly inattentive” ADHD. So, what about those in the middle? It is so absurd that I invented a disorder for healthy people, Adult Symptom Deficiency Disorder (ASDD), with a 10-item test that guarantees that no matter what your score is, there is a treatment for you.

7


ADHD is one of the oddest creatures in the psychiatric (be)wilderness. I do not dispute that some people suffer from their symptoms, but if you examine the central tenets of ADHD scientifically and logically, you’ll see that the diagnosis falls apart.

5


The latest misinformation, the Fogany review


On 9 October 2026, a so-called independent review of ADHD and autism was published. It took up 599 pages plus a 230-pages technical annex.

8

 The Acknowledgements on page 463 show that a huge amount of people had contributed to the report but there are no declarations of conflicts of interest for anyone.


The review noted that the current system is not working but the authors were sitting on the fence and didn’t dare tackle the biggest problem of all: overdiagnosis. This is remarkable considering that the report stated that, by the end of 2025, open referrals in England for ADHD assessment exceeded 560,000, more than 17 times the number recorded in 2019.


In 2011, Allen Frances, chairman for the DSM-IV task force, said that the responsibility for defining psychiatric conditions needs to be taken away from the American Psychiatric Association because new diagnoses are as dangerous as new drugs:

9


“We have remarkably casual procedures for defining the nature of conditions, yet they can lead to tens of millions being treated with drugs they may not need, and that may harm them.” Frances noted that DSM-IV created three false epidemics because the diagnostic criteria were too wide: ADHD, autism and childhood bipolar disorder.


As I shall explain below, the summary in the Fogany review presented highly misleading statements. It called ADHD a strongly genetically influenced neurodevelopmental disorder, which influences attention, communication, behaviour, learning and how people experience the world; the patients are neurodivergent; and the diagnosis can help explain difficulties that significantly impair a person’s functioning, participation and quality of life.


The Fogany review recommended banning direct-to-public advertising of NHS-funded ADHD and autism assessments. But when the

BMJ

published a news item about the review,

10

 it was accompanied by an ad for methylphenidate:


Methylphenidate is a narcotic on prescription used against ADHD. In the US, Ritalin, Adderall, and methamphetamine, all used against ADHD, are Schedule II controlled substances, which cocaine, oxycodone, and fentanyl also are.


Respectable medical journals avoid placing drug ads close to an article describing that type of drug or disease. But the

BMJ

 is no longer a respectable journal. This summer, the editor, Kamran Abbasi, refused to publish criticisms in print of its highly misleading suicide prevention articles

11

 even though he could have contributed to reducing the meaningless suicides caused by antidepressants by telling their readers that antidepressants do not protect against …

author: Unknown
title: Henry aus dem Antifa-Ost Verfahren ist gestorben!
content:
Henry Aulich ist tot. Er wurde 38 Jahre und starb heute in den frühen Morgenstunden, nachdem schon vor einigen Tagen die die lebenserhaltenden Maschinen abgeschaltet worden waren. Seit seinem Suizidversuch am 15. August 2026, bei dem er von einer S-Bahn erfasst und schwerst verletzt wurde, war er nicht mehr aus dem Koma erwacht.


Es war ein sonniger Dienstag im August, zu mehreren saßen wir zusammen, nach einem weiteren von über 50 Prozesstagen im Dresdner Antifa-Ost-Verfahren. Thema war auch Henry. Er war an diesem Tag nicht zum Prozess erschienen, denn wegen akuter Suizidalität war er in eine Psychiatrie eingewiesen worden. Vier Tage später sollte er von einer S-Bahn überrollt werden.


Seit 2013 im Visier des Staatsschutzes


Henry war seit 2013 im Visier der sächsischen Repressionsbehörden. Im Zusammenhang mit Ermittlungen gegen die Fanszene der BSG Chemie Leipzig wurde über Jahre gegen ihn wegen des Verdachts der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung ermittelt. Seine Telefone wurden überwacht, er wurde observiert, seine Kontakte erfasst. Auch besonders geschützte Gespräche wurden aufgezeichnet. 2016 wurde das Verfahren eingestellt. Der sächsische Datenschutzbeauftragte beanstandete später das Vorgehen des LKA und der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden.


Doch damit endete die staatliche Verfolgung nicht. Immer weitere Ermittlungen folgten, und die Wohnung seiner damaligen Partnerin und ihm wurde wiederholt durchsucht, einmal über 14 Stunden lang. Zu Anklagen kam es damals nicht.


Als Henry schließlich 2025 im Antifa-Ost-Verfahren angeklagt wurde, lagen bereits mehr als zwölf Jahre staatlicher Ermittlungen hinter ihm. Jahre, in denen es seinerseits immer auch immer wieder den Wunsch gab zu sterben.


Mehr als 50 Prozesstage und kein Ende


Henry saß nicht in Untersuchungshaft und kam er seit November 2025 zuverlässig zu den Verhandlungen nach Dresden. Über 50 Prozesstage, obwohl ihn nur ein vergleichsweise kleiner Teil der Anklage betraf. Die Verteidigung beantragte wiederholt vergeblich, sein Verfahren abzutrennen.


Auch der Versuch seiner Anwält:innen, einzelne Verhandlungstage früher enden zu lassen, damit Henry an einer notwendigen Therapie teilnehmen konnte, scheiterte am Gericht. Der Senat verwies auf das Beschleunigungsgebot, weil andere Angeklagte in Untersuchungshaft saßen.


Im Juli wurde Henry wegen akuter Selbstgefährdung in eine geschlossene Psychiatrie eingewiesen. Ein behandelnder Arzt empfahl eine dreimonatige Prozesspause für Henry, ein anderer Psychiater hielt ihn für verhandlungsfähig.


Am 12. August wurde Henry von der Polizei aus der Psychiatrie zur Verhandlung gebracht. Wie ein Möbelstück. So saß er dann da, von Tavor, einem starken Psychopharmakon etwas benommen wirkend die wenigen Stunden den verbleibenden Prozesstages an seinem Platz. Drei Tage später, am 15. August, wurde er in Leipzig von einer

S-Bahn erfasst

.


Selbst als Henry dann im Koma lag, wollte der OLG-Senat erst noch ein Gutachten über seine Verhandlungsfähigkeit einholen. Erst am 2. September wurde sein Verfahren schließlich abgetrennt.


Eine Frage der (Mit-)Verantwortung


Die Frage, welche Verantwortung die Richter:innen des Staatsschutzsenats des Oberlandesgerichts Dresden für den Umgang mit einem Menschen tragen, dessen akute Suizidgefährdung bekannt war, bleibt. Ebenso die Frage, was es mit einem Menschen macht, wenn er über mehr als ein Jahrzehnt immer wieder ins Visier staatlicher Ermittlungsbehörden gerät.


Jetzt also ist Henry tot


Henry galt einigen als ein gelinde gesagt schwieriger Mensch, wie es in einer differenzierten

Stellungnahme

 vom September beschrieben wird.


Zugleich gibt es jene die davon erzählen, er habe ihnen aus der Patsche geholfen, wenn es nötig war. Bei der

BSG Chemie Leipzig

 engagierte er sich über Jahre, wurde 2011 in den Aufsichtsrat gewählt und gehörte von 2012 bis 2015 dem Vorstand an. In ihrem

Nachruf

 vom 24. Oktober schreibt die BSG, Henry habe die positive Entwicklung des Vereins maßgeblich mitgestaltet.


Nach seinem Suizidversuch vom 15. August zeigte sich die

Rote Hilfe e.V.

 erschüttert und wütend.


Henry war eben nicht nur jener streitbarer Mensch, der über mehr als ein Jahrzehnt immer wieder ins Visier des sächsischen Staatsschutzes geriet. Es bleiben seine Freund:innen, seine Familie, darunter seine Kinder, und Weggefährt:innen.


Nach seinem Suizidversuch im August breitete sich eine

merkwürdige Stille

 aus. Nur hinter vorgehaltener Hand wurde darüber gesprochen …

author: Jenna Mahale
title: Pro-Israel Peers Call for Macklemore to Be Banned From the UK
content:
Fifty British peers have written to home secretary Shabana Mahmood urging her to ban American rapper Macklemore from the UK ahead of his Wembley gig this week. 


The letter, organised by ex-chair of Labour Friends of Israel Lord Walney, calls on Mahmood to revoke Macklemore’s electronic travel authorisation on the basis that proceeds from the tour will be donated to the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM).


Lord Walney’s letter claims the grassroots anti-genocide group has a “record of glorifying terrorism and intimidating elected representatives” – allegations that PYM denies and which are based on its positions regarding what counts as legitimate resistance and protest.  


The peers’ letter characterises a 2025 PYM campaign that

encouraged people

 to pressure Labour party figures over Palestine as “an attempt to coerce members of parliament through fear”. 


Signatories include former Conservative party chair Eric Pickles, former DUP leader Arlene Foster, former attorney general Lord Goldsmith, Lord Brady of Altrincham – appointed by Rishi Sunak – and Lord Roberts of Belgravia, who was appointed by Boris Johnson.


Macklemore announced his Free Palestine Tour – which quickly sold out its dates in Dublin, Paris and London – shortly after he was dropped as a support act on Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour last month. 


Pro-Israel

billionaire Robert Kraft

 spearheaded a ban on the rapper performing after he spoke out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza during shows at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium.


Lord Walney acted as a political violence advisor for the government between 2020 and 2025. 


In 2024, he

recommended the proscription

 of groups such as Palestine Action and Just Stop Oil while working for lobbying organisations in the arms and fossil fuel industries. 


That included a role as chair of the Purpose Business Coalition, whose members include oil giant BP and arms manufacturer Leonardo, which has extensive links to the Israeli military.

author: Access Now Advocacy Team
title: #NoExamShutdown: One step forward, another step back
content:
Every year, when exam season rolls around for students across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), many governments use the risk of cheating as an excuse to shut down the internet or block social media platforms. And every year, this results in millions of people losing connectivity, businesses grinding to a halt, and disruption to daily life across entire countries. Of course, exam shutdowns are not the only threat to education in the region;

students in Gaza

 have begun a third academic year in tents and makeshift spaces, while in Lebanon, nearly

100,000

 students were unable to return to school at all.


But across the wider MENA region, this year’s exam season saw mixed results for exam shutdowns. For the first time since Access Now,

SMEX,

 and the

Internet Society

 began tracking this phenomenon as part of the

#NoExamShutdown campaign

, the trend went in two different directions across the map. For example, Algeria, which has been a persistent offender for the past decade,

limited shutdown measures

 to the inside of exam centres, without disconnecting the rest of the country. Meanwhile Syria, which imposed

11 nationwide exam-related shutdowns just last year

, appears to have held its 2026 exams without any documented disruptions. On the other hand, Tunisia — a country previously ranked as having the

highest internet freedom environment

 in MENA — joined the offender list for the first time, imposing covert connectivity restrictions during both of its Baccalaureate exam sessions. Read on for more details of this year’s exam season results.


iraQ


sudan


syria


algeria


tunisia


jordan


india


✎ In Iraq, the numbers tell a complicated story


Iraq’s

exam-related internet shutdowns

 are now in their 11th consecutive year, with 2026 adding at least 34 documented disruptions, according to

Cloudflare Radar

 and

ISOC Pulse

 data.


The first set of disruptions occurred throughout June, aligned with the country’s middle and high school exam schedules. The Iraqi Ministry of Communications had

previously announced

 the shutdowns, planned to last approximately 90 minutes every morning on exam days. The Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad

later confirmed the shutdown

, vowing to develop a digital system to eliminate centralized exam distribution and, thus, the “need” to cut off internet access. However,

similar pledges have been made — and broken — before

. In August, a second wave of exam-related shutdowns hit on five consecutive mornings from August 26 to 31. The disruptions then continued daily until September 10, resuming from September 26 during postponed exams.


On average, this year’s disruptions were

shorter

 in duration than in 2025, and there were fewer of them overall, but whether this represents a genuine policy shift in the right direction, only time will tell.


✎ Sudan’s shutdowns continue amid war


For a

sixth consecutive year,

 Sudan’s government

cut connectivity during exams

, ordering

10 internet

 shutdowns between April 13-23. MTN Sudan

notified

 subscribers in advance of the disruptions, but these shutdowns were imposed amid the country’s

ongoing and devastating civil war

, making it even harder to justify the collective cost to people’s safety, access to information, income, and even healthcare.


✎ Syria: Breaking with the past?


Following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s tyrannical regime in 2024, many

wondered

 whether the new administration would break with the country’s longstanding pattern of implementing nationwide shutdowns during national exams. While authorities

stuck to tradition in 2025

, something appears to have shifted in 2026, with neither

Cloudflare

 nor

ISOC

 reporting any exam-related shutdowns during this year’s exam period. This marks the first time in at least a decade that Syria has refrained from imposing shutdowns during national exams; proof that even the most entrenched patterns can be broken.


✎ Algeria turns a page


When Baccalaureate exams began in Algeria on June 7 of this year, people across the country were pleasantly

surprised to find that their internet access had not been cut

, for the first time in 10 years. As the Minister of Education Mohamed Seghir Saâdaoui explained, connectivity would

henceforth only be imposed inside exam centres

author: labor4pal
title: Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: an Interview with Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman (UAWD Daily Struggle)
content:
Anthony Stoner October 26, 2026

Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman, authors of Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: The League of Revolutionary Black Workers, share their reflections on the UAW’s Black radical tradition, the tactic of the wildcat strike, and the importance of unions fighting for the working class as a whole.

In the 1960s, Chrysler—the only Big Three corporation whose operations remained largely in Detroit at the time—began to hire Black workers, many fresh from the U.S. South. They had the worst and most dangerous jobs, and Chrysler frequently fired them before they obtained UAW contract protections after a 90-day probation. In 1968, these conditions and the lack of representation by the white-dominated UAW—at that time led by Walter Reuther, whose “Administration Caucus” dominated the union then and for decades after his death led to a wildcat strike in the Dodge Main plant initiated by the Dodge Revolutionary Union Movement (DRUM) (A wildcat strike is a strike not officially authorized by a union). A number of other RUMs were then created around Detroit, and in 1969 the League of Revolutionary Black Workers (LRBW) was founded by Black militant labor organizers to help unite and aid struggles around the city. Among those organizers was Jerome Scott, who, along with Walda Katz-Fishman, has written an account of the LRBW, based on extensive interviews with surviving members of the League, their families and comrades. Their book, Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: The Story of the League of Revolutionary Black Workers, is available from University of Georgia Press.

—Anthony Stoner, UAW Local 4811

Anthony SToner: Why were wildcat strikes the tactic both DRUM and then the LRBW focused on? What’s the role of a wildcat strike for today?

Jerome scott: The wildcat strike became our principal tactic mainly because it was a two-edged sword. We could attack the company as well as struggle with the union. The company of course was and is the major enemy, but back in the day, and in some unions even today, the collaboration between the union and the corporation is not good for the workers themselves. And so we realized after the first wildcat strike (for us, and the first in the country for about fifty years) at Dodge Main that that wildcat strike really did attack both of our struggles. What we didn’t realize when we started it was that it was also a very offensive tactic. We were making the decisions; and the corporation and the union had to respond and defend against that, rather than the workers always being on the defensive. So the wildcat strike was a hell of a weapon.

AS: How did Doug Fraser [then head of UAW Chrysler Department] and the UAW International use the “flying squadron” during the 1973 wildcat?

JS: A little bit on the history of the flying squadron. It started with the United Mine Workers movement in Appalachia because of the rolling strikes that happened in the organizing of that union. It was an organized group of union members that they would take from strike event to strike event and try to make sure that nobody crossed the picket line. They were an apparatus that actually really backed up the picket lines in the strikes that were held in the heyday of organizing the UAW, the United Mine Workers, and so on. And the purpose was really to let the workers know that the International was part of this strike. So the concept of the flying squadron had a long tradition of respect from the union movement.

In our case, in our strike at Chrysler in 1973, we were able to shut down the entire Chrysler corporation for about a week; and that was because of the strategic nature of the Detroit Forge plant where I worked. There was only one other plant in the world that made the same parts that we made and it was a forging plant in [apartheid-era] South Africa. The corporation had done all it could do to try to break our strike, and try to break the picket line, but the picket line was going on 24/7.

What we learned later is that the corporation had called Solidarity House and said, “you have to do something about this strike.” And it was then that Fraser organized the historic flying squadron to come break our picket line rather than support it. And it was a pitched battle—it wasn’t like we saw them coming and laid down our picket signs—it was a big struggle. But eventually they were able to break our picket line and end our struggle after a week. Now the …

author: cnt.es
title: CNT denuncia la imposición de los servicios mínimos para la huelga general del 11N en Madrid
content:
Durante la jornada del viernes 23 de octubre, en que los sindicatos de la mesa sindical fuimos convocados para la supuesta negociación de los servicios mínimos por parte de la Comunidad de Madrid, lo que hemos presenciado es el autoritarismo que se ejerce desde esta administración y la constante falta de respeto a la clase trabajadora.


Esta convocatoria fue emplazada 7 días antes de la finalización del plazo de entrega de uno de los documentos necesarios para legalizar la huelga, la cual requiere de muchos pasos burocráticos para ser legalizada en su totalidad.


La costumbre es emplazar las negociaciones una vez finalizados todos los plazos para los sindicatos, sin embargo, quien moderaba comenzó la reunión poniendo en duda la capacidad negociadora de los sindicatos que aún no habían entregado la totalidad de los documentos.


Tras esto, en la reunión online, se enseñó un documento que había que leer en pantalla como supuesta propuesta, que se suele enviar días antes para su correcto estudio, con interrupciones, mostrándose los apartados sin sus títulos y con un continuo movimiento que dificultaba su correcta lectura.


No quedó un solo sindicato al que no faltasen al respeto por diferentes motivos, negándose continuamente a que pudiéramos tener una copia de la propuesta para poder analizarla y establecer una contrapropuesta con unos servicios mínimos que conciliasen las necesidades esenciales de la población con el derecho inalienable a la huelga de toda persona trabajadora.


Se comprometieron, tras dos horas y media de reunión, a enviar una copia a los sindicatos convocantes y emplazar una segunda reunión 3h después para que tuviéramos tiempo necesario para estudiar la propuesta.


La segunda parte de la reunión comenzó con la justificación de por qué nos habían tenido 3h esperando por un documento que nunca llegó, y es que, entre otras cuestiones, argumentaron que no tenían obligación de enviárnosla ni de negociar los servicios mínimos.


Los servicios esenciales no son algo baladí, la diferencia entre su fijación adecuada o abusiva implica la diferencia entre garantizar un servicio básico esencial o vulnerar el derecho fundamental a la huelga.


Esta actitud por parte de la administración regional de Madrid es otro caso más de su modus operandi a la hora de ningunear a los vecinos y vecinas de la Comunidad y a la clase trabajadora, como ya estamos comprobando con nuestras compañeras y compañeros de enseñanza, en plena huelga indefinida en la que, hasta la fecha, desde la Consejería de Educación no se han dignado a sentarse a negociar las reivindicaciones.

BAJEMOS LOS ALQUILERES

¡HUELGA GENERAL!

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Αίγυπτος: Στο εδώλιο η ανεξάρτητη δημοσιογραφία διά της… «αδειοδότησης»
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Αίγυπτος: Στο εδώλιο η ανεξάρτητη δημοσιογραφία διά της… «αδειοδότησης»


Σήμερα, 27 Οκτωβρίου 2026, πρόκειται να ξεκινήσει στο Κάιρο η δίκη της

Λίνα Ατάλα

 (Lina Atallah), συνιδρύτριας και διευθύντριας σύνταξης του ανεξάρτητου αιγυπτιακού δημοσιογραφικού μέσου

Μάντα Μασρ (Mada Masr)

,

με την κατηγορία ότι ίδρυσε, διαχειρίζεται και λειτουργεί ενημερωτική ιστοσελίδα χωρίς άδεια

 από τις αρχές.


Η παραπομπή σε δίκη ανακοινώθηκε στις 22 Οκτωβρίου, μόλις μία ημέρα μετά την πολύωρη ανάκρισή της από την Ανώτατη Εισαγγελία Κρατικής Ασφάλειας της Αιγύπτου. Η Ατάλα ανακρίθηκε για περισσότερο από έξι ώρες και αφέθηκε ελεύθερη με εγγύηση 100.000 αιγυπτιακών λιρών (περίπου 1.590€). Αρχικά αντιμετώπιζε και την κατηγορία της

διασποράς ψευδών ειδήσεων με σκοπό τη διατάραξη της δημόσιας τάξης

, η οποία δεν συμπεριλήφθηκε τελικά στο παραπεμπτικό της δίκης.


Η υπόθεση ενδέχεται να έχει σοβαρές συνέπειες για την ίδια την ύπαρξη του μέσου. Ο

αιγυπτιακός νόμος 180/2018

 προβλέπει για την παράβαση της υποχρέωσης αδειοδότησης πρόστιμο από ένα έως τρία εκατομμύρια αιγυπτιακές λίρες (περίπου από 15.900€ έως 47.700€). Το άρθρο 105 προβλέπει επίσης, σε περίπτωση καταδίκης, κλείσιμο της ιστοσελίδας και κατάσχεση του εξοπλισμού του μέσου.


Πρόκειται για την έκτη ποινική υπόθεση κατά του Μάντα Μασρ και των δημοσιογράφων του

μέσα σε έξι χρόνια

.


Αφορμή της δίωξης τα ρεπορτάζ για τις αιγυπτιακές φυλακές


Η τελευταία δίωξη ακολούθησε τη δημοσίευση

ερευνών του Μάντα Μασρ σχετικά με τις συνθήκες κράτησης και τις κινητοποιήσεις κρατουμένων στις αιγυπτιακές φυλακές

.


Σε

ρεπορτάζ της 14ης Οκτωβρίου

, το μέσο παρουσίασε καταγγελίες δικηγόρων και συγγενών κρατουμένων για κινητοποιήσεις σε διάφορες φυλακές, έπειτα από την αναβολή εφαρμογής, για ένα ολόκληρο έτος, του νέου Κώδικα Ποινικής Δικονομίας που προβλέπει μείωση στα όρια της προσωρινής κράτησης. Σημειωτέο ότι οι αιγυπτιακές αρχές δεν τηρούν ούτε τα όρια του σήμερα ισχύοντος Κώδικα, ωστόσο η κυβέρνηση του δικτάτορα Σίσι είχε παρουσιάσει τη μεταρρύθμιση ως «εγγύηση για τα δικαιώματα των κρατουμένων».


Σύμφωνα με τις μαρτυρίες που συγκέντρωσε το μέσο, κρατούμενοι πραγματοποίησαν απεργίες πείνας και άλλες διαμαρτυρίες, ενώ καταγγέλθηκαν βίαιες επεμβάσεις των δυνάμεων ασφαλείας και τιμωρητικές μεταγωγές σε απομακρυσμένες φυλακές. Το αιγυπτιακό υπουργείο Εσωτερικών ισχυρίστηκε ότι όλα είναι ψέματα.


Το συγκεκριμένο δημοσίευμα περιλαμβανόταν στον φάκελο που χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην ανάκριση της Ατάλα, μαζί με έγγραφα για το καθεστώς αδειοδότησης του Μάντα Μασρ, σύμφωνα με τους δικηγόρους του μέσου.


Είχε προηγηθεί, τον Αύγουστο του 2025, ακόμη μία

ποινική έρευνα

 μετά από ρεπορτάζ για καταγγελίες κακομεταχείρισης κρατουμένων στη φυλακή

Μπαντρ


3

. Τότε η Ατάλα ανακρίθηκε για τις δημοσιογραφικές πηγές και τη μεθοδολογία της έρευνας και αφέθηκε ελεύθερη με εγγύηση 30.000 λιρών (περίπου 480€).


Μια δεκαετία αποκλεισμών και διώξεων


Το Μάντα Μασρ ιδρύθηκε το 2013 από ομάδα Αιγύπτιων δημοσιογράφων και δημοσιεύει ανεξάρτητη ειδησεογραφία και έρευνες στα αραβικά και στα αγγλικά.


Από τον Μάιο του 2017 η ιστοσελίδα του παραμένει αποκλεισμένη από τους παρόχους διαδικτύου στην Αίγυπτο, στο πλαίσιο ευρύτερων αποκλεισμών εκατοντάδων ενημερωτικών και άλλων ιστοσελίδων.


Τον Νοέμβριο του 2019, αστυνομικοί με πολιτικά

εισέβαλαν στα γραφεία του μέσου

, κατέσχεσαν ηλεκτρονικές συσκευές και κράτησαν το προσωπικό επί ώρες. Τρεις δημοσιογράφοι, μεταξύ των οποίων η Ατάλα, προσήχθησαν και αργότερα αφέθηκαν ελεύθεροι. Την προηγούμενη ημέρα είχε συλληφθεί ο συντάκτης Σάντι Ζαλάτ (Shady Zalat). Η επιχείρηση ακολούθησε δημοσίευμα σχετικά με τον Μαχμούντ Αλ-Σίσι, γιο του Αιγύπτιου προέδρου, και τη θέση του

στις υπηρεσίες πληροφοριών

.


Τον Μάιο του 2020 η Ατάλα

συνελήφθη έξω από τις φυλακές Tora

, ενώ πραγματοποιούσε συνέντευξη με τη Λάιλα Σουέιφ (Laila Soueif), μητέρα του τότε κρατούμενου ακτιβιστή Αλάα Αμπντέλ Φατάχ (Alaa Abdel Fattah). Αφέθηκε ελεύθερη την ίδια ημέρα με εγγύηση.


Το 2022 τέσσερις δημοσιογράφοι του Μάντα Μασρ, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της Ατάλα, ανακρίθηκαν μετά από δημοσίευμα με καταγγελίες οικονομικών ατασθαλιών στο Κόμμα του Μέλλοντος του Έθνους (Mostaqbal Watan) το οποίο

δημιουργήθηκε από την Υπηρεσία Πληροφοριών του αιγυπτιακού στρατού για να υποστηρίζει τον δικτάτορα Σίσι

. Τρεις από τους δημοσιογράφους

παραπέμφθηκαν σε δίκη τον Μάρτιο του 2023

.


Τον Οκτώβριο του 2023 το Ανώτατο Συμβούλιο Ρύθμισης των ΜΜΕ ανακοίνωσε νέο εξάμηνο αποκλεισμό της …

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Was tun, wenn die Eigenbedarfskündigung ins Haus flattert?
content:
Einladung zum Nachbarschaftstreffen!


Am 27.10.2026 ab 19.00 Uhr in der Villa Felix


(Schreinerstr. 47)


Was tun, wenn die Eigenbedarfs- kündigung ins Haus flattert? Diese Frage müssen sich gerade sehr viele NachbarInnen stellen. Deswegen haben wir die Gruppe „Eigenbedarf kennt keine Kündigung“ (E3K) zu Gast.


E3K kämpft seit über sieben Jahren gemeinsam mit MieterInnen gegen Eigenbedarfs- kündigungen. Die Gruppe informiert, unterstützt Betroffene,


bereitet Gerichtsprozesse vor und organisiert solidarische Begleitungen zu Gerichts- terminen. Dabei konnten in den vergangenen Jahren zahlreiche Prozesse gemeinsam gewonnen werden.


Eigenbedarfskündigungen treffen selten eine einzelne Person. Sie können das ganze soziale Umfeld eines Hauses oder eines Kiezes verändern.


Kommt vorbei, bringt Eure Fragen und Erfahrungen mit – egal, ob ihr selbst betroffen seid oder einfach wissen wollt, was man tun kann. Wir freuen uns auf Euch!

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 27 octobre
content:
Le 27 octobre de l'éphéméride des luttes est une dure journée, parfois triste. Elle ne fait que marquer toujours plus profondément à quel point le monde qui nous entoure vit de notre tristesse et de notre souffrance, et donc toutes les raisons qui nous poussent à lutter.


1889 :

 A Gouliaï-Polié en Ukraine, naissance de Nestor Makhno, anarchiste Ukrainien qui mena une insurrection libertaire armée contre les prétentions bolcheviques, juste après la révolution Russe de 1917.


1962 :

 A Milan, au cours d'une manifestation en soutien aux révolutionnaires Cubains, l'étudiant Giovanni Ardizzone meurt renversé par une camionnette de police.


1968 :

 A Londres, 120.000 personnes manifestent contre la Guerre du Vietnam.


1969 :

 A Pise, au cours d'une manifestation organisée par

Potere Operaio

 contre le régime fasciste des Colonels en Grèce, des affrontements ont lieu entre les militant-e-s d'extrême-gauche et des néofascistes. La police intervient et une grenade lacrymogène tirée en plein visage tue le jeune Cesare Pardini, militant d'extrême-gauche.


1971 :

 En Irlande du Nord, l'IRA abat deux membres de l'armée anglaise à Rosemount, près de Derry et un troisième est tué par une mine de l'IRA à Kinawley. Le même jour, un membre du Royal Ulster Constabulary est tué à Toome par l'IRA.


1977 :

 - En Allemagne, funérailles de Baader, Ensslin et Raspe, militant-e-s de la Fraction Armée Rouge (RAF). Plus d'un millier de personnes sont présentes et sont bloquées par un triple cordon de police.


 A Gênes, les Brigades Rouges incendient les voitures de cinq responsables de la Démocratie Chrétienne, le parti au pouvoir.


1980 :

 En Irlande du Nord, les prisonniers de l'IRA revendiquent le statut de prisonniers de guerre en commençant une grève de la faim.


1982 :

 En Irlande du Nord, l'IRA abat trois membres des l'armée royale anglaise.


1991 :

 Au Pérou, arrestation de l'anarchiste Andrés Villaverde pour sabotage, qui sera maintenu longtemps en prison sans que rien ne soit possible de prouver contre lui.


1994 :

 A Berlin, le K.O.M.I.T.E.E attaque un bâtiment de l'armée à l'aide de plusieurs engins incendiaires.


1997 :

 En Ontario, c'est la plus grande grève de l'histoire de l'université et des écoles aux Amériques : plus de 2.1 millions d'étudiant-e-s y participent.


2005 :

 A Clichy-sous-Bois, Zyed et Bouna, deux jeunes poursuivis par la BAC, se réfugient dans un transformateur électrique et y meurent. S'ensuivront de grandes émeutes et une déclaration de couvre-feu, tandis que l'état d'urgence sera déclaré en région parisienne.


2006 :

 A Oaxaca au Mexique, lors de la répression contre le soulèvement de la ville contre le gouverneur, le journaliste anarchiste d'Indymedia Brad Will est abattu par la police.


2013 :

 A Nijni-Novgorod en Russie, un centre de recrutement de l'armée est attaqué au cocktail molotov. L'anarchiste Ilya Romanov, blessé, sera arrêté par la police.


2018 :

 A Titz en Rhénanie-du-Nord, dans la nuit, quatre bus de la société autocariste « Tirtey »

sont incendiés

 près de la mine à ciel ouvert. Il y en aurait pour plus de 400.000 euros de dégâts. L'attaque incendiaire n'est pas revendiquée, mais elle parle d'elle-même, dans un contexte local de lutte directe contre un projet d'extraction de charbon et de répression.


Voir aussi

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 27 octobre, qui offre notamment une biographie conséquente de Makhno.

author: Unknown
title: "Lula'yı zafere toplumsal taban, kitle seferberliği ve demokrasi taşıdı"
content:
Aralarında “Toplumsal Cinsiyet ve Eşitsizlikler: Brezilya'da Demokrasinin Sınırları” başlıklı kitabının da yer aldığı birçok yapıtın yazarı Brasilia Üniversitesi (UnB) Siyaset Bilimi Profesörü

 

Flávia Biroli başkanlık seçimlerini ülkenin popüler gazetelerinden

 Folha de São Paulo'da "Lula'yı zafere toplumsal taban, kitle seferberliği ve demokrasi taşıdı" başlıklı makalesiyle değerlendirdi. Biroli, Lula'nın kampanyasının 

Brezilyalıların irkilerek baba ve oğul Bolsonarolar'ın pandemi günlerine geri dönüşü temsil ettiklerini hatırlamalarına yardımcı olarak başarıya ulaştığına dikkat çekti. 


Siyaset bilimci, tarihçi ve feminist kuramcı Biroli, 2005'ten bu yana Brasília Üniversitesi'nde (UnB) ders veriyor ve halen Siyaset Bilimi Enstitüsü'nde profesör olarak görev yapıyor. 2018–2020 arasında Brezilya Siyaset Bilimi Derneğinin (ABCP) başkanlığını üstlendi; 2009–2017 arasında Revista Brasileira de Ciência Política dergisinin editörlüğünü yürüttü. Araştırmaları özellikle demokrasi, toplumsal eşitsizlikler, feminist siyaset teorisi, neoliberalizm ve yeni muhafazakârlık üzerinde yoğunlaşıyor. Önemli eserleri arasında Feminizm ve Demokrasi (Luis Felipe Miguel ile, 2014), Toplumsal Cinsiyet ve Eşitsizlikler: Brezilya'da Demokrasinin Sınırları (2018) ve Toplumsal Cinsiyet, Yeni Muhafazakârlık ve Demokrasi (Maria das Dores Campos Machado ve Juan Marco Vaggione ile, 2020) de yer alıyor.


Bu pazar (25 Ekim) tanık olduğumuz şey, son iki haftada giderek büyüyen bir dalganın sonucuydu. Lula ikinci turu kazandı, çünkü İşçi Partisi (PT) hâlâ geniş bir toplumsal tabana sahip. Bu taban, tarihsel olarak örgütlü kesimlerin, 2013'ten bu yana daha güçlü bir örgütsel varlık kazanan toplumsal hareketlerin ve o ana kadar potansiyeli bilinmeyen bir gücün birleşiminden oluşuyor: Bu ülkenin dört bir yanında sokaklara çıkan, aralarında oldukça genç öğrencilerin de önemli bir yer tuttuğu gençliğin gücü. Bu toplumsal taban aşırı sağı durdurmaya kararlı olduğu için Milletvekili André Janones'in sosyal medya atağı karşılık buldu.


PT'nin zaferi, bir siyasal programa sahip olmanın fark yarattığını da gösteriyor. Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Parti - PL), PT karşıtlığına bel bağladı; halk karşıtı tutumlarının artık savunulamaz hâle geldiğini anlamıştı. Ancak yeterince açıklanmayan bir “büyük kesinti” programıyla bir tür sağcı Lulacılığı birleştirmeye çalışan, inandırıcı görünmeyen bir taklidin ötesine geçemedi. Bu kez geniş cephe aşağıdan kuruldu. Birleşik Sağlık Sistemi'nin (SUS), asgari ücrette reel artışın, iş dışında bir yaşamın, kamusal eğitimin, Bolsa Família aile yardımı programının ve altyapı yatırımlarının (elektrik, su sarnıçları) savunulması, somut bir içeriğe sahip demokrasi savunusu olarak yaygınlaştı. Soyut bir kavramın ötesine geçti.


Demokrasiyi kitle seferberliğiyle savunurken, nelerin söz konusu olduğunun kavranması, hep bir arada oy kullanmayanların oranını ve geçersiz oyları azaltarak seçim sonucunu değiştirdi. Birinci ve ikinci tur arasında boş oyların oranı yüzde 1,84'ten yüzde 1,12'ye; geçersiz oyların oranı yüzde 2,93'ten yüzde 2,12'ye geriledi. Asıl etki, sandığa gitmeme oranının yüzde 21,08'den yüzde 19,21'e düşmesinde görüldü. Ancak Lula'nın oylarındaki artış bu farkı da aşıyor; bu da seçmenlerin oy tercihlerini değiştirdiğini gösteriyor.


Evet, ülke bölünmüş durumda. Ulusal Kongre de aşırı sağın gücünü ortaya koyuyor. Ancak nispi temsil sistemiyle belirlenen parlamento üyelikleri için kullanılan oylarla cumhurbaşkanlığı için kullanılan oylar arasında önemli bir fark var. İnsanların günlük yaşamlarını etkileyecek bir tehdidin açıkça ortaya konması, baba Jair Bolsonaro hükümetinin keyfî uygulamalarını yeniden hatırlattı. Haberler, halkla yapılan söyleşiler ve internet mizahı, pandemi felaketini yeniden gündeme getirdi. Baba Bolsonaro'nun gerçek ve olası şiddet örnekleri olarak hafızalarda yer etmiş kabalıkları, oğulun alaycı davranışlarıyla yeniden canlandı.


Öğleden sonra ülkede, seçmenlerin oy kullanmasının engellenmesine yönelik girişimlere tanık olundu. Bu son derece ağır bir durum ve seçim suçu oluşturuyor. Bu yazıyı bitirdiğim sırada, Bolsonaro yanlısı kesimden seçilmiş bazı parlamenterler, bir kez daha seçim sonuçlarını kabul etmeyeceklerinin işaretlerini veriyor. Önümüzde hareketli günler var ve demokratik kurumlar bir kez daha sınanacak.


Ancak bu kez iş başında, son haftalardaki sokak gösterilerinden güç alan, solda seferber olmuş bir siyasal hareket var.


(FB/EK)

author: infolibre
title: Εκδηλώσεις, Τρίτη 27/10
content:
>Η νεολαία και οι λαοί της Ευρώπης μίλησαν – Η ομορφιά βρίσκεται στον αγώνα!, 19:00 Εκτός των Τειχών


>Προβολή ταινίας και συζήτηση για το κίνημα στη Γαλλία, 19:00 Πάντειο


Εκδήλωση: Η νεολαία και οι λαοί της Ευρώπης μίλησαν – Η ομορφιά βρίσκεται στον αγώνα!


Προβολή ταινίας και συζήτηση για το κίνημα στη Γαλλία


Την Τρίτη 27/10, στις 19:00 στο αίθριο του Παντείου (αν ο καιρός δε μας το επιτρέψει θα μεταφερθούμε σε αίθουσα) θα προβάλουμε το ντοκιμαντέρ «Η ιστορία των κίτρινων γιλέκων από εμάς». Θα ακολουθήσει συζήτηση με καλεσμένο συντρόφι που μένει στη Γαλλία και συμμετέχει στις κινητοποιήσεις που λαμβάνουν χώρα την τελευταία περίοδο.


Οι εικόνες από τις μεγάλες διαδηλώσεις και συγκρούσεις στους δρόμους του Παρισιού μας γεμίζουν έμπνευση και ανασύρουν στη συλλογική μνήμη το δυναμικό φοιτητικό κίνημα του 23′ και τις τεράστιες απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις και πορείες των Τεμπών. Ταυτόχρονα, τα αδιέξοδα που προώθησαν τη γαλλική εργατική τάξη σε έναν αγώνα που φαίνεται διαρκής και αμετάκλητος είναι τα ίδια με αυτά που αντιμετωπίζουμε όσο εξοντωνόμαστε στη δουλειά (μεταφορικά και κυριολεκτικά) για έναν μισθό που τελειώνει στα μέσα του μήνα αφού ξοδευτεί στο υπέρογκο και ολοένα αυξανόμενο κόστος ζωής και όσο η κρατική μέριμνα συρρικνώνεται και κάθε πτυχή της ζωής μας βυθίζεται στην επισφάλεια. Από τα ρημαγμένα σχολεία και τις επικίνδυνες κτιριακές υποδομές, στις ελλείψεις διδακτικού προσωπικού, από το διαλυμένο δημόσιο σύστημα υγείας, από την εκπαιδευτική αναδιάρθρωση που υποτάσσει τα πανεπιστήμια στους νόμους της αγοράς και πετάει εκτός χιλιάδες από εμάς που δεν έχουμε την άνεση να σπουδάσουμε με τους ασφυκτικούς όρους που επιβάλλει το υπουργείο.


Και όλα αυτά μας οδηγούν σε ένα ερώτημα και μια επιτακτική ανάγκη: πώς μπροστά σε αυτά τα αδιέξοδα θα ανοίξουμε δρόμους αντίστασης στην πραγματικότητα που μας συνθλίβει; Πώς η κατάσταση στη Γαλλία, αλλά και σε άλλες ευρωπαϊκές χώρες θα πάψει να είναι ειδησεογραφικό θέαμα και θα γειωθεί στο εδώ και τώρα, στο ελληνικό εργατικό, μαθητικό και φοιτητικό κίνημα, στις δικές μας διεκδικήσεις με όρους έμπνευσης; Η πρόσφατη πανεκπαιδευτική απεργία που έφερε χιλιάδες μαθητές, φοιτητές και εκπαιδευτικούς στον δρόμο αποτυπώνει ακριβώς αυτό το κλίμα: το ξεχείλισμα της οργής, το ότι δεν αντέχουμε άλλο και η μόνη μας διέξοδος είναι ο αγώνας και η ολομέτωπη σύγκρουση με το σύστημα που υποτιμά τις ζωές μας και τις καθιστά αναλώσιμες.


Εμείς θα πούμε ότι δεν έχουμε ακριβώς την απάντηση, αλλά ξέρουμε ότι τα κινήματα δε συνδέονται με reels, αλλά με πραγματικές σχέσεις αγώνα και ανταλλαγή εμπειριών στη βάση των κοινών μας αναγκών και επιθυμιών. Σας καλούμε όλους όλες και όλα λοιπόν στον κοινωνικό και πολιτικό μας χώρο, να ανταλλάξουμε σκεπτικά και να ζυμωθούμε γύρω από τους τρόπους και τα εργαλεία συνέχισης του αγώνα.


Αυτόνομη Πρωτοβουλία Παντείου

title: Κοινή επιστολή 7 σωματείων για άμεσα μέτρα στήριξης στους εργαζόμενους της Pizza Fan
content:
Κοινή επιστολή 7 σωματείων για άμεσα μέτρα στήριξης στους εργαζόμενους της Pizza Fan.


ΠΡΟΣ: 1. Υπουργείο Εργασίας και Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης


Γρ. κ. Κεραμέως


2. Κεντρική Διοίκηση Επιθεώρηση Εργασίας


Γρ. κ Τζιλιβάκη


ΘΕΜΑ: Κατεπείγον αίτημα για την άμεση οικονομική στήριξη και την πλήρη διασφάλιση των εργασιακών και μισθολογικών δικαιωμάτων των εργαζομένων στην Pizza Fan


Αποστέλλουμε την παρούσα επιστολή με κατεπείγοντα χαρακτήρα, λόγω των πρόσφατων εξελίξεων στα καταστήματα της Pizza Fan, οι οποίες δημιουργούν σοβαρή ανησυχία για την οικονομική επιβίωση και την εργασιακή ασφάλεια εκατοντάδων εργαζομένων. Τα σωματεία διανομέων, μαγείρων, λαντζιέρηδων ζητάμε την άμεση παρέμβαση του Υπουργείου Εργασίας και της Επιθεώρησης Εργασίας, προκειμένου να προστατευτούν οι εργαζόμενοι/ες και να διασφαλιστεί η καταβολή του συνόλου των νόμιμων αποδοχών και αποζημιώσεών τους.


1. Άμεση έκτακτη ειδική οικονομική ενίσχυση των εργαζομένων για έξι μήνες


Αιτούμαστε τη θέσπιση και την άμεση καταβολή έκτακτης ειδικής οικονομικής ενίσχυσης για όλους τους εργαζόμενους στα καταστήματα της Pizza Fan, είτε αυτά λειτουργούν με εταιρική μορφή είτε μέσω συστήματος δικαιόχρησης (franchise), στο ύψος των 880 ευρώ μηνιαίως για τους επόμενους έξι μήνες. Η ενίσχυση αυτή κρίνεται αναγκαία για την αντιμετώπιση των άμεσων οικονομικών συνεπειών που υφίστανται οι εργαζόμενοι/ες εξαιτίας των πρόσφατων εξελίξεων. Επισημαίνουμε ότι ακόμη και το ποσό των 880 ευρώ, υπό τις σημερινές συνθήκες ακρίβειας και αυξημένου κόστους διαβίωσης, καλύπτει μόλις στοιχειωδώς τις βασικές ανάγκες ενός εργαζομένου/ης. Για τον λόγο αυτό, η άμεση ενεργοποίηση ενός ειδικού μέτρου στήριξης αποτελεί επιτακτική ανάγκη.


2. Άμεση διασφάλιση των οφειλόμενων αποδοχών και έλεγχος ενδεχόμενης μεταβίβασης επιχειρήσεων


Ζητάμε να διερευνηθεί άμεσα κάθε περίπτωση μεταβίβασης ή συνέχισης της επιχειρηματικής δραστηριότητας με αλλαγή ΑΦΜ, εταιρικής επωνυμίας ή φορέα εκμετάλλευσης, εφόσον αυτή ενδέχεται να χρησιμοποιείται για την αποφυγή καταβολής οφειλών προς τους εργαζομένους. Η συνέχιση της ίδιας δραστηριότητας υπό διαφορετικό επιχειρηματικό σχήμα δεν πρέπει να οδηγεί στην απώλεια ή στην υπονόμευση των εργασιακών δικαιωμάτων. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, ζητάμε την εφαρμογή των προβλεπόμενων διατάξεων του Π.Δ. 178/2002, καθώς και κάθε άλλου σχετικού μέτρου που απαιτείται.


3. Ειδικότερα, ζητούμε να παρέμβει άμεσα το Υπουργείο ώστε να διασφαλιστεί η εξόφληση όλων των οφειλόμενων δεδουλευμένων αποδοχών του τρέχοντος μήνα Οκτωβρίου, της αναλογίας του Δώρου Χριστουγέννων και του επιδόματος αδείας, καθώς και κάθε άλλης νόμιμης μισθολογικής υποχρέωσης που απορρέει από την εργασιακή σχέση. Παράλληλα, ζητάμε να εξεταστεί η ευθύνη κάθε εμπλεκόμενου, σύμφωνα με την ισχύουσα νομοθεσία, ώστε να μην καταλήξουν οι εργαζόμενοι απλήρωτοι και χωρίς ουσιαστική δυνατότητα διεκδίκησης των δικαιωμάτων τους.


Τέλος, ζητούμε τη διενέργεια ενδελεχών και άμεσων ελέγχων σε όλα τα καταστήματα της Pizza Fan, εταιρικά και franchise, για τις καταγγελλόμενες και δικαστικά διαπιστωμένες παραβάσεις που αφορούν την παράνομη υποδηλωμένη εργασία και την καταβολή μειωμένων αποδοχών σε σχέση με την πραγματική εργασία. Να αξιοποιηθούν οι σχετικές δικαστικές αποφάσεις, οι καταγγελίες και τα στοιχεία των Επιθεωρήσεων Εργασίας (ΣΕΠΕ), να καταλογιστούν οι προβλεπόμενες ευθύνες και να διασφαλιστεί η πλήρης αποκατάσταση και αναδρομική αποζημίωση των εργαζομένων για κάθε μισθολογική απώλεια.

author: Mada Masr
title: Mada Masr to challenge constitutionality of media law in Lina Attalah’s first court hearing
content:
During the first session in Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah’s trial on Tuesday morning, her defense counsel is to petition the court for access to evidence in the case, including documentation held by media regulators regarding the applications for a license that the organization has repeatedly filed since 2018.


It will also challenge the constitutionality of articles in the law regulating the press, requesting that the case file be referred to the Supreme Constitutional Court or that the defense counsel be granted authorization to file its own case before the court.


Attalah is present at the New Cairo misdemeanor court to attend the first hearing in her trial on charges of establishing, managing and operating a website without a license, following her investigation by the Supreme State Security Prosecution on October 21.


Lawyers are also set to attend the New Cairo court session on behalf of the Journalists Syndicate, which said on Monday that it has submitted a formal memorandum to the Supreme Media Regulatory Council “regarding the crisis over Mada Masr’s license application and the legal action linked to it.”


The memo stresses that there were violations of due process in the administrative handling of Mada Masr’s licensing application, that Mada Masr was not notified of the decision and that the proper recourse is “a challenge before the administrative judiciary rather than criminal prosecution,” according to a statement issued on Monday evening by syndicate head Khaled al-Balshy, which Mada Masr reviewed.


The syndicate’s lawyers are to submit a legal memorandum to the court during the Tuesday session in support of Mada Masr, based on arguments laid out in their memo to the SMRC.


More broadly, the syndicate called for a review of the licensing rules, as stated by Balshy.


The Supreme State Security Prosecution referred Attalah to the court on Thursday, less than 24 hours after questioning her on charges of running a website without a license and of publishing false news, with the latter accusation dropped from the charge sheet in the trial referral.


Lawyer Hassan al-Azhari, Mada Masr’s legal counsel,

described

the “haste” in the referral and its scheduling as “unjustified urgency,” given the absence of circumstances in the case that require rapid resolution.


During trial proceedings, the defense counsel will seek from the court full access to evidence in the case, including the facts of the licensing procedures and related notifications, details of the charges Attalah is accused of and the time period over which it is alleged that the crime took place.


The defense team is also set to ask the court to grant them access to the full case file and to request that the court access all documentation regarding Mada Masr’s licensing application held by the SMRC.


It will request that the original SMRC notification rejecting Mada Masr’s license, which was not delivered to the organization, be brought before the court. The defense counsel will challenge the claim that Attalah received notice of rejection decision, requesting proof of its receipt.


Mada Masr has applied on multiple occasions since 2018 for a license to operate, when a new law organizing the media and the press was

passed

, resubmitting its application 2020 upon the issuance of its bylaws.


It received no response from the regulatory council at the time. Instead, Attalah was informed by prosecutors, during a separate interrogation she was summoned to in 2022, that the SMRC had rejected the organization’s license application. Mada Masr responded by filing a lawsuit challenging the council’s failure to notify it of its decision.


Mada Masr will submit a memorandum to the court challenging the constitutionality of Articles 6 and 105 of Law 180/2018 Regulating the Press, the Media and the SMRC, arguing that they violate seven articles of the

Constitution

: 65, 70, 71, 92, 95, 96 and 211.


In light of this, the defense is asking that the court either suspend the case and refer it to the Supreme Constitutional Court or that it permit the lawyers to file a case before the constitutional court themselves to seek a ruling on whether the two articles of the media law are consistent with the constitutional provisions specified.


Article 6 of the media law states that “websites may not be established or managed in the Arab Republic of Egypt, nor may offices or branches of websites operating from outside the country be managed …

author: Albashir Dahab
title: Delayed Rains and Broken Routes: War and Climate Crisis in North Darfur’s Jebel Issa
content:
All names of individuals interviewed for this article have been changed their safety and privacy. 


The Fatal Rain of Wadi Saleh


In mid-September 2026, when rain finally touched the parched soil of Jebel Issa in North Darfur’s Al-Malha locality, it did not bring life, but rather severe ecological and economic devastation.


Under normal conditions along this fragile Sahelian belt, the rainy season begins in mid-June or early July and extends through late September This predictable precipitation serves as the ultimate lifeline for rainfed millet and sorghum farming, as well as the primary water source for livestock grazing across the northern Darfur plains. This year, however, unprecedented climate variability left the skies dry until 12 September.


When a sudden isolated downpour finally struck the western sectors of Jebel Issa livestock already severely weakened by months of starvation, scorching heat, and gruelling treks between depleted pastures and distant wells suffered immediate thermal and physical shock. Over three consecutive days, from 12 to 14 September, more than 420 head of sheep perished in Wadi Saleh alone, with additional unrecorded livestock deaths reported across neighbouring valleys.


Local livestock that have died from thermal shock after delayed rain. Photo credit: Albashir Dahab / Local Reporting Network.


‘The animals had been walking exhausting multi-kilometer distances every day searching for withered pasture left over from the previous year just to reach the few functional water points,’

explains Hassan Ahmed (name changed), representative of the Jebel Issa Emergency Response Room. ‘They arrived at the wells severely malnourished and dehydrated When the sudden downpour hit, accompanied by an abrupt steep temperature drop their weakened bodies simply could not endure the extreme climatic shock.’


In rural Darfur, livestock ownership carries a deeply collective social weight. ‘These 420 sheep were managed collectively by 16 caretakers, but under our traditional social structure, each caretaker manages a combined herd belonging to extended families brothers and kin’ Ahmed adds: ‘Wiping out these herds means destroying the entire financial safety net and accumulated wealth for dozens of vulnerable households in a single weekend’.


Regional Climate Anomalies and Sahelian Pressure


The crisis in Jebel Issa is not an isolated weather anomaly. It reflects a broader accelerating climate shift across the northern Sahelian belt. According to regional climate assessments and data from international bodies like the

Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change

 (IPCC), this zone is experiencing extreme rainfall variability characterised by shorter highly erratic rainy windows interspersed with prolonged, intense dry spells.


In Jebel Issa where subsistence farming relies strictly on rainfall without irrigation machinery or artificial reservoirs these delayed rains have disrupted the delicate ecological balance. According to estimates from the

Food and Agriculture Organization

 (FAO), regional cereal production across vulnerable belts in Darfur has plummeted sharply due to the convergence of delayed rainfall and conflict. Furthermore, the localised nature of the recent rainfall left the northern and eastern sectors of Jebel Issa completely dry, creating stark disparities where some farming councils received a single downpour while adjacent areas received not a single drop.


Weaponised Geography: Blocked Routes and Economic Siege


Jebel Issa sits roughly 35 kilometers from the administrative centre of Al-Malha. Jebel Issa serves as the central economic agricultural and water hub for a vast cluster of surrounding village councils including Wadi Hora, Jabra, Wadi Bisha, Wadi Tandis, and Del Sari. Neighboring areas such as Wadi Akhdar, Al-Har, Um Saro, Aito, Ashar, and Abkran face identical climatic conditions and rely entirely on Jebel Issa’s central infrastructure.


Wells in Jebel Issa are a source of water for a much wider region. Some currently stand empty. Photo credit: Albashir Dahab / Local Reporting Network.


Historically, communities in North Darfur weathered severe dry spells through vibrant cross-border trade and commercial supply lines moving along three major trade arteries: the Al-Dabbah route connecting to Northern Sudan, the Mellit route leading deeper into Darfur, and the northern Triangle (Al-Muthalath) border highway linking Sudan to Libya and Egypt.

author: Rachel Dubale
title: Eyes open in Addis
content:
If I squeeze my eyes shut and cover them with my hands, perhaps all of this will disappear. My father used to tell me something similar when, at an age perhaps already too old for it, I would whisper to him: “I’m afraid of the dark.”

“

Richo

,” he would say, “why in the world would you be scared of the dark? The dark is something we can make and unmake. See?” He would then cover my eyes with his big, calloused hands. “I made the dark for you.” And so I would fall asleep, covering my eyes with my hands and making my own dark.

So many years have passed since then — years in which I have learned not only how to make my own dark, but how to fill my eyes with the brightest colors: the green of my fields, the yellow suns of the Antilles, and the red of those tomato sauces shared over plates of pasta with the people I love.

With time I have also learned, and wanted

more

 and

more

 and

more

, to see and live those same colors lined up in a row: green-yellow-red. And again: green-yellow-red, the flag of my country of origin, Ethiopia. Sometimes for a few months at a time, during summers spent in the capital; sometimes buried in tedious readings, retracing its legendary history; other times — for longer, for months — trying to learn its script, so curved, as I did when I lived in Addis Ababa from September 2022 into 2023.

That time, in 2022, when I spent several months in the capital, is perhaps one of the times I most distinctly remember feeling like a child again: trying to memorize the

fidel

, the Ethiopic script, from the blackboard, slowly reading one letter after another, and then hoping that somehow a sentence that made sense in Amharic would come out of my mouth.

Perhaps it was also one of those times when, unconsciously becoming a little like a child again — learning how to read and write in a new language, discovering everything from scratch — I decided to do what my father had told me years before and cover my eyes with my hands.

By the time I arrived in Addis Ababa, the war in Tigray — mainly, but not solely, pitting Tigrayan forces led by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) against the Ethiopian federal government — had been going on for almost two years. Just two months later, in November, the two sides signed the so-called

Pretoria Agreement

, committing to a permanent cessation of hostilities. And yet, even in the capital, at least to me, the war and the tensions it had brought to the surface continued to come in fragments.

I remember, in order:

When the war came knocking at the edges of the city. That January of 2023 I was walking through the streets of Asko, right at the edge of the capital, wearing a traditional Wollo dress from the Amhara region.

All dressed up with my cousins, we hummed songs to celebrate Timket, the Ethiopian Orthodox festival marking the baptism of Jesus in the River Jordan, and were laughing our heads off about who had been hit by the most lemons — during Timket, young men traditionally toss lemons or limes toward girls they are interested in, as a sort of courtship — when some police officers on the street told us to keep it down. “And then,” they added, “you should be ashamed of wearing those clothes. We are celebrating Timket, not one particular ethnic group.” Ouch.

It took me, in fact, a little while — and an explanation from my cousins — to understand what I had initially taken as an insult to my sense of style. The traditional Amhara dress, it turned out, was not read simply as a dress but almost as a political statement in support of Amhara identity amid tensions around ethnicity — who was who, who was supposedly better than whom — that had been growing for years and that the war in Tigray had only exacerbated.

Funnily enough, this happened just as Amhara forces, which had fought alongside Ethiopian federal troops during the war, were reportedly

beginning to withdraw

 from parts of Tigray, seemingly in line with the provisions of the Pretoria Agreement. Yet on the streets of Addis, some of the tensions left by the war were proving harder to leave behind.

Something similar happened, for similar reasons, when I was denied access to my own home. Every March, Addis Ababa dresses itself in green-yellow-red to commemorate the majestic victory at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, when Ethiopian troops, led by Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu Betul, defeated the invading Italian army. Yet that year, even a victory remembered as pan-Ethiopian seemed to …

author: Mwangi Githahu
title: Kenya-US Relations: What the Immediate Future May Hold Under New Envoy
content:
A Sesotho proverb says, “Those who eat people, cry; those who eat a crocodile, laugh.” This proverb shows that reactions and alignments shift entirely based on whose interests are affected (we grieve when our friends are harmed, but rejoice when an adversary is neutralized).


Conversely, Lord Palmerston, a 19th-century Anglo-Irish nobleman and statesman who was UK prime minister, is reported to have said, “We have no eternal allies, and we have no perpetual enemies. Our interests are eternal and perpetual, and those interests it is our duty to follow.” 


Incoming US Ambassador to Kenya, Henry Wooster, who was unanimously confirmed by the US Senate at the end of September, less than a year ahead of what promises to be an unpredictable and highly volatile electoral contest, claims the US has no skin in the Kenyan game other than support for a peaceful and stable process. 


Wooster would say that, of course; he is a career diplomat.

He is coming to Nairobi to replace former ambassador Meg Whitman, a corporate executive appointed through political connections and seen by many observers as unusually close to President William Ruto for a diplomat. Kenyans will soon find out whether the new man picks up the old script, rewrites his own, or practices what he preached to the Senate confirmation committee.


Nevertheless, it’s fair to argue that over the last six decades Kenya has hosted its fair share of what some might call “interfering US diplomats”. As such, it would not be unusual for Wooster, who previously served as the chargé d’affaires at the US Embassy in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, managing operations amid severe security challenges, to change his tune once he hits the ground between mid-November and early December 2026.


As a former US Army Reserve and Special Forces officer who also worked as a foreign policy adviser for the US Joint Special Operations Command, he’s likely familiar with last-minute changes. From what I understand, military culture broadly relies on rapidly issuing adjustments to an existing plan. I suppose observers like myself will have to wait and see if the state hands-off policy survives.


At this juncture, I feel it may be instructive to look back at a few instances where the US was not as laissez-faire in Kenyan politics as they might wish us to believe.


As unpalatable as foreign influence on our politics is to many progressive Kenyans, the reality is that, as things stand, it is almost unavoidable. 


History shows that international interest in Kenyan elections typically intensifies in the years leading up to the polling date, and foreign envoys actively seek early ties with emerging leaders. 


Just look at how Western diplomats have been sniffing around Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, who has emerged as a potentially strong contender in the 2027 presidential election.


In August this year, Sifuna held closed-door meetings with several Western diplomats and high commissioners, chief among them the British High Commissioner, the outgoing French ambassador, the EU ambassador, and the German ambassador. 


In fact, the only major Western power whose ambassador hasn’t met with Sifuna is the United States. This is only because, as we have seen, President Trump’s pick as Washington’s man in Nairobi has yet to present his credentials officially, signalling his assumption of office.


This is not to say that the US has not got its beady eye on Sifuna. In January, he met with Susan M. Burns, Chargé d’affaires of the US Embassy in Nairobi, as well as US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, with whom he discussed expanding American business investments and creating jobs for Kenyan youth. Later in March, Sifuna met with Deputy Chief of Mission Marc Dillard at the US embassy in Nairobi.  


As much as the meetings with other Western diplomats show their curiosity about Sifuna, perhaps the most influential meeting, if it happens, will be with Ambassador-designate Wooster. Depending on how it goes, and what Burns, Landau, and Dillard collectively make of Sifuna and his chances, such a meeting could signal that the West has found another person they could “do business with”, to coin a phrase.


Meanwhile, Sifuna is not alone in attracting the USA’s attention. All current Kenyan presidential hopefuls, including President Ruto, have either already visited the United States or are planning trips there. author: Abahlali_3
title: Worsening Violence as the Election Comes Closer
content:
25 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo Press Statement

Worsening Violence as the Election Comes Closer

Our country is one of the most violent in the world, worse than some war zones. The rate of violence against women and the rate of murders committed by young men against other young men are among the highest in the world. There is violence in the home and in communities, violence from ordinary people, politicians, criminals and the armed forces in service of the state and the rich.

Our country and its people have been deeply damaged by generations of oppression, which has continued into the present for many people, especially the poor. The ANC has never pursued a project of healing, a project of restoring the humanity of our people and our society. They have just made themselves rich, leaving most of us poor and living in a broken society, a broken society in which the poor continue to be ruled with violence.

Things are getting worse. In KwaZulu-Natal armed mobs now parade through the streets accompanied by the police. People have been driven from their homes and livelihoods, assaulted and killed. The rise of the right, including violent fascist organisations, is a matter of grave concern for our movement and all people of good conscience.

As the election approaches, violence is worsening. So far 43 people have been killed, including people from the ANC, IFP and MKP. The political killings that are taking place are another grave concern for our movement. In a free, democratic country everyone should be free to campaign for election without fear. We know very well that the killing will not be confined to politicians. As killing becomes more common, more and more activists will be targeted in the years ahead.

Right now, the atmosphere in Durban is particularly threatening. Political intolerance has reached a fever pitch. The danger can be felt everywhere. Many politicians and parties have been complicit, and none have built a project in support of healing and a just peace. People are being assaulted and sometimes beaten to death in the streets. The political assassinations continue and will continue after the election as the politicians fight for power and money.

While the situation is at its worst in Durban and KwaZulu-Natal, it is moving into other parts of the country. ANC people have been killed in Katlehong.

People are being encouraged to hate, attack and kill as the election comes closer. But elections come and go. Every time there is an election, politicians come into our communities with promises, food and t-shirts and then they leave. We don’t see them until the next election comes. To them we are voting fodder, people who can be lied to and bribed, and not citizens of a democracy, or even just full human beings.

We have had elections for more than thirty years and the poor remain poor and without land, water, sanitation, electricity and housing. Our dignity continues to be vandalised by the state and the organised power of the rich. We continue to live with our suffering. This election will not resolve any of the problems that we face, and yet we are being encouraged to hate, attack and kill, and to support politicians and parties that are encouraging hate and are involved in political violence.

We cannot now glorify elections as the only thing that can resolve our problems and ensure that our dignity as human beings is recognised. Elections can be important, but all our advances as a movement and as a class have come from building our own power, popular democratic power. We must never allow politicians to divide us. We must never be divided by people who only come to our communities to lie to us when they seek power and then leave us poor and oppressed.

After careful discussions, we have agreed to encourage our members, and others who look to our movement for political direction, to vote according to their conscience if they wish to vote, but not to support those who have disappointed and betrayed them in the past, and who have made the poor suffer for more than thirty years. They must not vote for people who are trying to divide the poor with ethnic politics and political intolerance, for the corrupt who steal from the poor or for people who are xenophobic. They must not vote for any politicians or parties that encourage hate and violence.

When this election has passed, the oppressed will remain oppressed, there will be greater political intolerance and our society will be even more violent …

author: Ndivhuwo Mukwevho
title: Multi-million rand sports facility finally opens in Limpopo
content:
Finally, Waterval residents in Limpopo outside of Elim Hospital are now able to utilise their R55-million sports facility having waited for over a decade of delays. The Waterval facility is not the only one that has been neglected by Limpopo municipalities. Earlier this year,

Elitsha

reported on the R1.4-million upgrades to

Makwarela Stadium

 that never happened.


How it all started


The Waterval sports facility, which consists of a soccer field and a tennis court, was officially handed over to the Waterval community earlier this month. This came as welcome relief to local residents who had already lost hope that the facility would ever open. At one stage, it was left abandoned and turned into a drug den and a hiding place for criminals.


The facility is set to be utilised for various sporting codes by the local communities and schools. “At last, our children have got a ground where they can play their football with ease. Even though we had to wait for years for the facility to be completed, we are happy now that the ground is ours. To be honest, I am one of the people who had already lost hope that one day, the facility will ever be used for our benefit,” says Cedric Mulaudzi, a resident of Waterval.


Mulaudzi told

Elitsha

 that his 11-year-old son was not yet born when construction work began on the Waterval sports facility. “I am just happy that my son, who was not yet born when construction work started, will now have a place where he will be able to mature his football career,” says Mulaudzi.


The Waterval sports facility is the only decent, modern sports facility in the area and will be utilised by Mpheni, Shirly, Elim and other local communities.


Politically motivated?


“Why did it take too long for our government to complete this facility? This means that if it takes our government more than 10-years to complete just one stadium!” says Mulaudzi.


Nelson Mudzanani, who was born and raised in Waterval, also has questions about the timing of the project’s completion, while welcoming its completion. “For years, we have asked questions to the local municipality [Makhado] on why it was taking too long for them to complete the project and we never received any response. But now, we are due for elections in the coming weeks, and all of a sudden the stadium is finally completed. I just hope that the timing is not politically motivated,” says Mudzanani.


He believes that the sports facility will go a long way in empowering the local communities. “Those who want to exercise and those who want to play various sporting codes now have a decent place to do so. I just hope that the facility will be maintained accordingly,” he says.


During the handover of the Waterval sports facility, Makhado mayor, Dorcus Mboyi urged the local communities to utilise the facility properly and refrain from vandalising it. She also extended apologies for the delays they endured during the construction of the facility.
