author: April Holcombe
title: China’s forgotten miracle makers
content:
History has no parallel for modern China’s economic transformation. To what do we owe the China “miracle”, in which annual GDP growth averaged 9 percent over 40 years, wages up roughly tenfold in 30 years, and more high-speed rail built in ten years than the rest of the world in all time?

In the heyday of globalisation, people said China proved the magic of free markets and free trade. These days, people are more likely to attribute the country’s success to some special Chinese characteristic, such as its state-directed investment or its “Communist” dictatorship. 

These perspectives share in common a wilful or ignorant blindness to capitalism’s real wealth creators. Economic value comes neither from the market’s “invisible hand” nor the state’s “guiding hand”, but plain old everyday hands. The secret to China’s “miracle” is the not-so-miraculous condition of its working class.

Beginning in the 1990s, the greatest ever number of wage labourers was assembled through the collusion of profit-hungry foreign capital with millions of venal bureaucrats and their repressive state machine. Three hundred million people decamped from rural poverty to seek better lives in China’s cities, while urban compatriots in state-owned mines and mills lost their livelihoods through merciless privatisation.

China’s working class is legally stratified into “migrant” and “resident”, subject to the severest dictatorship of their bosses, and deprived of political rights to speak out or unionise. Apply hundreds of billions in Western and Taiwanese investments, lather, rinse, repeat for decades, and voilà! You have the most “miraculous” economic growth in capitalist history. 

China’s migrant workforce

We are used to hearing about how important migrants are to Western economies, but migration—the internal kind from village to city, not country-to-country—has been even more critical to China’s boom. In the 1990s, the government enticed young villagers with the prospect of independence, new experiences and better pay in newly established, deregulated Special Economic Zones with low wages and low taxes.

Lu Qingmin first left her family’s half-acre farm and came to Dongguan, a burgeoning megacity in the southern manufacturing heartland of the Pearl River Delta, in the early 2000s. Bosses preferred migrant women like her, considering them doubly docile. Writer Leslie Chang, in her 2008 book

Factory Girls

, described Lu’s experiences at her first job in a Hong Kong-owned alarm clock factory:

“A day on the assembly line stretched from eight in the morning until midnight—thirteen hours on the job plus two breaks for meals—and workers labored every day for weeks on end. From the moment she entered the factory she wanted to leave.”

The Pearl River Delta opened wide to investment in such sweatshops, and American-style hyper-individualism flowed in with it. Self-help books, life-coaching gurus, pyramid schemes, talent markets, unregulated colleges: each refracted through the false prism of empowerment what migrant workers already felt in their bones:

you are on your own

.

Hukou

: China’s internal visa system

Every migrant who left for the cities took the same thing with them: their rural

hukou

(户口), a residential registration that acts like an internal passport. Originally designed under Mao Zedong in 1958 to prohibit rural-to-urban movement altogether, the

hukou

household registration system was repurposed to create a pliant, defenceless workforce with second-class citizenship wherever it went.

Out-of-town

hukou

holders, also called the “floating population”, now represent just under half of the country’s workforce. Registered to villages far away, they are denied health insurance and pensions by the local government where they actually live. Many cities bar them from buying property, and local schools charge significant sums to teach their children. 

Think of them like the United States’ undocumented immigrants, who can get driver’s licences but not Social Security, who work in practically every key industry, but technically are not supposed to be there at all. Except there are now as many in China as the entire US population.

China does not offer the equivalent of America’s birthright citizenship: children inherit their parents’

hukou

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Students demand climate action and ‘No Cop-Outs at COP31’
content:
About 400 students and supporters took to the streets of Gadigal Country/Sydney on October 24 to demand urgent climate action ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November, which is being co-hosted by Australia and Turkey.

The rally called for serious climate commitments, including no new or expanded coal and gas, binding emissions targets and a just transition for workers and communities.

Students gathered at Sydney Town Hall to hear musicians performing climate-related songs and from speakers, before marching to the NSW Labor Party headquarters.

Performances by the Sydney Knitting Nannas, Eva Diana and Gailla set an optimistic and energetic tone.

They were followed by speakers, including Scott Franks, Wonnarua Elder and climate campaigner; Hannah Ferguson, founder of Cheek Media and independent candidate for Grayndler; Nanna Eury from the Knitting Nannas; Zack Schofield from Rising Tide; international human rights lawyer and climate activist Kavita Naidu; Ash, Aishling and Alissa students from the Australian Youth Climate Coalition AYCC); and NSW Greens MLC Sue Higginson.

Naidu emphasised the importance of listening to Pacific communities who are on the frontline of the climate emergency. “For us, going beyond 1.5 degrees warming is a death sentence that we will not be quiet about.”

She said addressing climate change can’t mean that Global South countries are exploited for the raw materials that are required for renewable technologies. “We reject all false solutions, including carbon offset and storage, nuclear energy, geoengineering and green or blue colonialism.

“We reject the dispossession of the land and ocean because of developed states need for transition … this is not just and equitable.”

Ferguson said federal Labor had refused to consider a duty of care for young people. “We have a NSW Premier who is in bed with the fossil fuel industry.”

Higginson celebrated the establishment of the Great Koala National Park, which passed through parliament the previous day. “People power can win!”

The rally was organised by Sydney Students for Climate (SSFC), a new coalition of students across Sydney who are concerned about climate inaction. It was MC’d by SSFC organisers Oscar Nellist and Lucy Millet, two students from the University of Sydney.

It was supported by at least 35 climate, student and social justice organisations, including Fridays for Future, the Sydney Knitting Nannas, Rising Tide, People’s Climate Assembly, Teachers for Climate, Bob Brown Foundation and many others.

It was also supported by independent and Greens MPs, including Greens leader David Shoebridge, independent MP for Bradfield Nicolette Boele, Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi and independent Senator David Pocock.

Millet told the crowd that Labor’s support for fossil fuel projects has left Australia on the backfoot for 2050 deadlines. “They need to represent us, the people, at COP31 and not the coal and gas companies.

“Climate action now is necessary and we will not settle for anything less.”

Nellist told Green Left he was inspired to organise the rally because COP31 was coming up and it seemed like no one was paying attention to the climate emergency.

“Australia is co-hosting the COP with Turkey, and Labor environment minister Chris Bowen is acting as the lead negotiator. We have to put pressure on them and show that we want real commitments for the climate.

“We have seen more frequent natural disasters in the past few years, including the recent disaster in Nepal and fires in Indonesia … with an El Niño summer coming up, it’s likely we will see more heatwaves and bushfires here in Australia.

“We need to act urgently to reduce emissions and transition to renewable energy.”

Nellist, Millet and many of the SSFS organisers were among the tens of thousands of students who walked out of classes as part of the Greta-Thunberg-led school strike for climate movement in 2019, which in Sydney culminated in an 80,000 strong rally in the Domain.

“We want to bring back the energy and momentum the climate movement had in 2019 before the COVID lockdowns,” Nellist said.

In addition to widespread support here, SSFC received messages of support from around the world, including from students in Belgium, the United States, Britain and Turkey.

[Sydney Students for Climate are holding a debrief meeting at Victoria Park on October 31. Oscar Nellist and Lucy Millet will be speaking at a Green Left public meeting about climate change on October 29 …

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Review: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History by Benjamin Moser
content:
Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History

 by US writer and Pulitzer Prize winner Benjamin Moser is a useful contribution to uncover the history of opposition to Zionism within modern Judaism. It traces the history of anti-Zionism from the late 19th Century through the lives of several anti-Zionist Jews across the Middle East, Latin America, Africa, Europe and the US.

Moser begins in the late 19th Century in the Russian Empire, where the deep oppression that the Jewish population faced led to a cultural Zionism that, among other things, sought to revive Hebrew. One of its leaders was Aaron Samuel Tamares. But around the same time, there was also a territorial, national, and racial Zionism being developed by figures like Theodor Herzl. Published in 1896, Herzl’s 

Der Judenstaat

 (The State of the Jews) gave a racial definition to Jewish people, as opposed to the then-dominant idea of Jews being a religious community. It also argued that European anti-semitism could never be eradicated and an independent Jewish state was therefore necessary.

In response to Herzl, the cultural Zionism of Tamares and many other rabbis quickly became an explicit anti-Zionism. They were among the first to criticise how Herzl’s Zionism reinforced the existing anti-semitism of the time by defining the Jewish population as a “race” and “foreign elements” in their own countries.

Tamares did not reject Jewish communities in Palestine despite being an anti-Zionist. But he ferociously opposed the establishment of a Jewish state. To him, such a project was inextricably linked to Western imperialism. He asked why the European powers “should make recompense for 

their 

wrongdoings by handing over foreign property, 

Ottoman

land”?’

When the British began that process with the establishment of the British Mandate after World War One, the Zionist movement remained on the fringes within the Jewish population as it had when Herzl published 

Der Judenstaat

. In 1917, for example, Zionist groups in England had no more than four thousand members between them.

Moser describes the early days of the British Mandate through Jacob Israel de Haan. When de Haan emigrated from the Netherlands to Palestine in 1919, he was among the most prominent Dutch Zionists. But after seeing the violence of the Zionist groups against the indigenous population of both the Palestinian Muslims and Orthodox Jews, he quickly became a leading figure of the Agudah, an anti-Zionist, Orthodox Jewish organisation.

De Haan’s articles were some of the first to document the growing Zionist domination of Palestine in the early 1920s. He explained “that no Arab is allowed to live in Tel Aviv. That no Arab is received in a Jewish hotel. That companies in their statutes decide that they can only employ Jews.”

De Haan quickly reached such prominence that 

Ha’aretz

 labelled him and other Agudah members “traitors” and “scum.” Such words helped fuel the violent attacks of Jewish settler groups against Agudah members to the point where, in 1924, a member of the Haganah, the main Zionist militia, assassinated him. The order was given by Yitzhak Ben-Zvi, later to become the second president of Israel. 

Moser then jumps to Egypt, focusing on Sadiq Saad, an Egyptian, anti-Zionist, Jewish leftist. One of Saad’s most important works was 

Palestine in the Claws of Colonialism, 

published in 1947 and detailing the apartheid-style system then already established. One of the book’s contributions was its coverage of the unique experience of the Palestinian peasantry. Unlike almost all other peasantries, when the Palestinians were expelled from their land, they were denied employment by the new owners of the land or in the cities. This came directly from the policies of the Palestine Foundation Fund, the World Zionist Organisation’s fundraising arm, which specifically stated in its loan contracts that the borrower “pledges to hire Jewish workers only.”

The book covers numerous other examples of prominent anti-Zionist Jewish individuals and groups. The chapters on the immediate post-World War Two period are particularly useful in understanding the rapid transformation of both Zionism and those opposed to it. The French New Left, for example, during the 1950s and 1960s suffered through a period of deep confusion that led many prominent figures to support a form of Zionism. Similarly, the chapter on Reform Judaism in the United States, which had opposed Zionism since the late 19th Century, shows how …

author: Elliot Downes
title: NT government closes Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter
content:
Residents of Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter were evicted by the Northern Territory government on 12 October, and relocated to Batchelor, a town 100 kilometres away.

Yilli Short Stay Accommodation (YiSSA), which is run by Yilli Rreung Housing Aboriginal Corporation, was home to hundreds of people, mostly Aboriginal. Many have experienced domestic violence and are living with serious health conditions, including kidney conditions requiring dialysis. 

Residents from communities across the territory would stay at YiSSA while accessing medical care or other services in Darwin. Nearly 400 people were directly affected by the closure of the facility, including 160 children.

YiSSA’s closure will place more pressure on remaining homelessness services in Darwin. Meanwhile, the minority of residents transferred to the smaller facility in Batchelor will not have the same access to support networks, food, healthcare and education. Batchelor is a town with a population of around 500, a small health clinic and no public transport. 

The closure of a key homelessness service is particularly egregious given the Northern Territory has the highest rate of homelessness in the country. According to data released last year by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, 

one in every 25 Territorians requires homelessness assistance

, and Aboriginal people make up 89 percent of those accessing homelessness services in the Northern Territory.

As the biggest landlord in the territory, the Northern Territory government is largely to blame for this situation. Territorians on the emergency public housing waiting list can expect to 

wait up to a decade for a roof over their head

. The government is also responsible for the apartheid-like conditions in Aboriginal town camps on the outskirts of places like Darwin and Alice Springs, as well as the overcrowding in remote communities.

The closure of YiSSA was announced by the ruling Country Liberal Party (CLP) in July. Ostensibly, it was due to a failure to secure a deal with Ausco, the owner of the buildings and other infrastructure on the Crown land site. But in reality, it was a political decision. 

After years of renting the demountable buildings, the government offered to buy them for $3 million—the equivalent of just one year’s rent. When this offer was rejected by Ausco, the federal government proposed to cover the cost of the purchase on the condition that Yilli Rreung continue running the service.

The CLP rejected the offer of federal funding, with Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro calling it a 

“waste of taxpayers’ hard-earned money”

. Yet it has cost 

$16.25 million to establish and fund the Batchelor facility

, run by Mission Australia.

The announcement of YiSSA’s closure sparked a campaign by the activist group, Justice Not Jails (JNJ). It culminated in a 200-strong rally outside of the Australian Homelessness Conference in Darwin just days before residents were to be evicted. 

Anna, an activist with JNJ, told 

Red Flag

 that the decision doesn’t make sense “unless you approach it from an ideological viewpoint. Some of the YiSSA residents have said that [the government] just don’t want Aboriginal people to have a nice, secure place to live.”

The YiSSA closure is symptomatic of a Trumpian government that has targeted Aboriginal people in particular. Since coming to power in 2024, the CLP have lowered the age of criminal responsibility to 10, reintroduced spit hoods in detention, and made it easier for Aboriginal children to be removed from their families and placed into long-term state care.

This has involved a significant expansion in the carceral state, with the prison population 

increasing by 24 percent between 2024 and 2025

, and the Finocchiaro government announcing earlier this year the construction of a new private prison in Darwin. 

The Northern Territory is one of the most incarcerated places in the world, 

second only to El Salvador

, with more than 1 percent of the entire population behind bars. Increasingly, this includes people on remand, who are awaiting trial or sentencing.

According to Anna, the next phase of the campaign will involve putting pressure on the federal Labor government. “There’s been a lot of disagreement between the CLP and Labor about what was actually promised. It’s all really immature and I think disrespectful to the people whose lives are actually being affected,” she told 

Red Flag.

author: Ben Smoke
title: Home Secretary Refuses to Meet Worker Affected by Her ‘Nasty’ Immigration Plans
content:
Home secretary Shabana Mahmood has refused to meet with a migrant care worker who will be affected by her rightwing immigration reforms.


Mahmood was asked to meet the worker as part of a discussion with Unison boss Andrea Egan about plans to make migrants wait up to 15 years to apply for indefinite leave to remain,

the i Paper reported

. 


But the home secretary refused Egan’s request and the meeting, which is part of

a charm offensive by Mahmood

 to stave off a growing rebellion against her reforms, was cancelled.


Unison is officially affiliated with the Labour party and has been at the forefront of opposition to Mahmood’s plans. Egan, who was expelled from Labour amid a purge of leftwing members in 2022, has described the reforms as “dehumanising”. 


Egan

said on X

 on Wednesday: “Shabana Mahmood’s failure to engage with the migrant workers whose lives her nasty proposals will devastate is totally unacceptable. These are brilliant, committed workers who hold our public services together. Unison won’t tolerate them being attacked and ignored.” 


The Home Office

told the i Paper

 the meeting was a private one-on-one talk between Mahmood and Egan that Unison had chosen to cancel.


Former shadow chancellor John McDonnell urged Mahmood to “think again on this decision not to meet” the worker. Writing on

X

, he said “the work visa issue is causing totally unnecessary division in the Labour party.”


In an interview with

 Sky News

 on Thursday, energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh refused five times to back Mahmood’s policy of making people wait 15 years for permanent residency. 


In a now deleted social media post earlier this week,

Fahnbulleh hit out

 at “any attempt to prolong the time people have to wait for settlement.”


In March this year whilst not a member of cabinet, Angela Rayner referred to the reforms as

“un-British”

. She

has since

 attempted to downplay reports of a cabinet split over the policy. 


The government

has delayed

 its official announcement of the policy, the Critic reported, and says it is “considering responses” to a public consultation that closed in February.

author: Unknown
title: Antalya'da hortum nedeniyle parçalanan konteynerlerde 4 işçi hayatını kaybetti
content:
Antalya'nın Kepez ilçesinde etkili olan hortumda parçalanan iki konteynerde bulunan 4 işçi hayatını kaybetti, 1 işçi yaralandı.

Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğünün sarı kodlu sağanak uyarısında bulunduğu kentte, Kepez ilçesi Fevzi Çakmak Mahallesi'ndeki bir inşaat alanında hortum oluştu.

Hortum, inşaat işçilerinin kaldığı iki konteyneri parçaladı. Konteynerlerde bulunan 5 işçi savruldu.

İhbar üzerine bölgeye 112 Acil Sağlık, polis ve itfaiye ekipleri sevk edildi.

İşçilerden 2'sinin olay yerinde, 2'sinin ise kaldırıldıkları hastanede hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi.

Yaralanan işçinin sağlık durumunun iyi olduğu öğrenildi.

Antalya Valisi Hulusi Şahin konu hakkında yaptığı açıklamada "Maalesef 2 işçimiz olay yerinde 2 işçimiz de kaldırıldıkları hastanede vefat ettiler. Bir işçimiz yaralı durumu hafif. Çok enteresan bir doğa olayı ile karşı karşıyayız. Çünkü şehrin herhangi başka bir yerinde fırtına, hortum ihbar edilmedi. Civarındaki binalarda bir şey yok ama sadece bu alanda iki konteyneri paramparça eden bir hortumla karşı karşıyayız."

Şantiye sahasındaki ölüm ve yaralanmaların vincin devrilmesi nedeniyle olmadığını söyleyen Şahin, bölgede incelemelerin devam ettiğini ve ekiplerin alanda yaralı veya ölü olup olmadığına dair çalışmalarını sürdürdüğünü kaydetti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Sırbistan | “Rejim devrildi; mücadele daha yeni başladı”
content:
Sırbistan'daki Marks21 sosyalist çevresinin ve Londra merkezli sosyalist yayın ve kampanya ağı Counterfire'ın üyesi olan Marksist yazar, siyasal yorumcu ve sosyalist aktivist Dragan Plavšić'in 26 Ekim 2026'da Counterfire'da yayımlanan Sırbistan seçimlerinde Öğrenci Listesi'nin zaferini değerlendiren “Sırbistan’daki öğrenci hareketi belirleyici bir seçim zaferi kazandı” başlıklı yazısını paylaşıyoruz.

 

2003'te yayımlanan Balkan Sosyalist Geleneği ve Balkan Federasyonu, 1871–1915 (The Balkan Socialist Tradition and the Balkan Federation, 1871–1915) başlıklı kitabın editörlüğünü Andreja Živković ile birlikte üstlenen Plavšić'in çalışmaları ağırlıklı olarak Balkanlar'ın siyasal tarihi, milliyetçilik, sosyalist hareketler ve emperyalizm üzerine. Kosova, Bosna-Hersek ve Sırbistan'ı konu alan yazılarında milliyetçiliği eleştirirken Balkan halkları arasında sosyalist dayanışmayı savunan yazar, Rusya, Çin, NATO ve Avrupa Birliği arasındaki uluslararası güç ilişkilerini de sınıfsal bir perspektiften değerlendiriyor. Makaleleri Counterfire ve LeftEast gibi yayınlarda çıkan Plavšić, Sırbistan'daki öğrenci hareketinin seçim zaferini de neoliberalizme karşı toplumsal mücadele ve demokratik örgütlenme bağlamında değerlendiriyor.


Sırbistan'daki parlamento seçimlerinde Öğrenci Listesi'nin kazandığı zafer muazzam. İlk kez seçimlere katılan liste, 250 sandalyenin tahminen 140'ını kazanarak çoğunluğu elde etti. Başbakanlık makamına sorunsuzca geçip iktidarı da beraberinde taşımayı uman otoriter Cumhurbaşkanı Aleksandar Vučić'in 14 yıllık iktidar hâkimiyeti, öğrencilerin öncülük ettiği kitlesel hareket tarafından kesin biçimde kırıldı. İki yıl önce, yeniden inşa edilmiş bir tren istasyonunun çökmesi ve 16 kişinin ölmesiyle başlayan hareket, 2025'te bir başbakanı istifaya zorlamıştı. Şimdi de cumhurbaşkanını görevinden ayrılmak zorunda bıraktı.


2024'ten bu yana süren kitle hareketleri kararlı ve kesintisizdi. Yalnızca Vučić'e değil, muhalefete de yönelen köklü bir halk hoşnutsuzluğundan güç alan bu hareketler, geleneksel siyasete güvenini kaybetmiş insanlar bağımsız biçimde örgütlendiklerinde kökleşmiş bir siyasal düzenin devrilebileceğini gösterdi.


Ancak zafer ne kadar büyük olursa olsun, hayati bir soruyu gündeme getiriyor: Kolektif eylem ve demokratik katılım üzerine kurulu bir hareket devlet kurumlarına girdiğinde ne olur? Bu sorunun yanıtı, Sırbistan siyasetinde yeni ve ilerici bir dönemin açılması olasılığı ile bir fırsatın daha kaçırılması tehlikesi arasındaki dengede yatıyor. Sonuç, büyük ölçüde hareketin kendisini iktidara taşıyan kitlesel seferberliklerle bağını koruyup koruyamayacağına, aynı zamanda Avrupa'nın dört bir yanında yayılmakta olan neoliberalizme karşı geniş çaplı toplumsal başkaldırıyla birleşip birleşemeyeceğine bağlı olacak.


Trajediden isyana


Kasım 2024'te istasyonun peronu üzerindeki sundurmanın çökmesiyle yaşanan trajedi, Vučić yönetiminin yolsuzluğunu, kayırmacılığını ve hesap verme sorumluluğunun ekonomik ve siyasal bağlantılarla geçiştirilmesini açığa çıkardı. Bunu izleyen öfke dalgasının yükselişine, istasyonun yeniden inşasıyla ilgili belgelerin yayımlanmasını ve sorumluların yargılanmasını talep eden öğrenciler öncülük etti.


Hesap verme sorumluluğu talebiyle başlayan hareket, hızla Vučić'e karşı daha geniş bir isyana dönüştü. Daha da önemlisi, hareket yalnızca tek tek suistimallere değil, sıradan insanların yaşamlarını yöneten kurumlar üzerinde güçten yoksunluğunun kaçınılmazlığına dair temel varsayıma da meydan okudu.


Üniversite işgalleri, gösteriler, yol kesme eylemleri ve mitingler Sırbistan'ın dört bir yanına yayıldı. Öğrenciler kentler ve köyler arasında gidip gelerek, zenginlere ve güç sahiplerine hizmete fazlasıyla alışmış bir siyasal sistem tarafından uzun süredir terk edilmiş insanlarla dayanışma bağları kurdu. Öğretmenler, üniversite çalışanları, işçiler ve diğer yurttaşlar da onlara katıldı.


Öğrenciler mücadelenin harekete geçirici gücü haline geldi. Resmî muhalefetten kararlı bir biçimde bağımsız kalmaları ve üniversite genel kurullarında (plenumlarda) kolektif tartışma ve karar alma ilkesine bağlılıkları, hareketin en belirleyici güç kaynağıydı. 


Mücadelenin sonraki adımı seçimlere katılma kararı oldu. Hareket, üniversitelerden ve toplumun daha geniş kesimlerinden gelen adaylarla kendi seçim listesini oluşturdu. Adaylar üniversite ve fakülte genel kurullarında önerildi; seçilmeden önce öğrenciler tarafından kolektif olarak titizlikle değerlendirildi. Adayların hiçbiri …

author: Lisa Xu
title: UFCW Members Protect Local Election After Sham Merger Attempt
content:
An insurgent slate is challenging the longtime incumbents in Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW), in what may be the local’s first competitive election in decades. And now, after protecting the election from a sham merger attempt that would have canceled the election, the battle is on.


Ballots are set to be mailed on November 21. But when members first saw the election notice in the local’s newsletter, they discovered a big “but.” The notice stated that the election would not proceed if Local 8 merged with another union, the

Staffing Agencies Federated Employees

 (SAFE), before the end of the year.


Members said they had never heard about this possible merger, or SAFE, before reading about it in the final sentence of the election notice, mailed to members on October 16.


What is SAFE? Publicly available information about the organization, which has multiple ties to Local 8 President Jacques Loveall, raised more questions than answers. Neither Local 8, the UFCW International union, nor SAFE has responded to inquiries about the merger.


With the help of Essential Workers for Democracy, a UFCW reform organization focused on member education and union democracy, the insurgent slate urged the Department of Labor to investigate SAFE and the merger. After a federal investigator began to probe, the local told them the merger had been “postponed indefinitely.”


A FAMILY AFFAIR


Local 8 represents 23,000 workers in grocery, meatpacking, health care, and cannabis across northern California and the Central Valley. End to end, it would take 10 hours to drive the length of the local’s jurisdiction.


The reform slate

At What Cost

 is running on opening up negotiations to members and training stewards in every workplace. Wages for grocery workers have stagnated across California. A

2025 study

 sponsored by several other UFCW locals on understaffing at Kroger and Albertsons found a high degree of financial insecurity among their workers.


“Grocery careers, once dignified, have been reduced to second jobs for most,” said Eric Marcuz, a veteran Safeway worker who is running for president on the At What Cost slate. The local has not had a competitive election in at least 40 years.


Marcuz’s slate created a

page

 to try to provide members more information about the merger, and sent a

letter of complaint

 to Local 8, UFCW International, and the Department of Labor over what they saw as an effort to avoid a democratic election.


The At What Cost slate is running against a slate of incumbents—the

Solidarity Works Team

— headed by Loveall, who has been president of Local 8 and its predecessor union, Local 588, since 2004. He took over the position from his father,

Jack Loveall

, who became president of Local 588 in 1984, after working in high-level positions for the UFCW International and one of its predecessor unions, the Retail Clerks, for many years.


When the elder Loveall retired, he was one of the highest-paid union officers in the country, earning more than $567,000 in compensation a year, equivalent to over a million dollars today.


“The Loveall family has led our union for decades,” said Marcuz. “Over that time they have consolidated power at the top and completely distanced themselves from the workers they claim to represent. While their wealth and wages have ballooned, the members have been left behind.”


On his LinkedIn page, the younger Loveall describes himself as “Chief Executive Officer of trade organization (UFCW8.org).” He received $306,000 in total compensation from the local last year, plus another $20,000 salary as an International Vice President and

$34,752

 from his role as a trustee of the UFCW Vacation Compensation Trusts. Loveall is also the director and co-founder of Solidaritus, a for-profit health care company that Local 8 has purchased millions of dollars of shares in, as have other unions.


‘THAT’S THEIR MODE OF OPERATING’


Leaders of the local have used a merger to avoid a competitive election before. In 2006, a slate of

reformers

 planned a challenge to the leadership of then-Local 588, including Loveall. But prior to the scheduled election, Local 588

merged

 with Local 1288 to form Local 8-Golden State, and elections were put off until 2008.


Meanwhile, Doug Slaydon, a 25-year meat cutter and the reform slate’s candidate for union president, was

fired

 from Safeway on the pretext of a customer complaint in …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Ni la muchacha ni la “chica que me ayuda”
content:
Historias de Trabajadoras de Casas Particulares organizadas: Lucía y Pirén de Junín de los Andes, Neuquén.


Por Juliana Díaz Lozano


Lucía y Pirén son trabajadoras de casas particulares en Junín de los Andes, y junto a otras mujeres forman parte de la Organización de trabajadoras de Casas Particulares de Neuquén. Además de abordar los derechos laborales de su sector, la organización participa de la Asamblea de Mujeres y Disidencias, viaja a los Encuentros Plurinacionales y varias de sus integrantes son parte del activismo mapuche. Invitamos a conocer una experiencia de organización colectiva detrás del trabajo del hogar asalariado, a veces invisible, a veces aislado, pero cada vez más interpelador dentro de las luchas de mujeres y disidencias.


Lucía Guentean tiene 35 años y hace ocho que es trabajadora de casas particulares. “Empecé por necesidad, tengo dos hijas y su papá había quedado sin trabajo. Mi mamá, mis hermanas, todas trabajan de lo mismo”. A pesar de haber estado cerca de diversos activismos, hace cinco años decidió organizarse desde el sector. “Fue una de mis empleadoras de ese momento quien me dijo que tenía conocimiento de un grupo de mujeres que se estaba reuniendo, así que me sumé a la organización”. Para Lucía, han logrado visibilizar la lucha en la región “hace dos años que en Junín nuestra lucha empezó a ser más visible, desde la Asamblea de Mujeres y Disidencias nos tienen como en cuenta en cada active para que sea más reconocido este sector”, agrega.


Piren Quilaleo tiene 39 y es trabajadora del hogar desde los 14 años. Como en el caso de Lucía, su abuela, tías y madre fueron o son trabajadoras de casas particulares. “Pero además vengo de una familia de activistas sociales, -cuenta-, me crié en esta onda de defender derechos y sobre todo causas juntas”, agrega. Pirén además es mapuche, forma parte de la resistencia ancestral y la lucha por el territorio como varias de sus compañeras de organización sindical. Recuerda que, en su trayectoria laboral, desde adolescente, tuvo que soportar “tratos no humanos”, para poder llevar un plato de comida a su casa. También tuvo experiencias buenas, y con el tiempo, aprendió a poner límites a lxs empleadores.


La palabra “límites” surge de manera repetida cuando las trabajadoras cuentan sus aprendizajes laborales. Poner límites de tareas, de horarios, a los malos tratos. Explican que el hecho de que el trabajo del hogar sucede en un ámbito íntimo, oculto a la vista pública “es lo más complicado de nuestro trabajo, porque nos toca está solas, cara a cara con el empleador. Incluso, aunque formes parte de una organización, cuando tenés que definir salarios, acuerdos de convivencia o tareas, estamos solas”.


En momentos de ajuste y pérdida de derechos laborales como hoy en Argentina, la situación de las trabajadoras del hogar, -no registradas en un 80 %-, se complica aún más. “Trabajamos en muchos lugares, de un lado para el otro, y también diferentes empleos, y después nos toca trabajar en casa”, explica Pirén. Como agravante, la reforma laboral amplió el período de prueba a 6 meses y la Ley bases recortó derechos al sector, en beneficio de los empleadores que ya no pagan doble indemnización como multa por no haber registrado la relación laboral.


Barriendo injusticias, juntando rebeldías


“Mi mamá y mis tías fueron parte del primer sindicato de trabajadoras de casas particulares en los años 80 en Neuquén”, comenta Pirén. “En Junín de Los Andes fue un sindicato superconocido, luego después en los 90 hubo tanta turbulencia que el sindicato se empezó a caer. Y nosotras empezamos a resurgir a partir de 2015 y retomamos el lema del sindicato ´ Barriendo injusticias, juntando rebeldías´. Somos un grupo chico, pero nos mantenemos y estamos siempre viendo cómo seguir”.


Pirén articula con su militancia diferentes miradas y realidades: “yo siempre estuve organizada como mujer mapuche, como mujeres mapuches venimos haciendo mucha visibilización de lo que nos atraviesa, y también soy parte de la organización de mujeres y disidencias de acá en Junín de los Andes”. En esta pluralidad de espacios, ella siente que el sector de trabajadoras de casas particulares siempre estuvo invisibilizado, “como escondido, poco visto, poco reconocido”. Pero en los últimos años, la organización de trabajadoras del hogar de la que forma parte comenzó a fortalecerse, a mostrar la situación de las trabajadoras adentro de las casas, los abusos, los maltratos, y esto volvió al sector …

author: Mag
title: [Buch und Debatte zur GEW] Die ideologische Ausrichtung der Lehrkräfte 1933–1945. Die Bildungsgewerkschaft GEW ringt mit ihrer Vergangenheit im Nationalsozialismus
content:
Dossier


„

Der Nationalsozialistische Lehrerbund hatte 97 % der Pädagoginnen und Pädagogen organisiert. Anhand seines Zentralorgans wird gezeigt, inwiefern der NSLB seit 1933 fester Bestandteil des Nazi-Systems war. Der Nationalsozialistische Lehrerbund hatte 97 % der Pädagoginnen und Pädagogen organisiert. Ein Drittel davon waren NSDAP-Mitglieder. Dennoch hält sich die Verharmlosung des NSLB auch in der Erziehungswissenschaft immer noch hartnäckig. Die vorliegende Studie weist anhand der Analyse des Zentralorgans des NSLB nach, dass und inwiefern der NSLB eben nicht eine harmlose Berufsorganisation war, sondern dass er seit 1933 fester Bestandteil des verbrecherischen NS-Systems war. Der Verband war Teil des Nazi-Regimes, das die Hetze, Rassismus und Judenfeindschaft des NSLB zur Vorbereitung und als Begleitung der realen Mordprogramme durchaus benötigte

.“ Verlagsinfo zum Buch von Saskia Müller und Benjamin Ortmeyer –

siehe mehr Informationen zum Buch

. In Reaktion auf die Buchveröffentlichung gibt es einen Offenen Brief des Bundesausschusses der Studentinnen und Studenten der GEW (BASS) an den Hauptvorstand und die Mitglieder der GEW sowie eine breite Debatte um die GEW:


Offener Brief an die GEW: Wo ist die öffentliche Begründung für die Umbenennung der Max-Traeger-Stiftung? Die GEW, die NS-Zeit und der aktuelle Judenhass


Seit über 10 Jahren gab es die  Forderung nach Umbenennung der GEW-nahen Max-Traeger-Stiftung, weil Max Traeger ein Nazi-Kollaborateur war. Vor vier Jahren, in 2022, wurde endlich die Umbenennung beschlossen. Dann dauerte es wieder Jahre, bis die Umbenennung auch durchgeführt wurde. Allerdings so, dass in der Öffentlichkeit und auf der Homepage der Stiftung die Gründe für die Umbenennung nicht benannt werden. Dagegen richtet sich der

Offene Brief von Benjamin Ortmeyer vom Oktober 2026

 


Gründungsvorsitzender entthront: Die Gewerkschaft Erziehung und Wissenschaft (GEW) benennt ihre „Max-Traeger-Stiftung“ um. Der Namensgeber war Mitglied im NS-Lehrerbund


„Die Basis der Gewerkschaft Erziehung und Wissenschaft (GEW) hat auf dem diesjährigen Gewerkschaftstag in Leipzig ihren umstrittenen Gründungsvorsitzenden Max Traeger vom Sockel gestoßen: Die gewerkschaftseigene Forschungsstiftung war bislang nach ihm benannt. Künftig soll sie aber den Namen einer – noch nicht bestimmten – Frau tragen, „die mit ihrem antifaschistischen Engagement vorbildhaft“ sei, heißt es in dem Beschluss vom Wochenende. Damit setzen sich KritikerInnen Traegers gegen prominente Wortmeldungen aus dem Vorstand durch. Max Traeger sei „wegen seiner Mitgliedschaft im Nationalsozialistischen Lehrerbund umstritten, insbesondere bei jüngeren Gewerkschaftsmitgliedern“, heißt es auf der GEW-Homepage zur Begründung. Bisher hatte der Vorstand der Gewerkschaft eher dazu geneigt, Max Traeger als „Mann der ersten Stunde“ zu glorifizieren. (…) Vor 24 Jahren hatte der Frankfurter Erziehungswissenschaftler Benjamin Ortmeyer erstmals die braunen Wurzeln der Lehrergewerkschaft angeprangert, vor allem die prominente Rolle von ehemaligen Mitgliedern des NS-Lehrerbunds in Nazideutschland. Diese hätten in Nazideutschland systematisch bei der Auswahl „unwerten Lebens“ assistiert. Insbesondere mit der Durchsicht von Kirchenbüchern haben sie geholfen, Menschen zu identifizieren, die laut der NS-“Rassenlehre“ als Juden galten und deshalb verfolgt, deportiert und ermordet wurden, argumentiert Ortmeyer seither in seinen zahlreichen Publikationen zu dem Thema. (…) Empfindet Ortmeyer nach der Entscheidung für die Namensänderung, für die er und andere gekämpft haben, Genugtuung oder eher Empörung, weil es so lange gedauert hat? „Beides“, antwortet er der taz, so auch „Empörung über das ‚katholische Kirche-Syndrom‘ der Verdrängung.“ Im Hauptvorstand vertrete man bis heute die These, dass das damals eben so gewesen sei. Gleichwohl habe sich das Engagement gelohnt. Zu dem späten Erfolg gratuliere er gerne den vielen jungen GEW-Mitgliedern und dem hessischen Landesverband, die in der Sache nicht nachgelassen hätten.“

author: anonerror
title: Huelga, sujeto y utopía «positiva»: respuesta a Rubén Morvolution
content:
Alfredo Apilánez


Un paradigma obsoleto


«No son pocos los que, bajo estas circunstancias difíciles, sueñan con una nueva unidad de clase acorde a los principios de la izquierda tradicional y del movimiento obrero (…). De ahí se deriva la idea, tanto esencialista como metafísica -enunciada especialmente por Lukács-, de que la clase trabajadora representa la totalidad social y, por tanto, debe asumir la conciencia de ello»


	Norbert Trenkle


Recientemente se ha publicado un

artículo

 de réplica a mi

texto

 de análisis de la situación del movimiento de vivienda, en el contexto actual de la «revuelta de las acampadas», y de crítica de la apuesta por la convocatoria de huelga general “por la vivienda” para el 11 de noviembre.


Antes que nada, quiero agradecer al autor -de seudónimo Rubén Morvolution, a partir de ahora RM- el tono constructivo y la claridad expositiva en la formulación de sus razonadas críticas y de las propuestas y reflexiones que plantea.


El título del texto de RM ya anticipa, de forma muy precisa, los puntos fundamentales del planteamiento que desarrolla: “La huelga como medio, la clase como sujeto: una respuesta al debate sobre el movimiento de vivienda”.


Me atrevería, por mor de brevedad, a sintetizar las principales tesis de RM en dos puntos neurálgicos. En primer lugar, como reza el propio título, la consideración de la huelga como un medio, no como un fin en sí mismo:


“La huelga no es el objetivo. La huelga ha sido uno de los instrumentos mediante los cuales la clase trabajadora ha aprendido a reconocerse como fuerza colectiva. Su importancia no reside únicamente en detener temporalmente la producción, sino en la posibilidad de que quienes sostienen la actividad económica descubran, mediante su propia experiencia, la capacidad que poseen cuando actúan conjuntamente”. El razonamiento de RM admite que, a pesar de que la convocatoria haya sido instrumentalizada por los sindicatos mayoritarios e incluso por el propio gobierno, y más allá de su grado de éxito en la paralización de la actividad económica, lo realmente importante es el proceso de «empoderamiento» colectivo, que pueda contribuir al fortalecimiento de la clase trabajadora. De este modo, la argumentación de RM se blinda ante las críticas más directas a la movilización, centradas en la falta de realismo y el estatismo de las demandas formuladas, o en su cooptación por los sindicatos de concertación, marginando la vertiente radical y antigubernamental de la iniciativa y capitalizando el impulso inicial surgido de la masiva movilización social que arranca con el despiadado desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal.


Sin embargo, RM omite que en el artículo original ya se esboza la crítica de su estrategia de defensa «indirecta» de la huelga, como medio de constitución del sujeto colectivo, mediante la alianza entre las organizaciones «combativas» de la clase trabajadora y el movimiento de vivienda:


«La respuesta ante tales críticas por parte de los partidarios de la huelga desde la izquierda radical política y sindical suele consistir en una defensa “indirecta” de la movilización, no solo como un fin en sí misma, sino como un medio para potenciar la organización y el empoderamiento de los colectivos populares y de trabajadores».


En segundo lugar, y aceptando el terreno que RM propone como el apropiado para evaluar el grado de acierto de la convocatoria, voy a centrarme en lo que considero que es el núcleo de la tesis central que desarrolla en su texto. A saber, la pervivencia de la clase trabajadora como potencial «sujeto» transformador, que debe ser «constituido» a través de la lucha y la movilización colectivas:


“Por eso, la diversidad de la clase trabajadora no elimina su importancia ni la capacidad de la huelga para convertirse en un instrumento de lucha colectiva (…). El objetivo no debería ser defender una herramienta por fidelidad a una tradición, sino contribuir a que la clase trabajadora contemporánea, diversa y fragmentada, pueda constituirse en un sujeto capaz de intervenir conscientemente sobre sus propias condiciones de existencia”.


La cuestión neurálgica, que sirve de fundamento para la defensa de la huelga desde las organizaciones de la izquierda radical y cuyo planteamiento el texto de RM refleja de forma paradigmática, gira por tanto alrededor de la vigencia de la categoría sociopolítica de clase trabajadora y, en consecuencia, de la posibilidad de formación de un «sujeto» en base a ese marco. title: Sevda Karaca: War policies undermine unity and labour struggles - Part Three
content:
Sevda Karaca, Deputy Chair of the Labour Party (EMEP) and MP for Antep, answered ANF's questions about labour struggles and the struggle for peace.


Part one of this interview can be read

here

 and part two

here

. 


How do war policies undermine class solidarity between Turkish and Kurdish workers? You frequently visit workplaces and meet workers. Have you observed this in practice?


One of the most important realities we observe on the ground is that workers face very similar economic problems. Workers in Antep, Başpınar, metal factories and the logistics sector talk about inadequate wages, long working hours, workplace accidents, job insecurity and obstacles to trade union organising. Workers living in different cities and belonging to different identities share many of the same problems. But the existence of common problems does not automatically lead to a common struggle.


That requires organisation, trust and shared experiences. War policies and nationalist polarisation undermine precisely these foundations. The conflict of interests between workers and their employers is pushed into the background. Instead of being seen as a fellow worker demanding the same rights, another worker may be portrayed primarily as a representative of a particular identity. As a result, workers who should be standing together against their employers may begin to distrust one another.


Nationalist rhetoric can obscure the fact that Turkish and Kurdish workers in the same workplace are condemned to the same low wages, face the same occupational safety problems and experience the same pressure against trade union organising. This is precisely what weakens working-class unity.


However, it would not be enough to attribute this situation solely to nationalist propaganda. There must also be a genuine reckoning with workers' different identities and the inequalities they experience. We cannot build unity between Turkish and Kurdish workers simply by opposing nationalist propaganda. There can be no genuine unity if the Kurdish people's demands concerning their language, identity and democratic rights are ignored. Nor can there be a meaningful call for working-class unity that dismisses the national oppression experienced by Kurdish workers. Unity cannot be built on the expectation that one side will remain silent about its own problems.


The task of socialists is not to ignore these divisions but to establish a common foundation for struggle capable of overcoming them. Every experience in which workers organise together, defend one another's rights and struggle shoulder to shoulder for wages and trade union rights is valuable in this respect. But for economic unity to become lasting, we must also defend demands for equality and freedom. That is why it is so important for the working class in Kurdistan to develop an independent movement.


Workers, working people and poorer sections of society in the region must be able to participate in the process with their own demands and defend their right to have a say over wages, trade union rights, working conditions and their living environments. This is particularly important at a time when industrial investment is expected to increase as a result of the peace process and Kurdish regions are once again being viewed by capital as new areas of exploitation. We need to take this discussion much further.


‘Turkish workers must support the Kurdish people's demands’


Turkish workers and working people also have a responsibility to oppose the policies of their own ruling classes and support the Kurdish people's demands for peace, equality and democracy. This is necessary not only as an act of solidarity but also to defend the independent interests of their own class. Because in an environment where peoples are turned against one another, it becomes harder to develop a common struggle against capital.


However, this is not something that can happen simply because we call for it. We must raise and discuss this issue within every struggle. Indeed, these discussions are most possible among workers who are already engaged in struggle. We have repeatedly seen that every strike and every act of resistance provides an important opportunity for such discussions. From the Şık Makas resistance to strikes in Izmir, from the protests in Başpınar to workers' struggles in Kocaeli and Bursa, we make particular use of these opportunities to strengthen the need for resistance based on mutual understanding …

author: anonerror
title: [Valladolid] Apertura de nuevo local de CNT
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla Mimo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.


A continuación hemos puesto en marcha unas jornadas de inauguración de las que tenéis información en las redes y web de CNT.


Reproducimos a continuación el manifiesto que refleja esta nueva etapa:


Hoy, sábado, 17 de octubre, inauguramos una nueva etapa en CNT Valladolid.


Estrenamos un espacio más amplio. Un espacio donde pueda entrar más gente, donde podamos encontrarnos, organizarnos y construir juntas una respuesta colectiva a la realidad que vivimos.


Porque este local no es solamente un lugar nuevo. Es un espacio de encuentro para quienes entendemos que nuestros derechos no son concesiones, que la dignidad no se negocia y que nuestra fuerza está en la lucha obrera.


Y cuando decimos clase trabajadora, no hablamos solo de quienes tienen un contrato o un empleo. También hablamos de quienes trabajan sin derechos, de quienes sostienen los cuidados y de quienes encuentran las puertas cerradas al empleo por su identidad o su condición.


Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT.


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos


Somos anarcosindicalistas. Entendemos que quienes vivimos de nuestro trabajo tenemos capacidad para defender nuestros derechos colectivamente y para construir otras formas de relacionarnos y organizarnos frente a la explotación.


Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.


Porque el sistema contra el que se organizaron quienes nos precedieron no ha desaparecido. La explotación adopta nuevas formas. La precariedad se normaliza. Trabajar ya no garantiza unas condiciones de vida dignas. Y quienes acumulan riqueza siguen teniendo capacidad para decidir sobre nuestras vidas.


Por eso estamos aquí.


Porque la lucha sigue.


Y esa lucha sigue hoy en múltiples frentes que se complementan.


Una de ellas es la

lucha antifascista

.


Estamos viendo crecer discursos que alimentan el odio y el miedo …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Brazil: Lula Wins Stunning Upset Over Flávio Bolsonaro in Blow to Far Right & Trump
content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a record fourth term in office, defeating far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro by 4 million votes in a runoff election on Sunday. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who remains under house arrest for plotting a coup against Lula four years ago. The younger Bolsonaro, who narrowly defeated Lula in the first round of voting earlier this month, is now refusing to concede.


Lula’s surprise comeback comes after weeks of student-led organizing and campaigning on his behalf, and amid accusations that U.S.-based tech companies were suppressing Lula’s reach online in favor of his Trump-aligned opponent. “The amount of organizing, the amount of marches and rallies, campaigning, pamphlets that we’ve seen the last three weeks has been something that I have never seen in my entire life, ever, covering elections for decades in so many different countries. It is absolutely unprecedented,” says Brazil-based journalist Michael Fox. “It is an absolute game-changer for the region.”

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Lula Wins Historic Comeback in Brazil Despite Far-Right Election Meddling
content:
Brazil’s president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won an unprecedented fourth term – a stunning comeback victory in the face of attempts by far-right opponents to interfere in the election. 


Lula secured 51.79% of the vote in the run-off on Sunday, 4.4 million more votes than his US-backed rival Flávio Bolsonaro, who secured 48.21%. 


The leftwing incumbent was the runner up in the first round of voting on 4 October, and polling showed both candidates were neck and neck ahead of the run-off on Sunday. 


It is the first time since Brazil’s dictatorship ended in the 1980s that a presidential candidate has won an election without coming first in the initial round of voting. 


“This election was a defeat for denialism,” Lula told a jubilant crowd of supporters in São Paulo on Sunday evening. “I want to thank God and to thank you, Brazilian men and women of this country… it was democracy that made this happen.”


Bolsonaro has refused to concede and is calling for Lula’s victory to be annulled. His father, ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for attempting to stage a military coup after losing to Lula in 2022. 


This year’s election was marred by widespread

reports of foreign

 and domestic interference aimed at swaying the vote against Lula. Bolsonaro’s supporters were accused of attempting to prevent people from voting for Lula on Sunday after public transport was shut down in several cities. 


The issue led Brazil’s supreme court to extend voting by two hours to give people more time to reach polling stations. 


The US was also accused of meddling in the election, including via president Donald Trump’s imposition of tariffs earlier this year, which was seen as an attempt to hurt Lula’s chances. And Lula’s supporters have expressed intense anger at Meta after Lula’s campaign said the

company was suppressing his posts

 on its platforms.


Numerous world leaders and other prominent figures congratulated Lula on his victory. “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won,” Mexico’s president, Claudia Sheinbaum, wrote on X. 


Former US presidential candidate Bernie Sanders said Lula’s comeback was “extraordinary”. He wrote: “Lula has stood up for Brazilian workers and democracy – and will continue to do so in the next four years.”


 

The election has also been hailed as a victory in the fight against climate chaos. Bolsonaro was expected to follow in the footsteps of his father and rapidly accelerate the destruction of the Amazon rainforest, a vital global carbon sink. 


Since Lula’s 2022 victory, forest clearing in the Amazon has fallen to its lowest level on record, from 45,600 sq km under Bolsonaro to 24,600 sq km, data from the country’s space agency shows.

title: Posición del colectivx anarquista NOS en las elecciones generales en Brasil en 2026
content:
POSICIÓN DEL COLECTIVX ANARQUISTA NOS EN LAS ELECCIONES GENERALES EN BRASIL EN 2026


A todxs


Este domingo, 25 de octubre de 2026, habrá segunda vuelta de las elecciones de la “democracia” burguesa en el espacio ocupado por la república Federativa de Brasil. Habrá elecciones para gobernador en algunos estados de la federación y para el cargo de presidente de la república. Los candidatos son: el actual presidente Lula da Silva en un intento de reelección; y Flavio Bolsonaro, senador e hijo del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro que gobernó Brasil entre 2019 y 2022.


Por un lado, Lula da Silva, representante de la izquierda institucional y del campo “progresista”. Notorio conciliador de clases y celoso gestor del capital en Brasil, Lula da Silva, su partido PT y su central sindical CUT representan la “democracia” de los ricos, con una política socialdemócrata disfrazada de socialismo donde las élites (financiera, industrial, terratenientes) siguen siendo élites y el pueblo permanece en una posición subalterna, con algunas migajas siendo distribuidas a los más pobres (subsidios en dinero, pequeños aumentos por encima de la inflación para jubilaciones y asalariados de bajos ingresos, ascenso social limitado para hijos de pobres a través del ingreso en universidades, etc.), y convivencia conciliadora más o menos pacífica con los dos bloques que se están formando en el mundo y que caminan hacia la Tercera Guerra Mundial: los Atlantistas (EE. UU., Unión Europea, “israel”) y el Mundo Multipolar (China, Rusia, Irán).


Por otro lado, Flavio Bolsonaro, representante de la extrema derecha y títere del imperialismo yanqui-sionista. Tan celoso como Lula da Silva en la gestión del capital, Flavio se diferencia de él por ser la figura clave en el proyecto del dictador yanqui Donald Trump de imponer gobiernos de extrema derecha en toda Sudamérica. Flavio mantiene una alianza con el dictador argentino Javier Milei y con el carnicero Benjamín Netanyahu, y ya ha advertido que aplicará la misma política económica que Milei en Brasil, que formará una alianza político-económica-militar con el Estado terrorista de “israel”, e incluso invitará a Marco Rubio, Secretario de Estado de Trump, A formar parte de su equipo de gobierno. Una de las principales bases de apoyo de Flavio son las iglesias evangélicas neopentecostales sionistas vinculadas a Estados Unidos y “Israel”.


Flavio es amigo íntimo del banquero Daniel Vorcaro, autor del mayor fraude financiero de la historia de Brasil, quien robó aproximadamente R$ 57.000.000.000,00 (US$ 11.000.000.000,00/EUR 10.000.000.000,00) de fondos de pensiones pertenecientes a empleados de empresas estatales, seguridad social y inversionistas privados. Flavio Bolsonaro recibió R$ 134.000.000,00 (US$ 26.000.000,00/EUR 23.000.000,00) de Vorcaro, supuestamente para la producción de la película Dark Horse, una biografía ficticia del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro. La mayor parte del dinero robado del pueblo fue desviado para el disfrute personal de la familia Bolsonaro.


Flavio tiene vínculos en el submundo del crimen con la cúpula de la organización mafiosa Comando Vermelho y con narcomilicias de extrema derecha.


Flavio actuó, sin cobrar honorarios, como abogado de Bruno Dias Delaroli, cabo de la despreciable PMERJ — Policía Militar del Estado de Río de Janeiro, quien en 2021 mató a la niña Ana Clara Gomes Machado, de 5 años, disparándole dos veces en la cabeza con un fusil de calibre 7,62x51mm NATO, sin motivo aparente alguno. El asesino permanece impune hasta el día de hoy gracias a las maniobras jurídicas de Flavio.


Flavio y su asesora económica, Daniella Marques, han declarado que las políticas criminales de Milei constituyen un “excelente ejemplo”; planean reemplazar a los funcionarios públicos por inteligencia artificial, modificar la Constitución de Brasil sin contar con una asamblea constituyente elegida para tal fin y cancelar las elecciones burguesas de 2030, con el objetivo de que Flavio ejerza un mandato ilegal y dictatorial de ocho años para, supuestamente, “poner a Brasil en su lugar”.


En definitiva, Flavio Bolsonaro es una figura similar a un Ramfis Trujillo o un “Tachito” Somoza: un *playboy* y vividor, hijo de un dictador, elevado a la categoría de político; alguien incluso peor, más perverso y maligno que su propio padre, que pretende transformar Brasil en una dictadura narco-fascista, evangélica, sionista y personalista al servicio de la familia Bolsonaro.


Ante este panorama alarmante …

title: 17 octobre 2026 : Et notre classe releva la tête
content:
La lutte de classe en France s'est accélérée et clarifiée en une séquence en réalité très dense et aux conséquences certainement peu mesurables actuellement. Dans tous les cas, la rencontre qu'il y a eu le 17 entre différentes fractions de la classe en lutte et la force prolétarienne qu'elle permet de poser est précieuse.


1 - Discussion en acte


Après un mois d'une lutte acharnée au sein du mouvement qui a pris dans les lycées en septembre 2026, les jeunes prolos les plus offensifs commençaient à être isolés face à la répression et la dissociation. Dans ce contexte la date du 17 octobre, qui circulait déjà comme un appel au retour des Gilets Jaunes, a sonné comme un appel à la classe : un appel à un grand mouvement fort, massif et déterminé à ne pas se laisser écraser par la répression. Un appel à ce que la classe relève la tête, prenne la rue et exprime sa force.


À cet appel, la classe en lutte a répondu présent. Défiant les tenants de l'ordre, posant une importante offensivité, elle a fait un doigt d'honneur à l'ordre bourgeois et exprimé en acte sa prise de parti pour la radicalité de la lutte. Les plus jeunes prolos doivent être tellement satisfaits de pouvoir trouver là la force de continuer à tenir tête à tout les tenants de l'ordre :

CPE

, flics, patrons, prêtres en tout genre, grands-frères, profs, éducs et parents.


Cette date du 17 a été un moment pour se constituer comme force. C'est un début. Et ça fait du bien. Il s'agissait déjà, pour la classe en mouvement, de se compter, d'éprouver la force dont elle est capable et de poser en acte la question de son orientation dans la période.


2 - Lutte dans la lutte


Il y a eu une lutte dans la lutte ce 17 octobre. Une lutte entre la tendance «

 

manifestation-revendication-réforme

 

» liée à la gauche et une tendance plus autonome, plus offensive, qui porte la proposition de l'attaque directe des institutions de l'État et de la marchandise. Une lutte entre les tendances qui portent le discours de dissociation d'avec les violences et les pillages, et les tendances qui poussent à la radicalisation, l'offensivité et la prise au tas. Cette lutte s'est faite par des discussions, des engueulades, et parfois des coups. Mais très vite il s'est avéré que la tendance réformiste était complètement dépassée, en particulier dans les métropoles de taille moyenne ou grande.


D'un point de vue général, c'est clairement la seconde option qui a gagné la bataille de l'hégémonie, en tout cas ce 17 octobre. Ce n'est pas un acquis pour toujours. L'autre camp de cette lutte dans la lutte, celui de la dissociation, s'organise pour répliquer. La gauche réformiste, partisane de la désescalade, de la négociation, de la respectabilité, de la République et de la démocratie est aujourd'hui dans le parti de l'ordre, préparant la contre-révolution. Elle y porte la solution démocratique et le retour à l'ordre par la réforme institutionnelle et le dialogue social (6

e

 République, nouvelle constitution, élection anticipées, etc.). La disquette habituelle, déjà expérimentée in vivo au Chili de 2019 à 2021 notamment. La gauche endort la révolte en engageant le processus démocratique de la réforme de l'État et en se posant comme l'alternative au fascisme. Mais partout où elle a été portée au pouvoir, elle n'a en réalité fait qu'entretenir le désastre, réprimant tout ce qui refuse son cadre et le déborde dans la lutte, préparant ainsi la victoire écrasante de l'extrême droite dans la foulée.


Mais le destin funeste promis au 21

e

 siècle n'est pas une fatalité. Les jeunes prolos se soulèvent partout dans le monde pour le refuser. L'autonomie, l'offensivité révolutionnaire, la volonté de synchroniser les offensives pour se constituer en force capable de détruire l'ordre existant, sont des positions qui existent dans la société. Elle ne sont pas majoritaires, mais elles ont une place de plus en plus importante dans la jeunesse prolétarienne actuelle. Et au vu du futur cauchemardesque et suffoquant promis par la bourgeoisie à notre classe, ces positions sont appelées à se répandre bien plus. Tout l'enjeu pour notre classe est de parvenir donc à se constituer en une force capable de frapper le monde bourgeois d'une façon si importante que cela lui soit fatal. Et de parvenir dans le même mouvement à poser les bases d'un rapport social où s'en sera terminé de l'exploitation, du fric, de l'État, des armes, des nations et de leurs colonisations permanentes, et de toute la liste des …

title: How The Proud Boys Lost Their Name
content:
West Palm Beach, FL – On Sept. 26, the film “American Martyrs” premiered at the Kravis Center’s Cohen Pavilion in West Palm Beach, Florida. 


The subject of the film, presented by the far-right media outlet Gateway Pundit, was the Proud Boys – specifically the “seditious five,” whom a federal jury found guilty of seditious conspiracy to stop the presidential transfer of power for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021 storming of the U.S. Capitol.


The official poster for the film, promoted by Enrique Tarrio and Gateway Pundit on X ahead of its premiere. Note that Zachary Rehl, first on the left in the lineup, is AI-generated.


The five Proud Boys presenting the film were chairman Henry “Enrique” Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joe Biggs, Zachary Rehl and Dominic Pezzola. In reality, the actual fifth member of the “seditious five” is Jeremy Bertino, not Pezzola, who pleaded guilty and testified against the others during their trial. 


In August 2025, Bertino appeared on an episode of Tarrio’s Substack podcast titled “Kiss of Judas,” where the “government star witness” allowed the permanently sunglasses-clad chairman to humiliate him for the twelve people who liked the post. Despite this entreaty to re-enter the flock, Bertino did not make the cut as an “American martyr.”


Besides Tarrio, who received a full pardon, the others had the sentences commuted by executive order during President Donald Trump’s first day back in office on Jan. 20, 2025. 


The film premiere, held less than four miles from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Club, was graced by numerous right-wing characters, including leading “Stop the Steal” figure and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani,

QAnon digital warrior

 and former U.S. Army general Michael Flynn and convicted fraudster George Santos.


Led by right-wing media figure Lara Logan, the event opened at 7 p.m. with an open bar that overlapped with a 10-minute window set aside for “prayer, national anthem and pledge.”


After the 80-minute film concluded, the Gateway Pundit presented Tarrio with a Gateway Pundit-branded award created specifically for the occasion recognizing him “as an American Martyr and Hero.”


“It’s not an Emmy,” Tarrio wrote on X two days later. “But it’s so much better.”


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Despite the obvious connections to the Proud Boys organization, the premiere lacked any of the recognizable branding belonging to what it depicted as a persecuted “drinking fraternity.”


Even on Tarrio’s person, the golden cock and abbreviated name have given way to the branding for his streaming outfit, “War Boys,” which has gained a whopping 700 followers on Rumble since the channel was created in April last year.


And on Tarrio’s merch website – where the Afro-Cuban now in his 40s markets just about any idea as apparel, including a t-shirt reading “Enrique Tarrio Eats Cream Pies” with an AI illustration of Tarrio licking an over-sized cream pie – reveals a distinct absence of Proud Boys related merchandise.


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Tarrio’s ability to capitalize on Proud Boys merchandising, which once characterized his merch store, hit a setback last year when a D.C. Superior Court judge awarded the brand to a historically-Black church following a years-long legal battle set in the wake of the 2020 Presidential election.


At the beginning of 2025, the Metropolitan African Methodist Episcopal (MAME) church was the only place one could purchase official Proud Boys merchandise, re-branded to signify Black pride, with proceeds going toward the church’s community justice fund.


In April 2025, the church’s hold on the brand was tested on the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, who were sued in the Southern District Court of New York for their continued usage of the Proud Boys branding and merchandising.


The court reached a default judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, a chapter associated with Tarrio, earlier this year on April 8, awarding MAME $75,000 for trademark infringement and nearly $200,000 in attorney’s fees.


The judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys is only a small part of the church’s pursuit to be fully compensated in the amount awarded by the court, which continues to be a major struggle to this day and sees all related parties continue to be wrapped up in the ongoing court battle.
