title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.


Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies


In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. While ever-greater resources are being devoted to armament and warfare, they say, poverty and social inequality are deepening. The consequences, they argue, are borne primarily by working and oppressed sections of society, women, and the natural environment.


The signatories view the growing strength of right-wing and fascist movements as part of this development. They argue that militarism, racism, sexism, hostility toward refugees and migrants, and the destruction of the natural foundations of life are interconnected. At the same time, social forces opposing these developments are increasingly being criminalized.


The organizations therefore call for stronger international coordination among movements of struggle. They remark that resistance movements from India to France and the United States, as well as Yemen and Rojava, must not remain isolated from one another. “Their experiences must be brought together and transformed into a shared framework of internationalist solidarity. Peace, democracy, and social justice cannot be expected from the very power structures responsible for war, exploitation, and oppression. Instead, the key lies in strengthening ties between working and oppressed populations across national borders.”


Joint resistance against AKP-MHP policies


Another key focus of the declaration is the political situation in Turkey. According to the organizations, the AKP-MHP government is exploiting the international shift to the right to consolidate its authoritarian system of rule on a permanent basis. They point out that repression against the political opposition, arrests, bans, and restrictions on democratic rights are aimed at suppressing social resistance and weakening organized opposition forces.


According to the organizations, those particularly affected include workers, trade unions, democratic organizations, intellectuals, artists, and opposition political groups. At the same time, the collective rights of the Kurdish and Alevi populations continue to be disregarded. Women face patriarchal violence and discrimination, while the protection of children and the right to life of animals, as well as the preservation of nature, are systematically neglected.


The organizations do not regard these policies as an isolated development in Turkey. Rather, they see them as part of a broader authoritarian offensive through which capitalist centers of power and reactionary governments are responding to social crises. This, they argue, makes it necessary to connect democratic and social struggles in Turkey with those in Europe and other regions of the world.


Democratic solution to the Kurdish question as a shared responsibility


The participating organizations explicitly address the peace and democratic society process, stating: “Although Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK have paved the way for political and democratic dialogue through their decisions to end the armed struggle, the AKP-MHP government and the Turkish state continue to refuse to take the necessary steps toward genuine progress.”

author: Danica Rachel
title: Operation Paperclip: The Nazis behind the US space program
content:
The Apollo moon landings are some of the most impressive technical feats ever achieved, and, for capitalism’s boosters, definitive evidence of the superiority of Western capitalism over all other social systems. The United States beating the Soviet Union to the finish line in the space race is held up as the ultimate triumph of capitalism over communism. But the path that took humans to the heavens began in the depths of hell: the Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp in Nazi Germany.

Built near the town of Nordhausen in central Germany, Mittelbau-Dora provided its prisoners as slaves to the Mittelwerk. This was a factory built under a mountain for the mass production of the V2 rocket, the world’s first long-range guided ballistic missile. The several thousand civilians killed in London and Antwerp by V2s were not the only victims of these Nazi weapons: at least 20,000 prisoners died as a result of the conditions in Mittelbau-Dora and the Mittelwerk.

Edwin Katzenellenbogen, who was convicted for crimes committed as a doctor at the Buchenwald camp, described Dora as “the Hell of all the concentration camps”. Tens of thousands of prisoners worked in interchanging 12-hour shifts, first to dig the kilometres-long tunnels of the Mittelwerk, then on the dark production lines within.

Sanitation was absent, disease and starvation were rampant, and collective punishment was common. Prisoners were hanged in groups of up to a dozen at a time, and on at least one occasion, bodies were left to dangle over the areas where others were forced to continue working.

Wernher von Braun was an SS officer, scientific director of the V-weapons project, and head of the Mittelbau-Dora planning office. He came from an aristocratic family in the German empire, and was among the first pioneers of advanced rocket science. Through the interwar years, Germany was banned from investing in many kinds of weaponry under the Treaty of Versailles, but rockets were obscure enough to avoid being on the list. During this time, von Braun became a leading designer and inventor of the engines needed to propel explosive missiles over incredible distances.

He joined the Nazi Party in 1937. If you believe his version of events, he joined only to be allowed to continue his scientific work. Regardless of his political loyalty, he was at least comfortable enough with the genocidal policies of the Third Reich to enjoy the slave labour it provided to him from Mittelbau-Dora. He was certainly aware of the reality of the Mittelwerk, having visited the tunnels himself at least ten times.

As the walls closed in on the Third Reich, with US and British forces moving in from the west and Russians from the east, von Braun hid the most important of the design documents for constructing V2s. Alongside Major General Walter Dornberger, head of the German army’s weapons department, von Braun used the hidden documents as leverage to get an amnesty with the Americans, betting that the US wanted the weapons more than they cared about prosecuting war criminals.

He was right. Von Braun, Dornberger and many other German experts in weapons of many terrifying forms—ballistic, chemical, and biological—were brought across the Atlantic under a secret program known as Operation Paperclip. They began work in the US, making weapons for a new, but no less bloodthirsty, empire. Their pasts were whitewashed, with the story being that they were innocent scientists forced by circumstance into working for the Nazi regime.

For his part, Joseph Stalin got the Mittelwerk factory itself, which continued operation for a few years before its machinery was brought back to Russia, along with thousands of German technicians needed to operate it. The USSR also got the equipment and methods to manufacture sarin gas, a chemical weapon so potent that contact with a single droplet causes a painful death.

Sarin was invented by Nazi chemists, among them Otto Ambros, who tested it on Auschwitz prisoners. Ambros was convicted for crimes against humanity in the Nuremberg trials, but that wasn’t a barrier to later working for US chemical companies and the US army. Within a few years of the end of the war, both imperial superpowers were producing large quantities of sarin and other chemical weapons.

The Cold War and the arms race 

The new phase of world imperialism had the globe divided into the West, with the US on top, against the East orbiting the USSR. The prospect of direct hot war between the empires gave …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Int’l solidarity vs Pax Silica
content:
At the Shut the Pax Down: Resistance and Solidarity Against Imperialist Plunder workshop in Bangkok, Thailand on October 14, 2026. (Photo from ILPS Philippines Facebook page)

Despite the advancements of AI technology, there is also the growing resistance.

BANGKOK – Organizations from different parts of the world are now united against the Pax Silica Initiative to be signed by the United States and the Philippines in November. US President Donald Trump reportedly will visit the Philippines to sign the agreement.

“We are in a period of extreme conflict between two very powerful and imperialist countries and the US is trembling and shaking. We have to maintain that fervor of revolution, that ability to throw stones at them, to bring them down and to make sure that the US imperialist power is no more,” said Azra Sayeed, secretary-general of the International League of Peoples Struggles (ILPS) during an activity in Bangkok, Thailand dubbed “Shut the Pax Down: Resistance and Solidarity Against Imperialist Plunder” on October 14.

The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank (IMF-WB) held its annual meeting in Bangkok from October 12 to 18. Participants included central bank governors, economic policy makers and business leaders.

In a statement, the Campaigners of the Peoples Global Campaign (PGC) Against IMF and World expressed concern over IMF-WB’s push for new technologies, including the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in Global South economies.

The group said that the “frantic race” for AI dominance intensified mining and extraction in resource-rich countries in the Global South. Transnational corporations are extracting rare earth elements (REEs) and other critical minerals to meet the growing demand for AI infrastructure. To secure control over the AI supply chain, countries like the US initiated the formation of Pax Silica and other similar formations.

“We know that imperialism is about world domination and control over resources. In the previous century, the rivalry among imperialist powers centered on oil because whoever controlled oil could wield significant influence over the military and the economy,” Arnold Padilla, secretary-general of ILPS-Philippines said during the event.

Now, he stressed, the battle is over critical minerals as whoever controls AI and the critical minerals needed to build its infrastructure could gain a significant advantage in dominating the world. “Essentially, that’s the battle now between the US and China. So, who will control this critical sector?”

This is why, Padilla said, the Philippines is up for a major battle to halt the signing of the US-led Pax Silica Initiative this year in time for the Asean Summit from November 16 to 18.

He said that AI is not just about the software that people use but also about weapons like drones “that can make decisions in actual battles without any human intervention.” He added that these sophisticated weapons will be made of minerals to be extracted from the Philippines.

Read: Critical minerals policy framework linked to Pax Silica? Read: War and plunder: US imperialism in the Philippines

“Pax Silica is made up of 24 countries, of course, led by the US. And it’s a special coalition. Specifically chosen by the US because countries that belong to Pax Silica perform a specific specialized role because it’s about controlling the supply chain,” Padilla said. “We don’t have high technology, we don’t have the logistic network, we don’t have capital or energy. But what do we have? We have the critical minerals. So for us in the Philippines, this is all about plunder.”

Donna Denina, secretary-general of International Women’s Alliance (IWA), said that US Undersecretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg, former tech executive and adviser tied to the controversial software firm Palantir, designed Pax Silica to give the US control over the global technology supply chain.

Palantir is a technology firm with clients from the Pentagon and foreign militaries including the Israeli government. But Denina said that Palantir is now expanding its influence beyond military tech into the health care sector.

In the US, she said that Palantir’s AI software is being used to manage hospital staffing and scheduling. This raised concerns among healthcare workers and prompted protests.

She said that more than 1,000 nurses from the National Nurses United union protested against healthcare institutions’ contracts with Palantir …

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Heilige Drecksarbeit – Die deutsch-israelischen Militärbeziehungen und die Staatsräson
content:
Der vorliegende Text ist eine gekürzte Fassung des gleichnamigen Beitrags aus dem Sammelband „

Trümmer auf Trümmer. Zur Kritik der deutschen Staatsräson

“, erschienen bei der Buchmacherei. Das Autor:innenkollektiv beschäftigt sich hier ausführlich mit der historischen Genese der militärischen Beziehungen zwischen der Bundesrepublik und dem zionistischen Staatsprojekt sowie der Geschichte des Existenzrechts Israels als deutsche Staatsräson. Neben diesem Beitrag finden sich im Sammelband zahlreiche weitere Texte, die sich aus historischer, juristischer und politischer Perspektive mit dem Thema der „Staatsräson“, deren Bedeutung für einen neuen deutschen Nationalismus, dem Phänomen der „Antideutschen“, kolonialen und antikommunistischen Kontinuitäten und der aktuellen Bedeutung im Bezug auf den Genozid in Gaza auseinander setzen.

von

AK Beau Séjour


Wirft man einen vergleichenden Blick auf die Zahlen der deutschen Waffengeschäfte im Jahr 2024, so fällt auf, dass Israel mit 161 Mio. Euro nur an sechster Stelle steht. An erster Stelle stand im Jahr 2024 die Ukraine mit 8,1 Milliarden Euro, gefolgt von Singapur (1,21 Mrd. Euro), Algerien (558,7 Mio. Euro), den USA (319,9 Mio. Euro) und der Türkei (230,8 Mio. Euro). Es gehe, so wird immer wieder zu Recht angemerkt, den Herren Rheinmetall und Thyssenkrupp nicht um die konkrete Tötung palästinensischer Kinder, sondern um das allgemeine Geschäft mit dem Tod. Die militärischen Beziehungen zwischen Deutschland und Israel müssen, das ist fraglos richtig, auch als gewöhnliche deutsche Handelsbeziehungen zwischen handelsüblichen Schurkenstaaten betrachtet werden. Doch dieses profane globale Geschäft mit dem Tod braucht, insbesondere in Deutschland, einen robusteren Überbau als das Geschäft mit Autos oder Kosmetikartikeln. Laut Marx spricht die »scheinheilige und heuchlerische Ideologie der Bourgeoisie ihre aparten Interessen als allgemeine Interessen« aus.

1

 Und in Bezug auf Wirklichkeit und Ideologie der bürgerlichen Familie schreibt er weiter, dass »[i]hrer schmutzigen Existenz […] der heilige Begriff in offiziellen Redensarten und in der allgemeinen Heuchelei« entspricht.

2

 Die schmutzige wirkliche Existenz deutscher Außen- und Handelspolitik muss in vergleichbarer Weise sakralisiert und den Deutschen als ihr allgemeines und moralisches Interesse verkauft werden, insbesondere deshalb, da sich nach 1945 jedes deutsche Großmachtstreben verbot. Gerade hierbei spielt Israel eine zentrale Rolle. Die umfassende und bedingungslose Unterstützung Israels wird in einen Akt höchster Sakralität verwandelt – eine sakralisierte Beziehung, hinter der sich, wie noch zu zeigen ist, die aparten Interessen der deutschen Bourgeoisie verbergen.


Diese Sakralisierung staatlicher Gewalt drückt sich in zahlreichen Reden deutscher Politiker:innen aus. So verkündete Angela Merkel in ihrer berühmten Staatsräson-Rede von 2008: »Deutschland und Israel sind und bleiben – und zwar für immer – auf besondere Weise durch die Erinnerung an die Shoah verbunden«. Die ehemalige deutsche Außenministerin Annalena Baerbock leitete aus dieser Erinnerung zum ersten Jahrestag des 7. Oktober im deutschen Bundestag die Legitimität von Gewalt ab: »Die Sicherheit Israels ist deutsche Staatsräson, unabhängig davon wer regiert, unabhängig davon, wer Außenpolitik macht […] Das Selbstverteidigungsrecht Israels ist auch unsere Verantwortung. Dazu stehen wir nicht nur mit Worten, sondern auch mit Taten, und zwar jeden Tag.« Zwar gehören, so Baerbock, laut deutscher Staatsräson »das humanitäre Völkerrecht und das Existenzrecht Israels auf das Engste zusammen«, doch Selbstverteidigung bedeute selbst verständlich auch die vollständige Zerstörung des Gegners und »wenn sich Hamas-Terroristen hinter Menschen, hinter Schulen verschanzen, dann kommen wir in ganz schwierige Bereiche. Aber wir ducken uns davor nicht weg. Deswegen habe ich vor den Vereinten Nationen auch deutlich gemacht: Dann können auch zivile Orte ihren Schutzstatus verlieren; weil Terroristen diese missbrauchen. Dazu steht Deutschland, das bedeutet für uns Sicherheit Israels.« Die mobile deutsche Artillerie von Rheinmetall, die Sa’ar 6 Korvetten von Thyssenkrupp, die Motoren in den Merkava-Panzern vom Bodensee und die 120mm-Panzermunition aus Niedersachsen sind, nimmt man Baerbock beim Wort, der materielle Ausdruck des »Versprechens ›Nie wieder!‹, das wir in der Vergangenheit gegeben haben«, denn »›Nie wieder!‹ heißt, jeden Tag das Richtige und nicht das …

author: Unknown
title: Jugendstreik Basel
content:
Aufruf zum Jugendstreik am 20.11. in Basel


Als Jugendorganisationen aus ganz Europa, und darüber hinaus, rufen wir Unter dem Motto «FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE, NOT THEIR WARS» zum Internationalen Jugendstreik auf.


Auch in Basel gehen wir am 20. November auf die Strasse.


Demo: 14:00 De-Wette Park


Fest: ab 17:00 (Genauere Infos werden über die Instagramkanäle bekanntgegeben)


Wieso streiken wir?


Unsere Staaten rüsten auf. Die Jugend wird darauf vorbereitet, in den Krieg zu ziehen. Während die Regierungen Milliarden in Aufrüstung investieren, wird der Sozialstaat kaputt gesparrt.


Auch die Schweiz macht mit. So plant der Bund zum Beispiel einen Rüstungsfonds in der Grösse von 24 Milliarden Franken. Das Budget für die Armee für den Zeitraum 2025–2028 wurde bereits um 4 Milliarden Franken erhöht. Gleichzeitig wird mit dem Entlastungspaket 27 in über 60 Bereichen gespart, unter anderem bei der Bildung, der Gesundheit und beim Klimaschutz.


Es zeigt die Priorität dieses Systems: Die fortlaufende Erweiterung des Kapitals.


Der Kapitalismus kann der Jugend keine Zukunft garantieren!


Die Armee dient der Interessen der herrschenden Klasse. Die neuen militärischen Kapazitäten erweitern dabei den Handlungsspielraum zur Durchsetzung dieser Interessen.


Beispiele dafür sind der Einsatz des Militärs an der Demonstration gegen den G7 Gipfel, die laufende Grenzmilitarisierung oder die Waffenexporte nach Israel.


Wir sterben nicht für ihre Kriege!


Wir schauen solidarisch nach Deutschland und Frankreich wo sich bereits hunderttausende Jugendliche gegen die Militarisierung und Kürzungen wehren.


Für uns ist klar: Unsere Antwort auf die Militarisierungsspirale muss international sein.


Wir sterben nicht für ihre Kriege – Wir streiken!


Basel:


Demo 14:00 De-Wette Fest ab 17:00 (Infos werden auf Instagramkanälen publiziert)


Streiken ist ein Grundrecht. Wenn du aber aufgrund von allfälligen Repressionen deines Betriebes, der Schule oder Polizei verhindert bist, ist es auch möglich, deine Solidarität in Form eines Banners zu zeigen.

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: From Haile Selassie to Abiy Ahmed: the Human Cost of Imperial Nostalgia
content:
The irony is difficult to escape. Haile Selassie became a symbol of resistance to foreign aggression while denying Eritreans the right to self-determination. Abiy Ahmed was rewarded for accepting Eritrea’s internationally recognized border, yet within a few years his government began advancing claims to sovereign access to the Red Sea. The very territorial settlement that helped earn him the Nobel Peace Prize now stands in tension with his maritime ambitions.

Both men benefited enormously from international recognition. Their reputations gave them prestige and influence, but those reputations have too often overshadowed the suffering of the people under their rule. Haile Selassie’s imperial government suppressed resistance in Tigray and annexed Eritrea. Under Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia has endured devastating wars, while his government’s Red Sea rhetoric has renewed Eritrean fears of territorial aggression.

I have written about the dangers of romanticizing Ethiopia’s imperial past, most recently in Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa. What concerns me today is that this nostalgia is no longer confined to history books or monuments. It has returned to contemporary politics, and the consequences could be catastrophic for another generation of Ethiopians and Eritreans.

Haile Selassie’s reputation rests heavily on his resistance to Italian fascism. His appearance before the League of Nations in 1936 became one of the defining moments of his international career. But the familiar account gives the emperor far more prominence than the people who actually fought the occupation.

Haile Selassie left Ethiopia in 1936 and spent the following years in Britain. Meanwhile, Ethiopian patriots remained behind, fighting a brutal occupation. They lived in the mountains, organized resistance, endured enormous hardship and risked their lives. The emperor became the international face of their struggle, but he was not the one carrying its daily burden.

Consider Belay Zeleke, one of the patriots who fought the Italians. After the emperor returned to power, Belay came into conflict with the imperial government. In January 1945, he was executed alongside his brother and other associates. Think about the irony. A man who had fought foreign occupation was hanged under the authority of an emperor celebrated around the world for resisting that same occupation.

The emperor’s record in Tigray reveals another contradiction. In 1943, when people in Tigray rose against imperial authority during the first Woyane uprising, Haile Selassie turned to Britain for military assistance. British Royal Air Force aircraft bombed Mekelle and other locations. As Human Rights Watch documented, British air power helped suppress resistance to the imperial government.

Here was an emperor celebrated for standing against European aggression using European aircraft against people resisting his own rule. How does that fit the image of a champion of freedom?

Haile Selassie’s reputation as a Pan-Africanist also deserves scrutiny. His role in establishing the Organization of African Unity in Addis Ababa in 1963 was important. But diplomatic achievement should not be confused with a consistent commitment to African freedom.

Haile Selassie and his foreign minister, Ketema Yifru, worked to establish Ethiopia as a center of African diplomacy. Hosting the OAU gave the emperor enormous prestige. Yet the same government was denying Eritreans the right to determine their future.

Eritrea’s federal autonomy had been systematically dismantled before Haile Selassie annexed the territory in 1962. While the emperor was celebrated as a defender of African independence, Eritreans were beginning a liberation struggle that would last thirty years.

The OAU largely treated Eritrea as an internal Ethiopian matter. Its silence is especially striking when compared with Western Sahara. The organization admitted the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic despite Morocco’s fierce opposition. It was prepared to confront one African government over self-determination but failed to extend comparable recognition to Eritreans struggling against Ethiopian rule.

The romanticization of Haile Selassie reached extraordinary heights through the Rastafari movement. Emerging from racial oppression in Jamaica, the movement invested in the Ethiopian emperor with immense spiritual and political significance. For some Rastafarians, he became a …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: The latest on Gabriel Rockhill’s “Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?”
content:
Controversy, controversy…it’s no surprise that this book is selling very well. See more on this from

Bisharat Abbasi

, in his post: “

In Defence Of Gabriel Rockhill’s

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism: Anti-Imperialist Marxism Versus The Imperial Theory Industry

.

“


DIGEST: Reviews, interviews, appearances


Marx Memorial Library

in London hosted a dual book launch for

Requiem for French Theory

 and

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?

with Gabriel Rockhill, Aymeric Monville, and Jennifer Ponce de León, who engaged in a discussion regarding the effects of imperialism on the production and dissemination of knowledge. Far from simply engaging in a critique of the faux radicalism of the prominent discourses within the imperial theory industry, the discussion was grounded in a reasoned defense of the vibrant international tradition of anti-imperialist Marxism. Topics included the imperial promotion of Western Marxism and postmodern French Theory, the international war of ideas, the failed efforts to discredit anti-imperialist Marxism, culturalism and identity politics vs. a materialist analysis of the colonial question, fascism past and present, the dialectics of actually existing socialism, and the current state of global class struggle in theory and practice.

Watch here

or below


The Left Chapter

, reviewed by Leo Schwarz:


“Shortly before his death, Herbert Marcuse wrote an essay on Rudolf Bahro’s book

The Alternative in Eastern Europe

. In the essay, Marcuse hailed Bahro’s ‘critique of actually existing socialism’ as ‘the most important contribution to Marxist theory and practice in decades.’ This statement was part of a coordinated campaign for the book and for Bahro that swept through the major media outlets of the Western world between 1977 and 1979–80. As we now know (or can know), a striking number of the key figures in this campaign maintained connections in the postwar decades to the Central Intelligence Agency or to various institutions and organizations that were either controlled, funded, or considered ‘friendly’ by the CIA or the U.S. State Department. In the first volume of his three-volume reconstruction of the ‘intellectual world war’ against actually existing socialism, Gabriel Rockhill examines the history and specific function of these networks of the ‘imperial theory industry’ that emerged after 1945, with his interest focused primarily on the Frankfurt School and the academic “Marxisms” of the Western world, which are usually categorized as ‘Western Marxism’…..”

 Read more….


Kaanan

“…I was among those who criticized the Soviet system in its post-Stalin decades, and the lesson learned was that the greatest losers were the peripheral countries, especially the Arab nation, since the Soviets had long acted as a force restraining the imperialist beast. More importantly, this collapse was, in historical-materialist terms, a setback—an exception—because history fundamentally advances upward. Though our wounds were deep, the class enemy emerged victorious but also wounded, most notably by becoming the sole superpower, exposing its flaws and unleashing its brutality. In this brief context, I attempt to summarize Gabriel Rockhill’s book—a painstaking and rigorously documented scholarly work. Yet its timing is no less important than the work itself, for it constitutes a bold revolutionary confrontation that demonstrates the author’s profound communist commitment in an era when loyalty to communism has become rare and the fungi of internalized defeat have spread everywhere, filling the burrows with fleeing rats….”

author: ROAPE
title: Eusi Kwayana (1925-2026)
content:
Eusi Kwayana was born Sydney King, as he was known initially for his first, more than two decades in public life. In 1968 he took on his African name which in Swahili means ‘Black man of Guyana.’


Eusi Kwayana was a founding father of post-colonial independence Guyana and Caribbean politics and was associated with the triumvirate of personalities that shaped them: Cheddi Jagan, Forbes Burnham, and Walter Rodney. He came to write the anthems of the three parties they led. Yet his own contributions to the Black and global radical traditions are still being recognized and recorded. This will be challenging in an environment where he receives national and regional honors for being a mere educator, writer, and cultural activist. It’s undeniable; he was a revolutionary.


What does it mean that Eusi Kwayana was a revolutionary? He was a campaigner against white supremacy, empire, capitalism, patriarchy, and ecological destruction. More than that, where he led breakthroughs against colonialism that denied Guyana, the Caribbean, and the Global South self-government, at the post-colonial independence moment he continued to confront the African and Caribbean political class, whether aristocratic or progressive. As historian and political activist, he always wished for everyday people to directly hold the reins of society. Of course, it was a matter of positioning ourselves to bring this about. His strategies of what to do and how to do it, must be revisited.


Detained When Guyana was Occupied by Anglo-American Imperialism


Eusi was detained when the Cheddi Jagan-led People’s Progressive Party (PPP) was overthrown by Anglo-American empire after winning election to Guyana’s colonial legislature in 1953. The country was occupied for 133 days. Before the Cuban Revolution of 1959, the PPP of Guyana was seen as a major threat to US and British hegemony during the Cold War in the Western hemisphere.


Eusi, with Rory Westmaas and Martin Carter, were perceived as the ‘ultra-left’ of the PPP.  In 1956, the split with Cheddi Jagan came, not over disagreements about commitments to a multi-racial party or movement. Rather, when Eusi and others advanced and defended the inclusion of Guyana in the movement for West Indian Federation. It was a permanent concern.


Multi-Racial Unity, Black Autonomy, and Caribbean Federation


This was part of an unfolding process of awareness. Cheddi Jagan was a socialist cosmopolitan when he faced the wider public. But he was also an ethnic leader of the Indo-Guyanese. Eusi concluded that it was no creative conflict to be an advocate for Afro-Guyanese as well. And it was important to address his Afro-Guyanese constituency

within the hearing

 of the Indo-Guyanese.


In 1959, Eusi became friendly with CLR James and Selma James in Trinidad at the height of the movement for colonial freedom led by Eric Williams’s People’s National Movement (PNM). He learned some important things about political journalism and activism in dialogue with CLR as he was editing

The Nation,

and Eusi was responsible for the People’s National Congress’s (PNC)

The New Nation

in Guyana.


Making Guyana a Global Refuge


In 1961, Eusi founded African Society for Racial Equality (ASRE) with the scientist H.H. Nicholson, known as ‘Vigilance’, and in 1964, co-founded African Society for Cultural Relations with Independent Africa (ASCRIA). With his wife

Tchaiko Kwayana

, an African American from Georgia in the US, who made her own mark as a teacher in New York and California, and her own sojourns to Nigeria, Ghana, and Latin America, Eusi pioneered the African cultural revolution in the Western Hemisphere, and was a transmission belt for African Americans and continental Africans finding a refuge from white supremacy and empire in Guyana as they pursued self-reliance and cooperative living. He was instrumental in making powerful ties between Ghana and Guyana.


It was Eusi that in 1966 gave Forbes Burnham the idea for Guyana being known as the ‘cooperative republic’ at official independence. In the early 1970s, Eusi was a supporter of the most dedicated cooperatives in the hinterland, such as the one at Marudi led by Joe Maxwell. The most dynamic cooperatives would be repressed by the state before the famous Jonestown fiasco.


An Original Educator of the African World


Eusi’s travels in Africa in 1964-65 and 1969 brought him to Nigeria, Mali, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Ghana, and Guinea-Conakry.  As a leader …

author: anred
title: Misiones: denuncian amenazas de desalojo contra una Comunidad Mbya en Puerto Iguazú
content:
Un nuevo procedimiento irregular tuvo lugar en una Comunidad Mbya en Misiones. Esta vez, en Kuaray Amba, ubicada en las 600 Hectáreas de Puerto Iguazú, donde efectivos policiales se presentaron sin previo aviso junto al Subsecretario de Gobierno, Asuntos Registrales y Tierras de Misiones y una agente municipal de Asuntos Guaraníes, y advirtieron a sus integrantes que debían abandonar el territorio.

Por Equipo Misiones de Pastoral Aborigen

.


Lidio Rivarola, mburuvicha de la Comunidad, relató que la primera visita ocurrió el 16 de septiembre. «Me dijeron: ‘Ustedes tienen que salir de acá y ver dónde se van a ubicar’. Yo le dije que no, que es nuestro territorio», recordó.


La segunda visita se produjo el 21 de octubre, nuevamente sin aviso previo ni documentación que respaldara el procedimiento. Según relató Rivarola, comenzaron a solicitar información sobre la cantidad de familias y personas que integran la Comunidad.


«El 21 de octubre vinieron de vuelta y fueron a pedir datos a la gente, de cuántas familias y personas somos. Yo no estaba, le dijeron a mi segundo cacique que era para llevar a la jueza. Andan diciendo que van a desalojarnos, nos están amenazando», denunció.


La situación genera temor entre las familias ante la posibilidad de un desalojo por la fuerza. «Quiero saber por qué están amedrentando a la Comunidad. Mi gente tiene miedo de ser desalojada a la fuerza. Yo les dije que no hay que tener miedo porque nosotros tenemos derechos», expresó el mburuvicha.


Rivarola también cuestionó la ausencia del director de Asuntos Guaraníes y el accionar de la representante municipal, quien –según relató- se acercó únicamente para intimidarlos, en lugar de cumplir con su función de acompañamiento y asistencia a las Comunidades indígenas.


«Vinieron sin papel, sin nota, nada, las dos veces que llegaron a la Comunidad. Es un atropello. Llegaron de sorpresa, sin aviso previo, no cumplen con la ley, no nos respetan», sostuvo.


Un mecanismo que se repite


Lo ocurrido en Kuaray Amba no es un hecho aislado. Se inscribe en un contexto de hostigamiento y vulneración de derechos que atraviesan distintas Comunidades Mbya en Misiones, muchas veces por parte de organismos estatales que deberían garantizar su protección.


El caso de Puente Quemado II es un antecedente reciente. En mayo de este año, integrantes de esa Comunidad sufrieron un operativo policial en el que fueron detenidos el mburuvicha y otras personas, entre ellas mujeres y niños, en un procedimiento denunciado como un desalojo encubierto. En julio, la Comunidad volvió a enfrentar otro desalojo.


La reiteración de estos hechos expone una forma de intervención que profundiza la violencia y el temor de las familias indígenas, mientras sus derechos territoriales siguen siendo vulnerados.


Frente a un avance sistemático sobre los territorios indígenas, la defensa territorial también debe ser sistemática y organizada.

      

  


Equipo Misiones de Pastoral Aborigen

author: Mag
title: Die Form des Wirtschaftens ändern: Mit dem Sozialstaatsprinzip zu Vergesellschaftungen
content:
Dossier


„

… Vergesellschaftungen sind nicht mehr eine abstrakte Angelegenheit, ihre Notwendigkeit wird immer auffälliger. (…) Mit der Initiative »Deutsche Wohnen enteignen« in Berlin, die die Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungsunternehmen erreichen will, wurden Vergesellschaftungen erstmals zu einem realistischen Szenario in der Politik. Die Corona-Krise zeigt, dass insbesondere im Gesundheitssektor ebenfalls über Vergesellschaftungen nachzudenken ist, denn der Markt regelt jedenfalls nicht, dass die Bedürfnisse befriedigt werden können. Wohlgemerkt, Vergesellschaftungen, nicht Enteignungen. (…) Wenn über Vergesellschaftungen gesprochen wird, dann geht es um die Erfüllung des Sozialstaatsgedankens des Grundgesetzes. Nicht alles kann oder sollte vergesellschaftet werden, aber wenn es um die Daseinsvorsorge geht und der Markt nachweislich keine Lösung bietet, müssen sie thematisiert werden…“

Bemerkenswert ist, wer sich hier gegenübersteht. IW und IfW argumentieren weniger als Vertreter der »Wirtschaft« oder der »Arbeitgeber«, sondern schlicht als Vertreter des Eigentums, und zwar des Eigentums an jenen Dingen, die die ganze Gesellschaft braucht: Wohnungen, Büros, Fabriken. Auf der anderen Seite steht das IMK als Vertreter der Lohnabhängigen, also der Nicht-Eigentümer. Die eine Seite repräsentiert jene, die von ihrer Arbeit – dem Lohn – leben. Die andere Seite jene, die von ihrem Eigentum – Miete, Zins, Dividenden – leben, also von der Arbeit der anderen. Der Reichtum der einen – teure Immobilien, hohe Aktienkurse, steigende Preise – ist die Armut der anderen.


Dass dieses Verhältnis Bestand hat, darin besteht letztlich das »Investorenvertrauen«, das eine Vergesellschaftung zu beschädigen droht. Nun könnte einem dieses Vertrauen der Eigentümer herzlich egal sein – wäre von ihm nicht alles abhängig im herrschenden System. Denn die erfolgreiche Investition, also die Kapitalrendite, ist die Quelle nicht nur für Gewinne, sondern auch für Arbeitsplätze, für Lohneinkommen, fürs Wachstum und damit auch für die Einnahmen des Staates, die die Basis seiner Verschuldungsfähigkeit bilden.


Insofern ist die Warnung vor Kapitalflucht und steigenden Zinsen nicht trivial. Sie verweist auf ein reales Problem bei dem Bemühen, die »Bezahlbarkeit« des Lebens für die breite Masse zu sichern und gleichzeitig die Eigentümer nicht zu verschrecken. Das IMK hält sich hier bedeckt: Es nennt einen Vertrauensverlust der Investoren im Zuge einer Vergesellschaftung zwar »theoretisch plausibel«. Praktisch aber sei das Ausmaß dieses Verlustes und seine Folgen »weitgehend offen«. Was aber, wenn …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Housing, homelessness in focus in Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier race
content:
Six candidates are vying to represent Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier ward ahead of next week’s municipal election, with housing, homelessness and support for the Inuit community among campaign issues.


Ottawans are set to elect ward councillors Monday to a four-year term. Rideau-Vanier includes Vanier, sometimes called “Little Nunavut,” home to an urban Inuit community.


Statistics Canada counted 1,270 Inuit in Ottawa in the 2021 census.


Lyra Evans, Julie Fiala Chartrand, Brian Paquette and Michael Karl Sewanaku spoke with Nunatsiaq News about issues that could impact Inuit residents in the ward.


Evans, a former Ottawa-Carleton District School Board trustee and chair, said residents have raised concerns about homelessness, addiction, poverty and food insecurity.


“Pushing people out of a park and destroying all their belongings doesn’t stop them from being homeless,” Evans said, criticizing the city’s approach to encampments.


For more than 30 years, the Rideau-Sussex pedestrian underpass has served as a gathering place for unhoused Inuit. Police patrols, tickets and removals over the summer have

scattered

 people throughout the city.

Evans, who experienced homelessness as a teenager, said Ottawa needs more supportive housing.


“I was fortunate enough to get the resources and support from the system to move from homelessness into a transitional housing program,” Evans said. “But those resources and that support should exist for everyone.”


Chartrand, an artist and community organizer, said she has friends in the Ottawa Inuit Circle, a mutual aid group, and has advocated for it when she was co-chair of a safety committee with the Vanier Community Association.


Her great-uncle, Cst. Albert “Frenchie” Chartrand, was an RCMP officer who spent years in the Arctic, spoke Inuktitut and had family ties to Gjoa Haven.


She has proposed a permanent intercultural gathering space in Rideau-Vanier guided by Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, or Inuit cultural values. She said she also hopes to address safety concerns about aggressive dogs and the sexual exploitation of Inuit women, if elected.  


Paquette, an entrepreneur, martial arts instructor and youth worker, said he has not directly approached Inuit organizations during the campaign. He said he wants to support residents facing homelessness, addiction or mental-health crises.


Paquette said he would donate at least 20 per cent of his councillor’s salary annually to food banks and homeless shelters. He also proposed more proactive overnight police patrols.


Sewanaku, who holds law and medical degrees and is training as a family medicine resident,

argued the city should not displace people without offering alternatives or addressing why they are homeless.


His platform proposes a housing first approach and a public report on the costs of homelessness.


While he has not spoken with Inuit organizations and residents as much as he should have during the campaign, he said he was open to hearing their concerns.


Incumbent Coun. Stéphanie Plante did not respond to an interview request.


During her term, she supported

renaming

 Sandy Hill Park to Annie Pootoogook Park after the Inuk artist and Emond Park in Vanier to Mary Papatsie Park to honour an Inuk woman whose remains were found in Ottawa in 2022.


Eric Smith’s nomination information did not include contact details.

author: James Crump
title: Berlin’s Plan to Take Back Homes Will Cost Europe’s Biggest Landlord £7bn
content:
Europe’s largest residential landlord is set to lose €8.4bn (£7bn) as a result of plans by leftwing political party Die Linke to bring more than 140,000 Berlin flats into public ownership.


The real estate company Vonovia, which owns roughly 130,000 apartments in the city and

528,000

 across Europe, would be the most affected by the plans, with 120,000 of its apartments set to be put into public ownership. Real-estate giant Heimstaden would also be hit hard with a projected loss of $1.5bn (£1.26bn), according to the

Financial Times.


Die Linke, which won Berlin’s state elections in September, has agreed to talks with the city’s Greens and Social Democrats as part of plans to transfer ownership of flats from companies that own more than 10,000 apartments, with the legislation scheduled to be brought forward in 2028.


Any apartments owned above that 10,000 threshold would have to be transferred into public ownership as part of the policy, with Die Linke proposing an average compensation of around €100,000 per apartment – around 40% below the market value.


Vonovia’s 130,000 Berlin properties have an average market value of $130,000, meaning the company would lose a projected $8.4bn if the legislation becomes law. The company’s chief executive Luka Mucic has labelled the plans as “unconstitutional”, adding that the country needs “reliability, legal certainty and a stable investment environment.”


Housing was a

key factor

in September’s Berlin elections and has been growing in importance over the last half-decade, with 10% of the city’s residents currently living in

housing poverty

and 160,000 reported to have

left the

 capital in 2025. In 2021, Berlin’s residents voted in favour of the city’s government seizing privately-owned flats from large corporate landlords, although that vote was not legally binding.


In order to govern in Berlin, Die Linke has had to form a three-way coalition with the progressive Greens and centre-left Social Democrats, leading to potential political concessions from the leftwing party. The Greens came fourth in September’s election on a commitment to push the property law through, but the Social Democrats’ leader publicly

opposed the policy

 en route to a fifth place finish.


Support for Israel is also a sticking point between the three coalition parties, with the Greens and Social Democrats insisting that “Israel’s right to exist” be non-negotiable if they are to govern together. The parties rejected general boycotts against Israel and did not state whether Palestine has a

right to exist

 in a joint document announcing the talks.

author: Marianne Dhenin
title: Tenants Unions Anticipate Housing Policy Gains After Progressives Win in RI
content:
Reclaim Rhode Island demonstrates the power of tenant organizing to effect change in local politics.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The housing crisis emerged as a central issue last month in Providence, Rhode Island, as Democratic socialist David Morales unseated incumbent Brett Smiley in the Democratic primary for mayor and a slate of progressives won their city council races in primaries throughout the Ocean State’s largest city.

In April, Smiley vetoed a rent stabilization ordinance passed the day before, and a month later the city council came up one vote short of overriding his veto.

“The campaign for rent stabilization and Brett Smiley’s veto of it laid the whole framework and groundwork for both David Morales’s race and the council slate,” said Daniel Denvir, co-chair at Reclaim Rhode Island, a member-led housing justice and progressive organizing group that is driving the growth of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. “It was a race around rent stabilization and with a clear mandate to pursue social housing — and we won every single contested race in the city. Now, Providence will be really an unparalleled site for innovative progressive solutions to the housing crisis.”

Reclaim grew out of connections organizers made working on the 2020 Bernie Sanders campaign in Rhode Island and has had some major successes organizing tenant unions across Providence County and in fighting to ban practices that drive rent hikes and profit for landlords, like algorithmic rent setting. One of its biggest wins in the tenant organizing sphere came this June when residents at Charles Place launched their union with supermajority support, becoming the largest chapter of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. The 200-unit apartment block is home to Section 8 tenants, many of whom are aging or disabled. The union has forced the building’s landlord to the table to negotiate an agreement expected to fix persistent problems, including broken air conditioners, an unreliable elevator, and absent management.

After the rent stabilization ordinance in Providence was quashed and an earlier Reclaim-backed effort to protect tenants from unreasonable evictions by codifying just-cause eviction at the state level failed, the organization shifted some of its efforts to organizing around progressive candidates who could help overcome institutional barriers to its just housing agenda in the legislature.

The City of Providence is among the nation’s least affordable for renters. Last year, the city council’s housing crisis task force found that almost half of the city’s renters are spending beyond their means on housing.

“It’s a working-class city, it’s a diverse city, it’s a young city, it’s an artistic and bohemian city, and the unaffordability of housing threatens all of those things that make Providence special,” Denvir told Truthout. “That’s an objective social and economic reality, [and] the role of political organizations like Reclaim Rhode Island is to organize the objective crisis into a collective political response that brings people together to exercise collective power to solve that crisis.”

With progressives expected to hold a majority, if not a supermajority, on Providence City Council after the general election, local organizers are looking forward to implementing the solutions they fought for on the campaign trail.

While candidates were campaigning ahead of Providence’s September 9 primaries, Reclaim fielded about 200 volunteers who knocked on thousands of doors on joint canvasses for Morales and progressive city council candidates. “We won this on the doors,” said Miguel Martínez Youngs, who defeated incumbent John Goncalves by 68 votes in the Democratic primary in Ward 1. Youngs will run unopposed in the general election on November 3.

Ward 1 includes downtown Providence and historic neighborhoods where residents have faced waves of gentrification and displacement. It also includes College Hill, home to Brown University and one of the city’s most affluent neighborhoods. Goncalves has represented the district since 2020 and bills himself as a progressive. But he was also a deciding factor that saw Smiley’s veto of the rent stabilization ordinance stand when he opted not to show up for the vote to override it. “I got good on the campaign trail saying, ‘It wasn’t a no vote, it was a no show — which is worse,’” …

title: Navigieren auf einer neuen Welle von Unruhen
content:
Jetzt ist es wieder soweit, europäische Regierungen zucken zusammen vor Tausenden Randalierer*innen die in den Metropolen auf die Straße gehen, ohne das sie von den Polizeikräften in Schach zu halten sind.


Macron tönt, nicht zum ersten Mal in seiner Amtszeit:

"Wer zerstört hat, muss dafür bezahlen. Wer geplündert hat, muss den Schaden ersetzen. Wer versucht hat, die Republik zu stürzen, wird dafür zur Rechenschaft gezogen."


Die Papageien der Medien schäumen vor Wut, wie immer wenn die Ohnmacht die Seiten wechselt, und auch die freiwilligen Putzkräfte, die im Sommer 2017 beim G20 in Hamburg mit Bürsten die Bordsteine des Schanzenviertels von Krawallspuren beseitigten sind am Start. Jetzt kratzen sie in Paris geschmolzene Leihräder aus dem Asphalt oder sortieren Mülltonnen in Mailand.


Aber wo sind wir? Überrascht von diesen Wutexplosionen, zu deren entstehen wir wie so oft, nicht viel beitragen konnten. Um nicht den Überblick zu verlieren, eine unvollständige Zusammenfassung der letzten Events,


Brüssel


Am 9. Oktober folgten 30.000 Menschen den Aufrufen von Gewerkschaften gegen die antisozialen Maßnahmen der Regierung. Schüler*innen und Student*innen blockierten Bildungseinrichtungen. Von morgens bis abends kam es im Zentrum, im Bereich der Bahnhöfe zu Zusammenstößen mit den Bullen. Unterbrechung des Konsums, statt die wie eine Pest verbreiteten E-Scooter für eine leicht zu trackende Fortbewegung zu nutzen, werden sie heute von Jugendlichen massenhaft ins Feuer geworfen. Die Spannungen hatten sich schon an den Vortagen und auch in anderen Städten angekündigt.


Am 17. Oktober weitere Krawalle in Brüssel und Lüttich, 195 Festnahmen bei einer Demo gegen die Sparmaßnahmen im frankophonen Bildungswesen, gegen die Polizei und gegen die aktuelle belgische Regierung.


Paris


Nachdem letztes Jahr eine Alles Blockieren Bewegung im September an vielen Orten eskaliert war, wurde deren vermeintliches Ende mit einer lahmen Stimmung eines müden Generalstreiks Anfang Oktober 2025 besiegelt. Um plötzlich mit den diesjährigen Bildungsprotesten und Schulblockaden in eine neue Runde zu gehen. Seit Wochen tut die CRS das, was sie immer macht, sie schießen Demonstrant*innen mit Flash-balls die Augen raus und sprengen Jugendlichen mit Granaten die Hände weg. Aber offenbar war am 17. Oktober die Wut größer als die Angst und Frankreichweit wurden Bullen angegriffen, Geschäfte geplündert, Symbole des Staats zerstört. Trotz jahrzehntelanger Erfahrung mit Aufstandsbekämpfung, gelingt es Politik und Verwaltung bisher nicht, die Allianzen von Schüler*innen, Überresten der Gelb Westen, Banlieue Bewohner*innen, Linken und anderweitig Angepissten zu spalten. Macron, der seine Truppen von Kanaky bis Erbil kämpfen lässt und momentan besonders die Golf Monarchien verteidigen will, kündigt Verhaftungswellen und Ausgangssperren an.


Barcelona


Lange blieb es ruhig in Barcelona aber am 5. Oktober kam es wegen der Wohnungsproblematik zu Riots im Zentrum. 100.000 Menschen beteiligten sich an einer Demo, zu der die Sindicat de Llogateres tenants' union aufgerufen hatte, danach Unruhen im Bereich Plaça Catalunya und La Rambla. Bullen setzten wie immer Gummigeschosse ein, 30 Mossos wurden verletzt, Stadtmobiliar lieferte an 28 Stellen das Barrikadenmaterial. Die Sprecherin des Sindicat erklärte als Ziel, das Land zu paralyzieren. Die Regierung hat nach dem Tod von Maricarmen Abascal aufgrund der Zwangsräumung und ihrem Scheitern in der Wohnungspolitik Neuwahlen für den 29. November angekündigt. Anarchist*innen verteilen ein Flugblatt während der disturbios:


"Möge die Wut über alle hinwegfegen. Politische Parteien, Gewerkschaften, Parlamente, alle Organisationen links von der PSOE, Polizei, Richter, Journalisten, Faschisten, jeder einzelne von ihnen ist Teil desselben Apparats zur Kontrolle und Bewältigung unseres Elends. ... Unser einziges Ziel ist es, Bündnisse im Kampf und auf der Straße zwischen Gleichen zu knüpfen, unsere Klassenfeinde zu identifizieren und sie mit allen Mitteln anzugreifen."


Mailand


Am 17. und 18. Oktober erlebte Mailand in seinem kommerziellen Zentrum die Ausschreitungen, die es verdient. Dort drehte sich die Demonstration um die für viele nicht mehr zahlbaren Lebenshaltungskosten. title: Fırat: Cem Foundation seeks to appoint trustee to Kıraç Cemevi
content:
A vigil launched in protest against the eviction order to transfer Kıraç Cemevi, which was built through the collective efforts of local people in Esenyurt and has served the community for nearly 20 years, to the Cem Foundation has achieved its first result. The eviction has been postponed for one month. Those demanding the complete cancellation of the transfer decision are determined to continue their vigil outside the cemevi until their demand is met. Celal Fırat, Istanbul MP for the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF and said, “The Cem Foundation, which operates according to the government's mentality, is seeking the support of the government-appointed trustee who took control of Esenyurt Municipality to effectively impose a trustee on Kıraç Cemevi as well.”


‘The walls of this cemevi were built through the people's labour!’


Celal Fırat, MP for the DEM Party, brought the decision to transfer Kıraç Cemevi to the Cem Foundation on the grounds that it stands on Treasury-owned land before parliament and met with the Interior Minister to seek its cancellation. Fırat stressed that the cemevi had been built over the years through the collective efforts of the Alevi community.


Fırat explained that Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, as well as Turkmen and Çepni Alevis, live in the area surrounding Kıraç Cemevi. He said, “Around 20 years ago, Turkmen Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, together with our Çepni community members, came together in Kıraç, Esenyurt, and established a place of worship using their own resources. Some contributed their labour, others their earnings, and some donated an entire day's wages. The walls of that cemevi contain more than stone and concrete. They hold the memory of a neighbourhood, the sweat of its people, the prayers of mothers, the breath of pirs and the collective labour of generations. In the 1990s, when Alevi institutions had limited opportunities to obtain legal status and organise, many cemevis began operating under foundations recognised as serving the public interest. Kıraç Cemevi also began providing services under the Cem Foundation during this period. However, this did not change the fact that Kıraç Cemevi is a place of worship built and managed through the collective efforts of local people, where cem ceremonies have been held, lokma offerings shared and funeral services carried out for years. The Kıraç Cemevi Cultural Association, made up of local residents, has been responsible for running the cemevi for years. There had been no problems until now. However, problems have continued for the past year because the Cem Foundation has attempted to remove the existing local management and replace it with its own appointees, relying on the authority to make appointments granted by its statutes. Alevis are standing up against this imposition by the Cem Foundation, which refuses to recognise the will of the people. The community does not accept this system of appointed management.”


‘The Cem Foundation sought control of the cemevi from the trustee who seized Esenyurt Municipality’


Fırat pointed out that the Cem Foundation had claimed the land on which Kıraç Cemevi stands belongs to the Treasury and had requested its allocation from the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation and Esenyurt Municipality, which is under the control of a government-appointed trustee.


Fırat said that the dispute had led to legal proceedings between the parties. Although the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association filed a lawsuit seeking to suspend the eviction decision issued by Esenyurt Municipality, Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court rejected the request for a stay of execution. He explained that Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate served an eviction notice on the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association on 6 October 2026, ordering it to vacate the cemevi. Fırat said, “Citing the decision of Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court dated 10 September 2026, which rejected the request for a stay of execution, Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate claimed that the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association was occupying the premises unlawfully. The directorate notified the association that it must vacate the building and hand over the keys to the Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change under the Istanbul Governor's Office. The Municipal Police Directorate gave the association 15 days from the date of notification to vacate the premises and …

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Lautstarker Protest gegen Wohnraumvernichtung und Räumung von Menschen
content:
Ca. 60 Menschen protestierten am Freitagabend (23.10.) gegenüber der Gürtelstraße


39-41 gegen Vernichtung von Wohnraum und Verdrängung von Menschen. Dort hatten sie die aktuelle Wohnraumvernichtung direkt vor Augen. In der Gürtelstraße 41, einem ehemaligen Hostel, haben bis Ende September Menschen gewohnt. Seitdem steht das Haus leer und die Fenster wie die sanitären Einrichtungen wurden zerstört. Auch das Haus Gürtelstraße 39


ist eingerüstet. Eine Gruppe der ehemaligen Bewohner*innen erklärte, dass sie durch eine kalte Räumung ihre Wohnungen verloren haben. Offiziell hätten die Bewohner*innen erst nach einer Klage geräumt werden können. Doch nach einer von dem Sicherheitsdienst provozierten Auseinandersetzung mit den Bewohner*innen mussten sie das Haus verlassen und konnten nicht mehr zurückkehren. Erst Tage später konnten sie einige persönliche Gegenstände aus dem Haus holen. Zwei Wochen lebten die geräumten Bewohner*innen des Hugo-Hauses, wie sie das Gebäude nannten, in einem Zeltlager gegenüber dem Haus. Das wurde von den Behörden ab Mitte Oktober nicht mehr verlängert und die Bewohner*innen so ein weiteres Mal vertrieben und zerstreut. So sollte die Vertreibung unsichtbar gemacht werden. Auf der Kundgebung konnten die Bewohner*innen ihre Forderung „Die Häuser denen, die sie brauchen“ skandierten.


Doch die Wohnraumvernichtung geht nicht nur in der Gürtelstraße weiter. Daniel, einer der Mieter in der Habersaathstraße 40-48, berichtete über den jahrelangen Kampf der Bewohner*innen gegen die drohende Verdrängung. Erst wurden die Gebäude des ehemaligen Wohnheims für Krankenschwestern der Charité unter der Ägide des Finanzsenators Sarrazin privatisiert. Seit Jahren versucht ein Wohnkonzern das Haus abzureißen, weil es sich


dann besser verwerten lässt. Er scheitert bisher am Widerstand von Mieter*innen, die nicht einsehen wollen, warum die bereits energetisch sanierten Häuser verschwinden sollen. Sie haben bisher sämtliche Klagen gewonnen und müssen doch weiter um ihre Wohnungen bangen, wie Daniel berichtete. Die Häuser in der Habersaathstraße wurden auch zu einem Symbol für den Kampf um Wohnraum, nachdem ehemals wohnungslose Menschen


dort eingezogen sind. Derweil schafft der Eigentümer Fakten, indem er ebenfalls Mitte Oktober Menschen aus den Häusern räumen und damit auf die Straße werfen ließ. Weitere Redebeiträge kamen von Bewohner*innen der Rigaer Straße 94, dem Bündnis Zwangsräumung verhindern, Nicole und Steffen vom Wohnungslosenparlament, die seit Jahren die Mahnwachengegen Obdachlosigkeit vor dem Roten Rathaus wesentlich organisieren.Auch Vertreter*innen der Union für Obdachlosenrechte (UFO) betonten, wie wichtig die Selbstorganisation der Betroffenen Menschen ist. Sie machen es vor, in dem sie für ihre Rechte kämpfen. „Wir sollten weniger auf sogenannte progressive Mehrheiten im Senat warten, sondern in der Tradition der Berliner Mietrebell*innen den Kampf für unsere Rechte selber in die Hand nehmen“, sagte ein Vertreter der Gruppe „Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain“, die die Kundgebung organisierte. Sie war klein, aber ihre Stärke lag darin, dass dort Menschen sprachen, die selber von Wohnungslosigkeit und Vertreibung betroffen sind und für ihre Rechte kämpfen: Die Bewohner*innen vom Hugohaus in der Gürtelstraße, die Bewohner*innen der Rigaer Straße 94, die Mieter*innen der


Habersaathstraße 40 – 48, das Bündnis Zwangsräumung verhindern, die


Union für Obdachlosenrechte, Nicole und Steffen vom Wohnungslosenparlament, ihre Stimmen sind uns wichtig.


Eine Aufforderung an die Medien: Hört ihre Stimmen und wartet nicht


immer darauf, dass irgendwelche Parlamentarier*innen über Wohnungslose


sprechen.


Zum Schluss noch was zu einem leidigen Thema: Wie andere linke


Veranstaltung wurde auch unsere Kundgebung von gleich 3 rechten Streamern beobachtet und gestört. Einer der Streamer stelle gegen eine Mitorganisatorin der Kundgebung anzeigte, weil sie ihn fragte, ob er vielleicht aus dem rechtsextremem Streamermilieu kommt. Später konnte er sogar aus dem eigentlich geräumten Hugo-Haus filmen. Er habe die


Genehmigung des Sicherheitsdienstes gehabt. Hie zeigt sich einmal mehr,


wer auf der Seite des Eigentümerblocks steht und wer auf Seiten der von


Räumung Betroffenen.


passiert am 23.10.2026

title: Families in Washokani Camp stage protest: We want to return to our homes before winter
content:
Families who were forcibly displaced from Serêkaniyê and Til Temir and are living in Washokani Camp staged a protest today. Blocking the Til Temir–Hesekê road, the families demanded to return to their homes as soon as possible.


The protesters stated that they were facing numerous difficulties in the camp and that no organization was providing them with assistance anymore.


Camp resident Mûsa Mihemed from the village of El Menacîr, said that no organization was helping them anymore and that their living conditions were poor. He explained that winter was approaching and that when it rained, water poured through their torn tents, leaving them exposed to the rain. He demanded that they be enabled to return to their homes as soon as possible.


Another resident of the camp, Cabir Ebdulrehman, said: “I am from the village of El Kêf in Til Temir. We are organizing protests because we want to return to our homes as soon as possible. Our situation is difficult, theft has increased, there is chaos, and we have no means of making a living. We want the return convoys to include all displaced people.”


Mihemed Ebdulrehman, from the village of El Kinêhir in Til Temir, stated: “The return convoys only include people from certain areas. We want to return to our village before winter arrives.”

title: Galatasaray Üniversitesi'nde tutuklanan öğrenciler için eylem: 'Nehir ve Nevin derhal serbest bırakılsın'
content:
Fotoğraf: @tipli_ogrenci/X

Milli Eğitim Bakanı Yusuf Tekin'in Kadıköy Lisesi ziyareti öncesinde "Bize gelecek yoksa, sana huzur yok! Yusuf Tekin istifa!" yazılı pankart astıkları gerekçesiyle tutuklanan TİP’li öğrencilere yönelik dayanışma eylemleri devam ediyor. Galatasaray Üniversitesi (GSÜ) öğrencileri, tutuklanan sıra arkadaşları Nehir Dizdar ve İstanbul Üniversitesi (İÜ) öğrencisi Nevin Tekin’e destek vermek amacıyla kampüste eylem yaptı.

BirGün'ün haberine göre, gece yarısı evlerine düzenlen baskınlarla gözaltına alınan ve ifadeleri dahi alınmadan "Yusuf Tekin'i tehdit" suçlamasıyla tutuklanan öğrenciler için GSÜ'de pazartesi sabahı tüm dersliklerde boş sandalyeler bırakıldı. Boş bırakılan sandalyelere Dizdar'ın fotoğrafının yer aldığı "Bu sandalye boş çünkü sıra arkadaşımız tutuklandı!" yazılı posterler asıldı.

Kampüs içinde yürüyüş düzenleyen öğrenciler, ardından ortak bir basın açıklaması okudu. Öğrenciler adına yapılan açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verildi:

"Eğitim Bakanı Yusuf Tekin'in Kadıköy Lisesi'ni ziyareti öncesi bir pankart asıldı: 'Bize gelecek yoksa, sana huzur yok!' Bu pankartı asan sıra arkadaşlarımız Nehir ve Nevin, Yusuf Tekin'i tehdit ettikleri gibi meşru olmayan, uydurma bir gerekçeyle dün tutuklandı. Öğrencileri mahkûm bıraktığı geleceksizliğin eleştirilmesine dahi tahammülü kalmayan rejim tarafından tutuklandılar!

Görev süresince eğitimde gerici politikalarıyla şanını yürüten Yusuf Tekin'e hesap sormaktan geri durmayacağız. Bugün okullarda artan şiddetin de MESEM projesiyle korkunç koşullarda çalışmaya mahkum bırakılan çocukların da sorumlusu belli. Baskılarınız bizi susturamayacak. Galatasaray Üniversitesi öğrencileri olarak okul saldırıları sonrası eğitim emekçileriyle birlikte MEB önünde haykırdığımız gibi bir kez daha haykırıyoruz: Yusuf Tekin istifa!

Arkadaşlarımız için bir kez daha tekrarlayalım: Bize gelecek yoksa, sana huzur yok! Nehir ve Nevin derhal serbest bırakılsın!"

title: Ta walka to nasza sprawa – pikieta solidarnościowa z protestującymi we Francji
content:
Jeśli jesteście zainteresowani i zainteresowane tym co dzieje się obecnie we Francji i innych krajach Europy zachęcamy Was żeby „przystanąć” na chwilę i zastanowić się nad sytuacją w obecnej Europie późnego kapitalizmu.


21 września w liceum pod Paryżem młodzież zaczęła swoje pierwsze strajki. Były to pojedyńcze blokady licealistów, które finalnie rozlały się na cały kraj.


Postulaty dotyczyły fatalnych warunków szkolnictwa publicznego we Francji. Niszczejąca infrastruktura, spadająca liczba nauczycieli, która prowadziła do tego, że uczniowie szkół publicznych w ogóle nie mieli zajęć z języka francuskiego czy geografii, które potem musieli zdawać na maturze. W sondzie ministerstwa edukacji we Francji 55% nauczycieli szkół publicznych – licea, wskazało że nie jest w stanie wykonywać należycie swoich obowiązków ze względu na złą izolację termiczną szkół.


Dlatego młodzież zaczęła protestować. Do protestów zaczęli przyłączać się studenci a następnie nauczyciele i rodzice. Protesty zaczęły być masowe – ruch narodził się i zyskał dynamikę w uboższych i marginalizowanych dzielnicach Francji a jego motywacją była frustracja związana z gorszymi warunkami życia i dyskryminacją.


Tymczasem jaki obraz protestów dostajemy w Polsce? Bełkot skrajnej prawicy o tym, że protesty związane są z kontekstem narodowościowym czy rasowym. Zdjęcia na których widać osoby o innym niż biały kolor skóry, budowanie narracji o obcych, którzy wzniecają zamieszki. Tymczasem relacje młodzieży z protestów, które są obecne na mediach społecznościowych pokazują zróżnicowaną i solidaryzującą się grupę dla której kluczem był wiek, status społeczny a co za tym idzie uczestnictwo w publicznym systemie edukacji –

PIERWSZE KŁAMSTWO JAKIM KARMIĄ NAS MEDIA


Ruch we Francji stał się masowy – młodzież domagała się lepszych warunków edukacji, domagała się sprawiedliwości społecznej i bycia wysłuchanym. We Francji bunt ma szczególne znaczenie, jest częścią historii tego społeczeństwa. Trudno więc się dziwić, że kiedy wieloletnie wołanie o pomoc przez ludzi tworzących system szkolnictwa publicznego we Francji było ignorowane, kolejne pokolenie francuzów wyszło na ulice traktując protest jako formę uczestnictwa w życiu publicznym. Protest to coś więcej niż opór, konfrontacja z rządem czy policją. To dowód na samoorganizację i pomoc wzajemną gdzie nauczyciele, związki zawodowe i uczniowie ramie w ramie żądali spełnienia swoich postulatów. Osoby podjęły walkę o odzyskanie prawa do organizowania się i oddolnego decydowania o swoim miejscu nauki czy pracy. Jednak nie możemy zapominać, że każdy skuteczny protest dla władzy jest tylko kolejnymi zamieszkami. Aparat władzy pozwala na publiczne protesty tak długo jak pozostają one w akceptowalnych granicach. Kiedy ludzie samoorganizują sie bez czekania na pozwolenie dochodzi do zachwiania fundamentów władzy. Francja protestowała przez prawie miesiąc, a rząd zamiast potraktować ich postulaty poważnie, uznał że dzieciaki trzeba zgnoić i zastraszyć. Uznał że pokaże im miejsce w szeregu. Przed 17 października (czyli przed datą największej fali protestów) zostało aresztowanych 7 tysięcy nieletnich protestujących osób – nieletnich! A co my widzieliśmy w mediach? Czy mówiono o postulatach, czy pokazywano warunki, w których nikt nie chciałby żeby jego dziecko, rodzina czy przyjaciel spędzali po kilka godzin dziennie pięć dni w tygodniu? Niestety nic z tego do nas nie dociera – palące się śmietniki, barykady uliczne i zapętlające się rolki pokazujące te same zamieszki – mają lepszą klikalność –

DRUGIE KŁAMSTWO JAKIM KARMIĄ NAS MEDIA.


I teraz najważniejsza rzecz, o której nie usłyszysz praktycznie w żadnych populistycznych kanałach informacyjnych – przemoc policji.


Francuska policja słynie z ogromnej brutalności. Prawo jest tam tak skonstruowane, że policja w dowolnym momencie protestu może w pełni arbitralnie, bez żadnego ostrzeżenia użyć siły. I takiej siły używali wobec nieletnich i wobec protestujących na ulicach Francji. Udokumentowane są przypadki chłopaka który stracił mowę ponieważ policjant celując w głowę strzelił do niego z wyrzutni granatów łzawiących. Wyrzutnia powinna być używana pod kątem, bo w przeciwnym razie zagraża życiu i zdrowiu gdyż nabój z kostkami łzawiącymi musi zdążyć się otworzyć.


Mimo to policja stosuje wyrzutnie jako broń celując nimi prosto w tłum protestujących. Policja francuska używa również broni na gumowe kule celując z niej w ludzi.


W mediach społecznościowych widzimy relację …

author: Unknown
title: Dilan Karaman’ın yarım kalan 25 Kasım yürüyüşü
content:
Geçen yıl Kasım günlerini hatırlar mısınız? Daha doğrusu Dilan Karaman’ı hatırlar mısınız? Önce, “hayatını kaybetti” diye duyuldu, sonra “intihar”, ardından “intihara sürükleme” ve bir dolu soru işareti, bilinmezlik, sorumlular, sorumsuzluklar, suçlamalar, yazılan raporlar, yazılmayan raporlar, soruşturmalar, tanıklar…


Yüzlerce insan Dilan için adalet istedi, sorumlular açığa çıksın dedi, talepler sıralandı…


Bugün, 25 Ekim’de ise bütün bunların ötesinde bir şey oldu. Dilan’ın ablası

Gönül Karaman

, “

Dünyanın En Güzel Dilan’ı / Dîlana Herî Xweşik a Cîhanê”

isimli bir derleme kitap hazırladı. Güldünya Yayınları etiketiyle okurla buluşan kitapta yoldaşının anlattığı Dilan’ı da okuyorsunuz, ailesinin hafızasında yaşayan Dilan’ı da. Fotoğraflarıyla, anılarıyla, geride bıraktığı izlerle…


Kitabın tanıtımı bugün Avcılar’daki Barış Manço Kültür Merkezi’nde yapıldı. Halkların Demokratik Kongresi (HDK) Eş Sözcüsü Meral Danış Beştaş, insan hakları savunucusu ve avukat Eren Keskin, Nimet Tanrıkulu, Kürt kadın siyasetçiler, arkadaşları ve ailesi Dilan’ı anmak için bir araya geldi.


Etkinlikte Dilan’ın yaşamından kesitler içeren kısa videolar da gösterildi. Onun ne kadar çalışkan olduğundan, yorulmak bilmediğinden, gülüşünden, yoldaşlarıyla kurduğu bağdan söz edildi.


Dilan’ı tanımayan biri olarak, anlatılanların çok daha ötesinde bir insan olduğunu hissettim. “Her ölüm erkendir” derler. Bu kez yalnızca bir ölümün erkenciliğini değil, ölümün ardından sorularla baş başa bırakılmanın, adalet arayışının ve bütün bunların içinde yalnız kalmanın ağırlığını da hissettim.


Peşimizi bırakmayan hisler


Ölenlerin ardından söylenen sözlerden biri de “Kel ölür, sırma saçlı olur”dur. İnsanlar öldükten sonra güzelleştirilir, eksikleri unutulur, anıları parlatılır. Ama Dilan için anlatılanlarda başka bir şey vardı. Onun yalnızca ölümünden sonra hatırlanan bir kadın olmadığını, yaşarken de bir mücadele yürüttüğünü, çalıştığını, ürettiğini, güldüğünü, sevdiğini ve hayatın içinde olduğunu görüyordunuz. Şüphesiz anlatılanlar, onu yalnızca kaybıyla tanımlamaya yetmiyordu.


Geçen yıl ölüm haberi duyulduktan sonra Dilan için ne kadar çok çaba gösterildi, neler yapıldı. Adalet talep edildi, sorular soruldu, açıklamalar yapıldı. Ancak Dilan’ın ve ailesinin yaşarken yalnız bırakıldığı hissi, bugün de peşimizi bırakmadı.


Salonda çok az insan vardı. 


“Baro seçimi vardı”, “yer uzaktı” ve benzeri gerekçeler sıralanabilir. Elbette herkesin kendi koşulları var. 


Dilan, içine düşürüldüğü duygulardan kurtulmak, sesini duyurmak için sesini yükseltmiş ama duyuramamıştı. Bugün, ölümünden sonra adını yaşatmak için bir araya gelenlerin önünde, kocaman konferans salonunun boş sıraları bana bu yalnızlık duygusunu yeniden hatırlattı. Gözyaşlarını tutmakta zorlanan kadınlar, ailesi, onu unutturmamak için emek verenler…


Gönül Karaman: Bu kitap, Dilan’ın yarım kalan 25 Kasım yürüyüşü


Dilan Karaman’ın ablası @GKaraman77252’ın bugün “Dünyanın en güzeli Dilan’ı” kitabının tanıtımında konuştu, dinlemenizi öneririm. https://t.co/wNiwlkXU6f


— Evrim Kepenek (@kepenekevrimm)

October 25, 2026


Dilan’ın ablası Gönül Karaman, kitabın hazırlanma sürecini anlatırken Dilan’ın anısını yaşatmak için bir araya gelen herkese teşekkür etti. Kitabın onun için taşıdığı anlamı, dayanışma ve ortak mücadele üzerinden anlattı:


“Herkes onun anılarının şahidi olarak o kitabın tamamlanmasına katkıda bulundu. Bunun bizim için anlamı çok büyük. Çünkü bu denli korkunç bir karanlık yine ancak bu renklerle aydınlanır. Bu renkler ki bizim sahiplendiğimiz dünyanın yaşanılacak yanı, tutunacak dalı, mücadelenin ışığı ve umududur.


“Aslında bu durum onun adıyla da çok uyumlu. Bu yüzdendir ki dünyanın en güzel Dilan’ı odur. Biran, Türkçede halay demektir. Halay çekmek kolektif bir eylemdir. İnsanlar bütün renkleriyle, stranlarıyla el ele tutuşmasını bilir. Yüz yüze bakar, adımlarla birlikte atılır ve en güzel şarkılar, en güzel ritimlerle tek bir ses olup söylenir.


“Dilan isminin bütün özelliklerini gerçekten de ruhunda taşıyordu. Onun anısına dair herkesin kendi ritmi ve rengiyle kalem tuttuğu bu eser, tam da onun isteyeceği gibi koroların tuttuğu bir dayanışma içerisinde hayata geçiyor. Bu yolculukta kalemleriyle onun yürüyüşünü sürdüren bütün yoldaşlarıma yürekten teşekkür ederim.


“Bu eser, onun yarım kalan, aslında hiç kalmayacak 25 Kasım yürüyüşüdür.”
