title: İsrail, iki askerin öldürüldüğü saldırının ardından El Halil’de kuşatma ve yıkım başlattı
content:
İsrail ordusu, işgal altındaki Batı Şeria’nın El Halil kentinde iki İsrail askerinin öldürüldüğü silahlı saldırının ardından geniş çaplı bir operasyon başlattı.


Dün (23 Ekim) El Halil yakınlarındaki geçici bir kontrol noktasına ateş açan iki Filistinli, iki İsrail askerini öldürmüş ve üçünü de yaralamıştı. Ateş açan Filistinliler yaklaşık 20 dakika süren çatışmada öldürülmüştü.


Saldırının ardından İsrail Başbakanı Binyamin Netanyahu, El Halil ile komşu Halhul’un kuşatma altına alınmasını istedi. İsrail güçleri kentin giriş ve çıkışlarını kapatırken bazı mahallelerde yaşayan Filistinlilerin evlerinden çıkarıldığı bildirildi.


İsrail ordusu operasyonun “saldırganların faaliyet gösterdiği bölgeyle sınırlı” olduğunu ve birkaç gün sürmesinin beklendiğini açıkladı. Ordu ayrıca bölgede silah ve “terör altyapısı” arandığını ve onlarca kişinin sorgulandığını duyurdu.


Netanyahu: Daha büyük operasyon yolda


The Guardian’ın aktardığına göre Netanyahu, Batı Şeria’da 1967’den bu yana gerçekleştirilecek en kapsamlı İsrail askeri operasyonu için planların hazırlandığını söyledi.


Operasyon için tarih açıklamayan Netanyahu, El Halil’de tahliyelerin ve yıkımların süreceğini, Batı Şeria’daki İsrail yerleşimlerinin de genişletileceğini belirtti.


İsrail Savunma Bakanı Israel Katz da saldırganların geldiği mahallelerin boşaltılacağını açıkladı.


Katz, El Halil’de uygulanacak yöntemi Gazze ve Cenin Mülteci Kampı’ndaki İsrail operasyonlarıyla karşılaştırarak, “Cenin Mülteci Kampı modeli El Halil’e geliyor” dedi.


“Bugün teröristlerin çıktığı El Halil’deki her aşiret mahallesi sakinlerinden boşaltılacak. Gazze’de olduğu gibi, Lübnan’da olduğu gibi.” İfadelerini kullandı.


Smotrich yıkım görüntülerini paylaştı


İsrail Maliye Bakanı Bezalel Smotrich ise saldırının ardından bir Filistinliye ait evin buldozerle yıkıldığı sırada çekilen görüntülerini sosyal medya hesabından paylaştı.


Smotrich, ruhsatsız olduğu belirtilen yapının yıkılmasının amacını “caydırıcılık yaratmak ve bedel ödetmek” sözleriyle açıkladı.


Yıkılan evin sahipleriyle saldırganlar arasında herhangi bir bağlantı bulunduğuna ilişkin açıklama yapılmadı.


İsrail Yüksek Mahkemesi, yıkımlar başladıktan kısa süre sonra işlemlerin geçici olarak durdurulmasına karar verdi. İnsan hakları avukatı Mohammed Dahleh, bölgedeki iki fabrika sahibinin adına yaptığı acil başvuruda yıkımların uluslararası hukuktaki kolektif cezalandırma yasağına ve İsrail idare hukukuna aykırı olduğunu savundu.


Dahleh, yaşananları şöyle değerlendirdi:


“Bugün gördüğümüz şey, Gazze’de kullanılan hukuka aykırı uygulamaların Batı Şeria’nın kalbinde tekrarlanması girişimiydi. Gazze’de ve Batı Şeria’daki mülteci kamplarında yaptıkları gibi tüm bölgeleri ortadan kaldırmak istiyorlar.”


İsrailli insan hakları avukatı Michael Sfard da Smotrich’in açıklamasının yıkımların “kolektif cezalandırma” amacı taşıdığına ilişkin doğrudan bir kabul olduğunu söyledi.


Filistinlilerin hareketi kısıtlandı


İsrail ordusu El Halil’de araç giriş ve çıkışlarını büyük ölçüde durdurdu. Kentte yaşayan Filistinlilerin bazı bölgelerden yalnızca üç noktadan, kimlik ve güvenlik kontrolünden geçirilerek çıkmasına izin verileceği açıklandı.


Filistin haber ajansı WAFA ise İsrail askerlerinin bazı mahallelerde onlarca kişiyi evlerinden çıkardığını bildirdi. AP’nin aktardığına göre kapanmalar ulaşımı ve sağlık hizmetlerine erişimi de etkiledi.


Yaklaşık 250 bin Filistinlinin yaşadığı El Halil, işgal altındaki Batı Şeria’nın en büyük Filistin kenti.


AFP foto muhabiri hedef gösterildi


Çatışmayı olay yerinden görüntüleyen AFP foto muhabiri Hazem Bader de saldırının ardından bazı İsrailli siyasetçiler ve medya kuruluşları tarafından hedef gösterildi.


Bader, başka bir haber için yoldayken kontrol noktası yakınlarında silah seslerini duyduğunu, güvenli bir noktaya geçerek çatışmayı fotoğrafladığını anlattı.


Bazı İsrail medya kuruluşları, isimsiz kaynaklara dayanarak Bader’in saldırıdan önceden haberdar olmuş olabileceğini öne sürdü. İsrail polisi ise foto muhabirinin saldırıyla ilgili önceden bilgi sahibi olduğuna dair herhangi bir şüphe bulunmadığını açıkladı.


Yabancı Basın Derneği (FPA) suçlamaları “tehlikeli ve iftira niteliğinde” olarak nitelendirdi.


Dernek, Bader’in uzun yıllardır çalışan profesyonel bir gazeteci olduğunu ve başka bir göreve giderken tesadüfen olay yerinde bulunduğunu belirterek, aksi yöndeki iddiaların gazetecilerin güvenliğini tehlikeye attığını söyledi.

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Does Wes Streeting Want Us Ready for War?
content:
Like many long-eyelashed men before him, Andy Burnham is sending mixed-messages. On the one hand, the prime ninister is keen to differentiate himself from his predecessor. Where Keir Starmer carried himself like a doctor who could only break bad news, Burnham is keen to stress that there is a role for the state in the improvement of people’s lives (even if it’s just capital punishment for playing reels without earbuds in). 


But how does the PM’s sunny disposition square with this Cabinet urging us to stock up for the apocalypse?


Wes Streeting – defence secretary, and creature hatched under a jar by the Labour Right – has urged Britons to

prepare for crisis

. The public has been advised to stock up with three days worth of water, food, non-mains light sources and stuff to keep warm, in case of disruption to supply chains caused by cyber-attacks, terrorism, or extreme weather events. You can find the government’s ‘Be Ready Checklist’

here

, and books you can burn in lieu of central heating

here

.


How big of a deal is this? Ordinarily, governments tend to prioritise the prevention of panic-buying. Readers may remember the toilet paper craze in the early days of the Covid pandemic, in which shoppers cleared shelves of loo roll because a rumour had gone round alleging that the Chinese had switched Andrex-production to the manufacturing of paper masks. It doesn’t take huge swings in consumer behaviour to put a dent in just-in-time supply chains – and the sight of depleted aisles can send people scurrying to buy even more. If ministers are advising people to stock up, it’s a sign that they sincerely think something scary is on the horizon.


The government’s resilience programme wasn’t a brainchild of Andy Burnham. It got going during

Keir Starmer’s time in office.

 Some critics say that Burnham hasn’t actually made

enough

 noise about it, pointing to

the lack of a big, shiny rollout

. But regardless of its prominence in No. 10’s grid, the instructions to the public to stock up in case of crisis is dominating the headlines today – and it’s perhaps meaningful that Wes Streeting’s public comments about the issue were made at the opening of a

new weapons manufacturing site

 in Shropshire.


As FT journalist Gideon Rachman noted on Newsnight last night, the language used by leaders in the West has been markedly hawkish on the prospects of World War III. Keir Starmer warned of a Nato war with Russia

as soon as 2030

; Mark Rutte, head of Nato, has said that we have to be prepared for wars of the scale that

our grandparents fought in

 (that’s the Second World War, not

the 2005 Ikea riots

). Rachman has warned that we could be

sleepwalking into World War III

 – I can’t help but wonder if some of our leaders are tapdancing there.


Threats to food supply – not least due to the

‘Godzilla’ El Niño

 superpowering extreme weather events – are real. But it might be the case that the government’s urging of preparedness is both a prudent message to the public in the face of an increasingly chaotic global order, and part of an effort to normalise the prospect of the UK being pulled into a brutal, meat-grinding war. It’s worth minding some of the lessons of the 20th Century: you can only manufacture so many weapons before they get used.

author: Unknown
title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

title: HORROR AS FLEEING HUNTED STAG COLLIDES WITH CAR CARRYING WOMAN AND CHILD
content:
On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds met in West Bagborough, an area which falls within the constituency of Liberal Democrats MP Rachel Gilmour. Rachel has recently spoken publicly about her support for “trail” hunting, presenting what is a grim and violent reality as something that reads like a Disney fairytale.


MP Rachel Gilmour at last year’s BHSA “trail” hunting day, reported in the West Somerset Free Press.


Although stag hunts do not profess to “trail” hunt, like their fox hunting counterparts, they too manipulate the current law, exploiting loopholes to ensure the continuation of barbarism that brings terror to the countryside.


Rachel’s comments come at a time when sickening reports of hunting in the area are piling up, and you would think someone who has previously worked as Head of Strategy at the Environment Agency, would have a greater understanding of the countryside and the views of those that live there.


12th of October 2026


North Dorset Hunt Sabs and Mendip Hunt Sabs were joined by Holford Against Hunting as they sabbed the Quantock Staghounds.

Reports and video footage

 from the day detail how a hunted stag crossed the path of sabs and was subsequently seen to safety, thanks to them calling the hounds off.


More stags were chased throughout the day, with one seeking refuge on land owned by the League Against Cruel Sports. Reports also detail how two pairs of hounds were out at the same time; only two hounds are permitted to be used under the relevant legal exemptions within the Hunting Act.


However, since the reports were published there has been a disturbing update.


A stag crosses the path of sabs as he desperately tries to escape the Quantock Staghounds.

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


At 4:30pm, two members of the public were travelling along the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford when they came across the hunt. As we continue to see, rabid hunt supporters will line roads, making as much noise as possible to prevent stags from crossing as they seek safety. This incident was no different, except that what was described as a “gigantic stag” ran across the road and collided with a vehicle.


A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”


The driver of the vehicle was a young woman with a small child on board, and thankfully, neither of them sustained any injuries, but both were badly shaken up. The hunt, showing absolutely no concern or regard for the members of the public who had been involved in or witnessed this horrific incident, fled the scene as police were called.


The witness went on to say that, despite looking for the stag, they couldn’t see him. Sabs have since reported that it is believed the stag did get away and was not killed by the hunt. However, after being hit by the car, there is no way of knowing what injuries he sustained or whether or not he ultimately survived this horrifying ordeal.


Quantock Staghounds causing chaos and terror in an area of “outstanding natural beauty.”

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


Excuses, excuses


Stag hunts often try to use the excuse of dispatching an injured or sick deer to justify their barbaric actions. However, on this occasion, when there was clearly an injured stag, albeit as a result of their actions, they were quick to flee the scene. 


In her recent defence of “trail” hunting, Rachel Gilmour has claimed that hunt meets offer “

companionship to retirees and widowers who might otherwise face isolation and loneliness.”

 She also added that hunting “

forms part of a long and richly woven rural social fabric that binds farms, villages and families together through shared work, ritual, and memories.”


Her comments are a far cry from the realities of hunting. Many people living within these communities are not only opposed to it but are also put in grave danger every time these hunts go out.


It’s not just stag hunting taking place under Rachel’s nose


As well as stag hunts operating in Rachel’s constituency, the Tiverton Foxhounds’ kennels are also located within it.

report

 from the day details how “

one fox after another”

 was chased as they kept watch from the ground and used their drone.

title: Lies the Fur Industry Tells!
content:
Mink and fox killers and their apologists often say the most ridiculous things to try and mitigate their losses after raids like the two we have seen in the last couple of months, in which 3000 or more captive mink were liberated from horrific captivity. Sample absurdities spouted as fact include:

Lie #1: Many or most of the escaped animals were run over and killed by cars.

– The absurdity of this statement is that before liberation, death was 100% certain. Every animal on the farm was bred to die by the end of November. While it is true a small number may be hit by cars after being released, most will not, and if nothing else they have been given a chance at freedom. In reality, fox and mink farms are located in rural areas with little traffic, the animals are quick and solitary animals, and it beggars belief to imagine them aggregating in the road waiting to be run over by the rare passing vehicle.

– Mink are in fact only a few generations removed from their wild cousins and have not yet had their wild instincts bred out. The “Mink Rehabilitation Project” led by convicted ALF liberator Rod Coronado proved this decades ago. Mink legally purchased from a fur farm were released into the wild and shown through observation to retain natural survival instincts and thrive in the wild after a lifetime in a cage. Studies with radio-collared mink demonstrate clearly the animals are capable of surviving in the wild. No, they won’t starve or freeze to death or die from dehydration. Most areas where mink are imprisoned are actually native habitat for American mink.

Lie #3: Most of the mink are recaptured

– Mink normally travel several miles a day. Most mink have dispersed into the surrounding fields before the liberation is even complete. A few may be recaptured, but only a handful at most. Its absurd to imagine hundreds of wild animals being recaptured by lunkhead farmers running around looking for them. Our hearts go out to those few recaptured who were given a shot at life and now have only suffering ahead.

– Captive, now free and wild fox and mink have no desire to be anywhere near humans and their “livestock” or pets. There may be some minimal impact on the local ecosystems temporarily while the animals disperse and learn their way around, but no habitats are decimated or overrun or rendered free of other small animals. And no, the animals do not kill wantonly and more than they need to survive, and they certainly don’t attack human bystanders, as some apologists have had the audacity to suggest.

Liberationists break the law in adherence to a higher law – one which states animals are not commodities, not objects, but sentient creatures with a right to live. They will fight for the lives of these animals “as if they were our own.”

The Animal Liberation Front and other anonymous activists utilize economic sabotage in addition to the direct liberation of animals from conditions of abuse and imprisonment to halt needless animal suffering. By making it more expensive to trade in the lives of innocent, sentient beings, they maintain the atrocities against our brothers and sisters are likely to occur in smaller numbers; their goal is to abolish the exploitation, imprisonment, torture and killing of all innocent, non-human animals.

Join the ALF – Historically, those wishing to participate in direct action have either acted alone or gotten together with others they could trust of like mind and just started doing actions. ALF cells of 1 or more persons operate independently, and typically are begun locally by like-minded individuals who decide to take action against animal abusers. To begin learning about direct action, start here and follow the links where they may take you. Only you can decide what action to take, when to get started, and how much longer the animals must wait for liberation.

The number of fur farms in America has dwindled from more than 300 in the 1990s to less than 100 today, as the fur industry continues its steady decline into oblivion. A listing of all known fur farms in North America, is available here: https://finalnail.com/

author: Sylvie Bunz
title: Nach Aufdeckungen: Rumäniens grausamste Hundetötungsstation schließt
content:
Update vom 21. Oktober 2026


PETA und seine Partnerorganisation sind schockiert über die behördliche Entscheidung, die Wiedereröffnung der Tierheime VetMedan und Daeni zu genehmigen. Seit Monaten kämpfen unsere NGO-Partner vor Ort gemeinsam mit PETA und anderen Tierschützenden sowie Organisationen mit aller Kraft dafür, dass diese Einrichtungen dauerhaft geschlossen bleiben.


Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern prüfen wir nun erneut, ob es juristische Möglichkeiten gibt, gegen diese Entscheidungen vorzugehen und die Umsetzung der Beschlüsse auszusetzen. Solange mit Hunden erhebliche finanzielle Gewinne erzielt werden, stoßen Tierschutzbemühungen immer wieder auf massive Widerstände und es wird deutlich, wie stark das System ist, das an dem Leid der Hunde viel Geld verdient.


Update vom 22. Juni 2026


PETAs Partner im Einsatz gegen Rumäniens Hundetötungsstationen: Uzunu von Aspa Ivets für immer geschlossen


Nach Jahren voller Leid, Gewalt und systematischer Tötungen wurde das von einem Privatunternehmen geführte Tierheim Uzunu im Juni 2026 dauerhaft geschlossen. Die Entscheidung markiert einen Wendepunkt – für die Tiere, für die Tierschutzbewegung und für alle Menschen, die sich unermüdlich gegen diese Grausamkeiten eingesetzt haben. PETAs Partner in Rumänien, der Verein Eduxanima, hat sich zusammen mit weiteren lokalen und internationalen Vereinen dafür seit Monaten intensiv eingesetzt.


Das Tierheim Uzunu im Kreis Giurgiu war über Jahre hinweg ein Ort des Schreckens: Hunde wurden auf den Straßen eingefangen, in der Tötungsstation unter widrigsten Bedingungen eingesperrt und grausam getötet. Die jüngsten Pathologieberichte bestätigen, was Tierschützer:innen seit Langem vermutet haben: Viele der Tiere starben durch Vergasung – ein qualvoller Tod.


Hintergrund: Aufdeckungen über massives Tierleid


Erst als die Polizei des Kreises Prahova im März 2026 eingriff, kam Bewegung in den Fall. Die Ermittlungen führten zur Entdeckung von über 105 Hundekadavern, die trotz eines Tötungsverbots im Kühlcontainer des Lagers aufbewahrt worden waren. Die anschließenden Untersuchungen der toten Hunde belegten eindeutig, dass die Tiere an schwerer Methämoglobinämie und Hypoxie starben – ein klarer Hinweis auf Vergasung.


Auf Grundlage dieser Ergebnisse ordnete die Veterinärbehörde schließlich die endgültige Schließung der Einrichtung an.


Das derzeitige massive Tierschutzproblem ist, dass an diesem Ort weiterhin rund 240 Hunde vor sich hin vegetieren und kaum versorgt werden. Nur zwei Mitarbeiter kümmern sich um die Hunde, die an diesem Ort an Krankheiten leiden, sich gegenseitig verletzten und sterben. Es gibt weder medizinische Hilfe noch Unterstützung für die Vierbeiner. Unser Partner vor Ort setzt sich für die Hunde ein und fordert von den zuständigen Behörden, dass diese dringend und sofort die Verantwortung übernehmen müssen. Die Behörden und die Polizei sind nach der offiziellen Schließung für die Hunde verantwortlich.


Tierfreundliche und nachhaltige Lösungen sind erforderlich


Einrichtungen wie Uzunu existieren, weil Gemeinden weiterhin Verträge mit kriminellen Firmen abschließen, die Hunde einfangen und töten – finanziert mit öffentlichen Geldern, ohne nachhaltige Wirkung. Die einzige wirksame Lösung gegen Überpopulation bleibt: Kastration, Aufklärung und Bildung. Seit vielen Jahren hat unser Partner ein entsprechendes Konzept, welches immer wieder Gemeinden und Behörden vorgelegt wird und mit dem Rumänien innerhalb von zehn Jahren – statistisch berechnet – nahezu keine heimatlosen Hunde mehr hätte.


Dieses Konzept fußt auf ethischen Maßnahmen und weist geringere Ausgaben auf. Es ist an der Zeit, dass dieses Konzept Beachtung findet und das „System Hund“ sich endlich zum Positiven verändert. Die Schließung von Uzunu zeigt, dass Veränderung möglich ist, wenn Behörden handeln und die Öffentlichkeit hinschaut.


Hundetötungsstation Rumänien: So arbeitet PETA weiter


Nachdem wir von PETA Deutschland uns mit einem nachdrucksvollen Brief an die zuständigen Politiker, die Polizei und die oberste Veterinärbehörde gewandt haben, ist klar: Der Fall ist noch nicht abgeschlossen. Wir werten aktuell die Antworten mit allen Informationen aus, um weiter in den Austausch mit den Behörden zu gehen. Wir erhöhen den Druck und bleiben weiter an dem Fall Uzunu dran und kämpfen für die verbleibenden Hunde und deren Versorgung.

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Animal Rights Advocates Call for Referendum on Snare Traps
content:
ANIMAL RIGHTS ADVOCATES are currently campaigning for a referendum to be held on the use of wild boar snares.

In particular, animal rights advocates have long criticized wild boar snares as overly cruel. Such traps use spring-loaded mechanisms to tighten around animals’ limbs when triggered.

Nevertheless, such traps have also been criticized for ensnaring other species, as they do not distinguish. Endangered species such as Formosan black bears and leopard cats had also been killed by such traps, as have cats and dogs, sometimes resulting in their losing limbs if they survive.

Though claims had been made that Indigenous hunters used such traps as part of traditional hunting rights, animal rights groups have generally cited that this was rarely the case, in that Indigenous hunters generally do not use such traps. By contrast, such animal rights advocates state that Indigenous hunters more commonly use traps made from wood, bamboo and vines, and other natural materials. In the past, the Central Election Commission turned down calls for a referendum on the use of wild boar snares on the basis that the referendum was unclear as to whether it pertained to traps used by Indigenous hunters.

Otherwise, such traps are sometimes used by farmers as a means of preventing damage to their crops. Animal rights advocates have called on the government to provide electric fencing, protective netting, or other means for farmers to protect their livestock and crops.

The proposals called for by animal rights advocates are relevant to the use, display, and sale of wild boar snares, as well as their import and export. It is thought that China is a major source of some of the wild boar snares used in Taiwan.

It is unclear as to whether the Central Election Commission will approve the referendum currently called for by animal rights advocates. At the same time, without a major political party endorsing it as an issue, such a referendum is unlikely to gain traction. It is to be seen if either the DPP or KMT, or perhaps even both parties, throw their weight behind the proposal.

One notes that there have been cases of political bipartisanship between both major parties on the issue of animal rights in past years, as seen with politicians of both parties supporting enshrining animal rights in the constitution. Even so, such politicians ultimately did not prove serious about such promises outside of election campaigning, as a result of which neither the KMT nor DPP acted on claims in past election cycles that animal rights would see constitutional protection.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

Chris Packham condemns the Quorn Hunt footage.


The footage lays bare the brutal reality of cub hunting – the practice of using foxes to train young hounds to hunt and kill.

Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. title: Activists Release 1,500 Mink From Idaho Farm
content:
Activists called the raid on an Idaho mink farm “liberation” for the 1,500 minks they released. But they can’t take care of themselves, said the farm’s owner, leaving many to die of heat, stress or get run over. “This is an unethical thing to do,” he said.

Intent on liberating caged animals, masked protesters broke into a family-owned mink farm in southeast Idaho, less than 80 miles west of Wyoming, and released 1,500 mink into the wild on Saturday.

Farm owner Jeff Hobbs told Cowboy State Daily that instead of freedom, the activists delivered a death sentence, leaving the animals to perish from dehydration, stress, heat or getting run over on the road.

“This is an unethical thing to do to animals,” Hobbs said. “Regardless of your value system, I haven’t quite figured out how you can claim that you’re doing something for the benefit of the animals that’s so harmful to them.”

When he spoke to Cowboy State Daily on Tuesday, Hobbs said he was still working to gather the loose minks in Franklin County. At this point, he said about 90% of the mink have been caught but still face health risks from the trauma of being temporarily released.

“This stressed them hard,” Hobbs said. “You stress animals and you run into problems. You have to do something to offset that stress so this has created a serious herd health problem.”

Hobbs said the break-in happened around 2:30 a.m. Saturday. Mink were almost immediately killed by passing cars and several more were running around the area, Hobbs said.

“Immediately we started calling out to people that we thought could assist us, and word spread in the community,” Hobbs said. “In a short time, I had almost 100 people here help them to catch animals.”

In a Saturday statement, the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office said it was investigating the incident. The department did not respond to Cowboy State Daily by publication.

On Sunday, the North American Animal Liberation Press Office posted a statement celebrating the release of the mink.

“The animals liberated this weekend have a fighting chance at life,” the statement said. “They faced a 100 percent death rate if they stayed on the farm.”

In an email to Cowboy State Daily, North American Animal Liberation press officer Jerry Vlasak disputed claims from Hobbs and the sheriff’s office that most of the mink had been recaptured.

“Almost surely did not happen,” Vlasak said. “These mink are not domesticated as the farmers claim. Scientific studies have shown them to be easily able to survive in the wild when they are released.”

Challis Hobbs, Jeff Hobbs’ son and executive director of Fur Commission USA, said in a Saturday statement that the action should be handled as a federal offense under the Animal Enterprise Terrorism Act.

“Those responsible for this attack are terrorists, plain and simple,” Challis Hobbs said.

Vlasak threw that same label back at Challis Hobbs and the Fur Commission USA.

“Those who breed, imprison and kill thousands of innocent animals every year to make a profit are the real terrorists,” Vlasak said.

Hobbs said that his fourth-generation family farm has long been the target of animal-rights organizations. In the 1990s and early 2000s, Hobbs said, authorities warned him twice that his farm ranked high on a list of likely targets and recommended he increase security.

Since then, he said, drones have flown over the property and people have driven by with cameras. Hobbs said a drone flew over the farm on Oct. 6, his father’s birthday, and was seen by a family friend who was preparing for a party.

“She didn’t realize that was a threat until after the release,” Hobbs said.

Hobbs said he understands people have different values and are entitled to be against the business of harvesting mink for fur.

“But none of us are entitled to try to press our value system on other people,” Hobbs said.

Moreover, he said the action of releasing 1,500 minks, which have no skills to survive in the wild, is antithetical to the larger goal of animal welfare.

“When people come in and do something this blatant, it’s done a lot of damage,” Hobbs said. “Animals are dying because of it.”

He also said releasing 1,500 mink, which have no skills to survive in the wild, runs counter to the larger goal of animal welfare. For Vlasak, it’s “laughable” for Hobbs, who profits from harvesting and selling mink pellets, to claim concern for the animals.

title: Data Center Near Yellowstone River Would Cause “Irreparable Harm,” Activist Says
content:
The Northern Cheyenne Tribal Council voted to ban data centers, but the Apsáalooke have yet to take a position.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Northern Cheyenne Tribal Council voted unanimously this October to ban data centers on tribal land in Montana. The ban follows a decision in August by the Fort Peck Tribes to bar officials from projects involving data center developers.

But Montana’s Tribes are now split. Next door to the Northern Cheyenne, the Apsáalooke, or Crow Tribe, has not taken an official position and remains open to hearing proposals from companies, according to Shane Doyle, an Apsáalooke tribal member and The Nature Conservancy’s Indigenous right relations director. Doyle grew up on the Crow Reservation and has consistently advocated for reciprocity with the land, rendering him a voice in the dissent, whether he intends to be or not.

The stakes are highest in Crow country. In the small city of Hardin, at the Crow Indian Reservation’s northern edge, a former cryptocurrency mine is being actively converted into an AI data center. About 14 miles northwest of the reservation, Texas-based Quantica Infrastructure plans to build its Big Sky campus on nearly eight square miles of ranchland near the town of Broadview, north of Billings, Montana’s most populous city. As it’s currently planned, the data center would rank among the largest data centers in the world. The Yellowstone River Valley is “the heart of the Crow Nation,” Doyle said.

Krystal Two Bulls, who is Oglala Lakota and Northern Cheyenne, has been tracking these data centers closely. As the executive director of Honor the Earth, a nonprofit tracking data centers on or near reservation lands, she takes an extensive view of history and geography when it comes to tribal land and AI developments.

“Broadview is still a traditional territory of the Northern Cheyenne and also the Crow,” she told Truthout. “It may not technically be on the reservation, but it definitely is still going to have an impact on the land and the people around it.”

The divide over data centers comes as developers eye Montana for its land, water, and power, and as Tribes test how far their sovereignty can actually reach. Bans like the Northern Cheyenne’s are enforceable on tribal land, said Matthew Fletcher, a University of Michigan Law professor and member of the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians. But tribal bans on off-reservation data centers that affect reservation waters are “unlikely to be enforceable,” Fletcher said, unless a tribe can show a very significant threat to its waters, enterprises, or citizens’ health.

Quantica has asked Northwestern Energy for more than 7,000 megawatts. The utility currently serves about 750 average megawatts, said Anne Hedges, executive director of the Montana Environmental Information Center. “We’ve never imagined something this massive,” she told Truthout. The company’s plan includes about 1,700 megawatts of gas generation, which alone would be more than the gas generated by all Montana’s existing gas plants combined.

The gas would affect more than just the rural Broadview community. A retired Billings pulmonologist modeled the air-quality impact of 1,700 megawatts using EPA tools, Hedges said, and found fine-particulate pollution spreading to communities east of the site, including the Crow, Northern Cheyenne, and Fort Peck reservations. “It’d be a disaster,” she said.

The Northern Cheyenne resolution, which passed by a vote of 8-0, covers all land on the reservation, says Melissa Lonebear, a Northern Cheyenne citizen and tribal council member. It quashes any extant or future data center discussions on their territory. (None are currently active.) “We have fought historically to preserve our land,” says Lonebear. “We have fought against coal development, coal bed methane, all these things.”

The Northern Cheyenne own nearly all of the land within their reservation, which makes the Tribe a target for developers looking for large, contiguous sites, Lonebear said. She added that the governor had remarked in a closed meeting with tribal leaders that big corporations were looking for land. “I almost felt like we would be targeted,” she said.

Fort Peck’s ban bars the tribal government, individuals, and entities from discussing proposals to build data centers on the tribe’s reservation. The tribe passed the ban after three companies …

author: ROAPE
title: Mining in contemporary African underdevelopment
content:
One of the defining characteristics of capitalism is its remarkable ability to emerge from every crisis even stronger.[1] History has shown time and again that war and militarisation serve capitalism’s interests. And even in the case of the climate crisis – for which capitalism bears the greatest responsibility – we are presented with an alleged ‘win–win’ solution. While multinational companies at least partly withdraw from coal mining (see Tsuji et al. 2026, in this issue), the massive rise in

demand for metals and minerals

 that are needed for ‘clean energy’, digitalisation, consumer electronics, aerospace and militarisation has led to a renewed mining boom, notably of so-called critical raw materials (UNCTAD 2026). In a business-as-usual scenario, demand for these materials between 2024 and 2040 is projected to increase by 353% in the case of lithium, 131% for graphite, 69% for nickel and 49% for cobalt (UNCTAD 2026, 3).


Many of the deposits of these raw materials are located in the global South, with the African continent accounting for about 30% of the world’s critical minerals and metals: for example, 85% of global deposits of manganese (in South Africa and Gabon) and 21% of graphite reserves (in Mozambique, Madagascar and Tanzania). Guinea alone holds one-quarter of global bauxite reserves. South Africa is one of the world’s leading producers of chromium and platinum, while the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is the second-largest producer of copper, with a 13% share of global supply in 2024 (after Chile with 24%). Around 70% of the global supply of cobalt is extracted in the DRC (Boafo et al. 2024; IEA 2025; Cobalt Institute 2026; US Geological Survey 2026).


Lithium has become the epitome of the metal needed for energy transition: it ‘embodies the fantasy of a “technological fix”, capable of turning the climate crisis into a political and economic opportunity for those in power’ (Voskoboynik and Andreucci 2022, 803). Critical research, political debate and activism has focused on the catastrophic impacts of the expansion of mining in the ‘Lithium Triangle’ (Chile, Argentina and Bolivia) that holds the largest part of global lithium reserves (Ahmad 2020; Ciftci and Lemaire 2023; Mejia-Muñoz and Babidge 2023). Yet, less attention has been paid to Zimbabwe, for instance, which holds the world’s fifth- or sixth-largest lithium deposits, accounting for almost 10% of current global production (Manduna 2026b, 4; OECD 2026, 6); or to Mali, which has 700,000 tons of lithium reserves (Chandler 2022, 2). Possibly one of the largest undeveloped hard-rock lithium deposits lies in southern DRC: an exploration licence for the Manono Lithium Project was granted in 2023 to Manono Lithium SAS, a joint venture of Chinese company Zijin Mining and Congolese state-owned Société commerciale et Minière du Congo, whereby Zijin holds a 54.9% majority (Zijin n.d.).


Remarkably, Europe’s largest lithium deposits are located in Ukraine. Ukraine is estimated to hold around 5% of the world’s strategic raw material reserves, including reserves of lithium, graphite, titanium and rare earths. Half of these reserves are in territories currently under Russian control (Baranowski, Jabkowski and Kammen 2025; Crescenzi 2026). Multinational companies are interested in the other half: for example, Irish company TechMet Ltd, in a joint venture with Ronald Lauder (heir to Estée Lauder Companies and a personal friend of Donald Trump), was awarded the concession to exploit the Dobra lithium reserve deposit in Kirovohrad by the Ukrainian government in January 2026 (Barba 2025; Méheut 2026). Here, too, geopolitical competition for the decarbonisation markets turns out to be a driving force of the war.


‘Critical’ minerals, however, are critical first and foremost for the global North, not for local and national demand and supply on the African continent itself. Very few African countries process and use minerals and metals for low-carbon technologies. This is hardly surprising, given that African states have fewer industries and consequently contribute far less to global greenhouse gas emissions. The G20 states are responsible for almost 83% of global greenhouse gas emissions, notably the EU, the USA, China and India (or, based on per capita emissions, Saudi Arabia, Canada and Australia) (EDGAR 2025).


Resource nationalism on the rise?

author: Harriet Williamson
title: The Weather Outside Is Frightful. So Is Labour’s Climate Forecast
content:
If you only had to nail down your wheelie bin to stop it blowing across the street this weekend, you were lucky. 


Three days of back-to-back storms – Austen on Friday, followed immediately by Boelo –

caused flooding

, power cuts for

almost 83,000 households

 and

travel chaos

 across swathes of the UK. Winds of over 80mph were recorded, roads were blocked and flood waters surged in

apocalyptic scenes

. Two men

were

killed by falling trees

. 


After a summer of

extreme temperatures

, drought and

a food production crisis

, with more than

 2,800 excess deaths

 due to consecutive heatwaves in May and June alone, you’d think the government might be taking a more muscular approach to the climate emergency.


But just days before the UK was plunged into killer-storm territory, Andy Burnham’s government approved new North Sea drilling in the form of the Jackdaw gas field. 


The Cortado


          Get your shot of political analysis from

Ash Sarkar

 and

Steven Methven

, every Monday and Friday morning.


First name:


Email:


I agree to the

Privacy Policy


      Sign up error:

. Try again later.


      Thanks for signing up.


Climate experts are clear:

no new oil and gas fields

are compatible with keeping global heating around the 1.5°C mark. Jackdaw and the as-yet-unapproved Rosebank oil field, the two new North Sea projects previously

halted in the courts

over their climate impact, are not an exception. 


Perhaps more immediately painful as the weather turns (and I sit cradling a hot water bottle like my firstborn child) is the knowledge that gas from Jackdaw will do sweet FA to bring down energy bills at home,

according to most analysts

. However, it

is

 a big win for owner and operator Adura, a joint venture between fossil fuel giant Shell and Norwegian firm Equinox, so I guess we can all be pleased for their shareholders. 


And congratulations might be in order for the climate-wreckers once again, with Whitehall

‘sources’ briefing

on Saturday night that Burnham and chancellor John Healey are set to “defy eco-zealot Ed Miliband” and approve Rosebank, despite energy secretary

Miatta Fahnbulleh insisting

 she’s the only one who can make the final decision. 


Rosebank is far bigger and will be

significantly more damaging

 than Jackdaw, with predicted lifetime emissions of over 200 million tonnes of CO2 (

equivalent to nearly 70%

of the UK’s total emissions last year). 


If approved, Rosebank’s oil will be sold on the international market for the benefit of its owners, which include a 20% stake for Ithaca Energy (and Ithaca’s majority shareholder, the

illegal West Bank settlement-facilitating

 Israeli oil and gas firm Delek). If the UK government goes ahead with Rosebank, it could be in breach of the Geneva Conventions – something that should give major pause to an administration

banning trade

 with illegal Israeli settlements. 


But there’s more incoherence from Burnham’s lot at play here. On one hand, the government is urging us to stockpile tins and buy windup radios,

 citing severe weather

, and then on the other, ignoring the science in favour of

“taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea”

, which seems to mean little more than capitulating to fossil fuel giants with delusory benefits for the British public. 


While the government waited until after its

Holborn and St Pancras byelection win

against Zack Polanski to announce Jackdaw’s approval, Labour may now be feeling diminishing pressure from the embattled party to its left. The Greens, for which climate should be a slam-dunk issue, are sinking into a polling black hole while Labour rides high with

 32% and an eight-point lead,

according to Ipsos. Labour peer Harriet Harman certainly felt unembarrassed to tout the

“green argument for Rosebank”

 on Friday – an equivalent to the turkey’s argument to play a central role in Christmas dinner. 


Jackdaw was the smaller fish, and approving it might’ve been a compromise to soothe the more vociferously climate-denying elements of our political and media class, allowing Rosebank to be rejected as a ‘climate red line’ with less pushback. But what’s the point in speculating? Too much of Westminster analysis is a glorified game of ‘guess what’s in teacher’s head’. Burnham’s first budget is looming on Wednesday, and we can soon judge the government by what it

does

author: winter oak
title: A message from dreamland
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


I had a couple of vivid and, I think, significant dreams the other night.


In the first of these my (deceased) parents turned up at my home bearing ancient suitcases and chests apparently full of my possessions. They looked very familiar and it seemed as if I knew what was inside each of them.


I felt I had to accept these items, even though I did not really have the free space – I managed to stuff one of them under my bed. I was left with the impression of being encumbered and cluttered, overwhelmed with

stuff

.


On awakening, my first reaction was that this was about the inter-generational mental baggage that is handed down to us all by our families.


I thought of a remark someone had made to me about the danger that the attitudes of our ancestors – a subject I had just

written about

 – might actually represent a

barrier

 to our direct individual connection to the Whole.


It was far too early to get up and so I went through a mental exercise of opening up each of these old suitcases in turn, sifting through the contents to check that there was nothing of importance, and then throwing everything into a skip outside.


Having achieved this to my satisfaction, I realised that there was probably a lot more in my own head that was responsible for this sensation of being cluttered and blocked.


I thought of what Malidoma Patrice Somé said, as cited in the aforementioned article, about his Western education preventing him from fully accessing traditional shamanic knowledge and I had to admit to myself how much my mind was full of incoming

information

,

news

 and

detail

.


When I slipped back into dreamland I found myself looking at a terrible landscape. It was the countryside – with no buildings in sight – but a

devastated, unrecognisable countryside

.


It had lost all aesthetic charm and was even

ugly

. Tree stumps were everywhere around. The distant hills were planted with row upon straight row of commercially lucrative pines and even the stunted and hacked-about oaks nearby were in a mechanical line stretching away from me, rather than in an organic copse.


I was surprised by a terrible roaring sound to my left and turned to see flames bursting up into the sky behind some other trees. Alongside, I noticed a drilling rig and other unidentifiable industrial structures.


A small girl-child had materialised in my arms and, as we looked out at this hideous scene, I said to her: “Oh my god, they really want to do this to us!”


I knew at this point that the people behind this desecration of nature did not so much

not care

 about the harm they were causing in their own self-interest, but that they actually took a

demonic delight

 in destroying all that is good and beautiful, all that means most to

us

.


A small boy was now holding my hand, as well, and I said to the little ones: “We’ve got to stop them!”. Suddenly aware that it seemed a bit too late for that, I added: “We have to go back in time and do everything we can. With love in our hearts!”


We stepped through the portal and I woke up in 2026. I am getting on a bit now, but those children have their whole lives ahead of them.

author: Unknown
title: Duvara tutturulmak ya da duvarın içinde kalmak
content:
Bir bedene yer açmak ile onu bir mekana yerleştirmek aynı şey midir? Görünür olmak, hareket edebilmek anlamına gelir mi? Dilan Cudi Saruhan’ın

Beden

 adlı yerleştirmesiyle Maurizio Cattelan’ın

A Perfect Day

’i, bu soruları duvarın önünde yeniden kurar. Birinde canlı beden dışarıdan sabitlenir; diğerinde beden imgesi, kendisini kuşatan yüzeyle aynı maddede oluşur. Duvar her iki yapıtta da varlığın yerini belirler. Fakat o yerin içinde nasıl kalındığı değişir.


Şeritlerin merkezde yoğunlaşıp çevreye yayılması, iki çalışma arasında çarpıcı bir görsel yakınlık yaratır. Bu benzerlik, doğrudan etkilenmenin kanıtı değildir. Karşılaştırmayı verimli kılan, benzer düzenlerin farklı toplumsal deneyimler içinde ürettiği ayrımdır: bedenin hareketini durdurmak ile sınırı bedenin içine yerleştirmek arasındaki ayrım.


Saruhan’ın figürü cenin formunda kendi üzerine kapanmıştır. Başı gövdesine yaklaşır, uzuvları merkezde toplanır; beden, dışarıya açılmak yerine kendi içine çekilir. Bu duruşu yalnızca sıkışmanın sonucu saymak, figürün kendini koruma hareketini gözden kaçırır. Ancak korunmanın daralarak mümkün oluşu da başlı başına bir sorudur. Beden burada hem sığınak hem sığınılandır.


Kuşatan ile kuşatılan


Beden’de oluklu karton şeritler merkezde düğümlenerek hacim kazanır, kenarlarda uzayıp seyrelir. Figürün çevresini izlerken bir noktadan sonra bedeni mi, onu içine alan dokuyu mu gördüğümüz belirsizleşir. Çünkü kuşatan ile kuşatılan aynı maddeden yapılmıştır. Karton, figürün çevresindeki engel olduğu kadar onun varlık koşuludur. Sınırı kaldırdığımızda altında özgürleşmeyi bekleyen, önceden tamamlanmış bir beden bulacağımızdan emin olamayız.


Cenin formu bu maddesel ortaklığı daha da yoğunlaştırır. Başın eğilmesi, gövdenin kıvrılması ve uzuvların içe çekilmesi, bedeni kendi sınırları içinde yeniden toplar. Anne rahmini çağrıştıran bu biçimde korunma ile kuşatılma birbirine yaklaşır. Yine de burada güvenli bir başlangıca dönüşten söz etmek güçtür. Figür, onu taşıyan dokunun içinde saklanırken aynı dokunun baskısını da taşır. Bir sığınağın ne zaman kapatılma mekânına dönüştüğünü, formun içinden sorar.


Cattelan’ın 1999 tarihli

A Perfect Day

’inde ise galerici Massimo De Carlo, yapışkan bantlarla kendi galerisinin duvarına sabitlenmiştir. Yüzü, giysisi ve ayakkabıları, kuşatmanın içindeki kişinin kimliğini görünür tutar. Düşey gövde ayakta durma hâlini anımsatır; fakat ayaklar yere değmez. Bedenin ağırlığını taşıma işi zeminden bantlara aktarılmıştır. Başın yana düşüşü, bu duruşun kişinin kendi dengesiyle sürdürülemediğini açığa çıkarır (MASSIMODECARLO, 1999; Phillips, t.y.).


Maurizio Cattelan, A Perfect Day, 1999. Massimo De Carlo’nun yapışkan bantlarla galeri duvarına sabitlendiği eylemin fotoğrafik belgesi. Görsel kaynağı: Phillips, yapıt kaydı, lot 23.


Duruşun izleyicide bıraktığı iz


Cattelan’ın bedeni dışarıdan tutulur; Saruhan’ın bedeni kendi üzerine kapanır. Birinde düşeyliğin dayanağı alınmış, diğerinde bedenin kapladığı alan daralmıştır. Bu ayrım, bakışın yönünü de değiştirir. De Carlo’nun açıkta kalan yüzü bizi belirli bir kişiye götürürken Saruhan’ın yüzü dokunun içinde geri çekilir. Karşılaştığımız, portresinden tanıyabileceğimiz bir kişi kadar, duruşunu kendi bedenimizde yoklayabileceğimiz bir varlık hâlidir.


Görmek, burada bedenden bağımsız bir etkinlik değildir. Merleau-Ponty’nin bedensel algı yaklaşımıyla düşünüldüğünde, izleyici gördüğü duruşu kendi hareket olanakları içinden kavrar (Merleau-Ponty, 2012). Cattelan’ın karşısında kendi ayaklarının yere bastığını fark edebilir; Saruhan’ın figürüne bakarken dizlerini kendine çekmeyi, başını eğmeyi, omuzlarını daraltmayı hatırlayabilir. Cenin formunun tanıdıklığı, bu yakınlığı güçlendirir. Bununla birlikte tanıdıklık, bütün izleyicilerin aynı duyguyu yaşayacağı anlamına gelmez.


Saruhan’ın kapanan bedeninde özdeşlik, yüz benzerliğinden önce bir korunma jesti üzerinden kurulabilir. Kendi kırılganlığımızı o kıvrımın içinde düşünürüz. Fakat “Ben de böyle kıvrılabilirim” demek ile “Ben de aynı kapatılmayı yaşadım” demek arasında aşılması kolay olmayan bir mesafe vardır. Yakınlık, başkasının tarihini kendimize mal etme hakkı vermez. Bakışın sorumluluğu, bu mesafeyi koruyarak yaklaşabilmektir.


Görsel 3. Dilan Cudi Saruhan, Beden, 2026. Oluklu karton ve sünger. 


Yandan bakışta figür duvardan öne çıkar; karşıdan bakışta dokunun içine çekilir. Bakış yer değiştirdikçe beden de görünürlük kazanır ya da kaybolmaya yaklaşır. Duvarın içinde kalmak, burada …

author: Zeit Online
title: Warum die Deutschen nicht ausrasten?
content:
Während in Frankreich Barrikaden brennen, bleibt es hierzulande ziemlich ruhig. Geht’s den Deutschen so viel besser? Nein, sie sind nur die Summe ihrer Ängste.


Verschwitzte Gesichter hinter Sturmhauben, ein Rathaus, das lichterloh in Flammen steht, Ascheberge am Straßenrand. Die Bilder der Ausschreitungen in Frankreich, die in diesen Tagen zu uns herüberschwappen, können bei deutschen Betrachtern für gemischte Gefühle sorgen. Im ersten Moment kann man erschrecken; die Franzosen, meine Güte! Oder aber man macht einen Schritt zur Seite. Und fragt: Warum blieben wir in Deutschland von solchen Ausschreitungen bislang verschont? Warum rasten die Deutschen nicht aus, wie Menschen in anderen Ländern der Welt, zumindest nicht in diesen Massen? Und das, obwohl radikale Einstellungen auch hierzulande zunehmen?


Beobachtet man die Protestkultur in Deutschland in den vergangenen Jahren, kann man sich fühlen wie in einer düsteren Variante von Samuel Becketts Warten auf Godot. Man spürt, da baut sich etwas auf, der Unmut, so erwartet man, muss bald eskalieren, das Aufbegehren steht vor der Tür. Und alle fürchten es schon. Doch dann? Bleibt es aus.


So war es, als die Gelbwesten in Frankreich durch die Straßen zogen und die Zeitungen ein baldiges deutsches Pendant prophezeiten. So war es, als die Klimaaktivisten ihre Hände auf die Autobahn klebten; CSU-Politiker Alexander Dobrindt sah damals gar die Entstehung einer »Klima-RAF« voraus. Und auch auf die Pegida-Demonstrationen und die Bauernproteste schaute die Öffentlichkeit voller Angst vor flächendeckender Eskalation. Nur kam diese nie. In Deutschland gibt es den Zorn der Masse. Aber er kocht selten über.


Bevor sich jetzt jemand wütend in die Kommentarspalte verabschiedet: Ja, auch hierzulande kommt es zu Gewalt bei Protesten. Linksradikale schmissen in den vergangenen Jahren Steine auf Polizisten, Rechtsradikale griffen Gegendemonstranten an, Corona-Demonstrierende kletterten über das Gitter zum Reichstag, Pro-Palästina-Demos endeten mit Verhaftungen. Aber im Vergleich zu Frankreich etwa rasteten die Deutschen zuletzt selten richtig aus, zumindest nicht in Gestalt einer gewaltbereiten Masse, die landesweit durch die Straßen zieht, öffentliche Gebäude in Brand steckt und Läden plündert.


Das vielleicht bekannteste Beispiel für gewaltsame Ausschreitungen bei Demonstrationen der letzten Jahre sind die linksradikalen Proteste rund um den G20-Gipfel 2017. Aber auch diese blieben auf einen Ort und den Anlass beschränkt. Und es war kein allein deutscher Protest, er war international. Aus ganz Europa reisten Demonstrierende an, um ihrer Wut Ausdruck zu verleihen.


Was also passiert mit der deutschen Wut auf der Straße? Unmut gibt es hier schließlich auch. Die AfD macht längst mit der mangelhaften Infrastruktur, der übertriebenen Bürokratie, dem Aussterben von Kleinstädten und der Verelendung von Großstädten Politik.


Wenn man in die Zahlen schaut, gibt es viele der Probleme, die in Frankreich beklagt werden, auch hier: Der Anteil derer, die armutsgefährdet sind, liegt hier wie dort bei 16 Prozent. Die Preise für die Verbraucher sind in beiden Ländern um ziemlich genau drei Prozent gestiegen. Die hohen Mieten sind in Deutschland sogar ein größeres Problem als in Frankreich. Beim letzten Pisa-Test schnitt Deutschland so schlecht ab wie noch nie. Die Jugendarbeitslosigkeit ist in Frankreich zwar deutlich höher, aber auch hierzulande haben Jugendliche, was ihre Zukunftsaussichten angeht, allen Grund, die Fassung zu verlieren. Steht uns der Kipppunkt also vielleicht doch nur noch bevor?


Telefoniert man Protestforscher im Land ab, rechnet keiner von ihnen damit, dass Ausschreitungen, wie wir sie in Frankreich sehen, in nächster Zeit bei uns drohen könnten. Strukturelle Gründe werden da genannt. Die Tatsache, dass hierzulande Gewerkschaften regelmäßig mit Unternehmern am Tisch sitzen und Kompromisse aushandeln, bevor alles eskaliert. In Frankreich gehe die Polizei viel härter gegen Demonstrierende vor, auch das befördere die Eskalation eher, als dass es sie verhindere. Der vielleicht größte strukturelle Unterschied ist, dass es in Deutschland keine Zentralregierung gibt, die von oben alles entscheidet und auf die sich die geballte Wut einer ganzen Bewegung entladen kann. Im föderalen System bleibt der Protest eher lokal, statt sich im Land auszubreiten.


Oft erstickt die Wut aber auch in der Frustration. Der Protestforscher Simon Teune von der FU Berlin sagt: »Die Deutschen haben …

title: Zahl seit 2008 in 2019 verdoppelt: Mehr Krankheitstage durch Hitze und Sonne – und Tote, weltweit
content:
Dossier


„

Die Zahl der Krankheitstage durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht hat sich im Zeitraum von 2008 bis 2017 verdoppelt. Zudem werden mittlerweile jährlich Tausende Fälle von Hautkrebs als Berufskrankheit anerkannt. Hitzschlag, Sonnenstich, Krämpfe, Ödeme, Probleme durch Salz- und Wasserverlust – das sind einige der Gesundheitsschäden, die durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht ausgelöst werden können. Wie aus Angaben der Bundesregierung auf eine Anfrage der Linksfraktion hervorgeht, gab es 2017 etwa 40.000 Arbeitsunfähigkeitstage „auf Grund von Schäden durch Hitze und Sonnenlicht“. (…) Derzeit herrschen aber auch in Deutschland große Hitze und hohe UV-Strahlung. Ärztepräsident Klaus Reinhardt forderte Hitzepausen. (…) Die Industriegewerkschaft BAU beklagt, es gebe zwar Regelungen, diese würden aber von zahlreichen Bauunternehmern gebrochen

…“

Beitrag von Patrick Gensing und Wulf Rohwedder vom 23.07.2019 bei tagesschau.de

Grundinfos

An der Hitze in Europa starben im Sommer 50.000 Menschen. Eine britische Analyse zeigt: Die Folgen des menschengemachten Klimawandels werden deutlicher

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Displaced Marawi survivors still long for justice
content:
Marawi displaced survivor Baiminang Madale speaking in the opening of Alongan sa Marawi exhibit. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

More than nine years have passed since the Philippine government declared the “liberation” of Marawi City after the siege that displaced more than 300,000 families. Some of them are now living in different parts of the country, uncertain if they could return.

“We were already familiar with the term bakwit (evacuee/displacement). But the Marawi Siege was different. Before, our bakwit would only last for three days. This time, it feels as though we have been permanently driven out of Marawi,” Baiminang Madale, a displaced Maranao survivor living in Manila, said in the vernacular during the opening of Alongan sa Marawi (One Day in Marawi) exhibit.

The exhibit runs until November 15, 2026, at the Rift Gallery Edsa. It is organized by researchers, journalists, survivors, and advocates to commemorate the ninth year of the city’s so-called liberation. It seeks to provide a visual experience of Marawi from the survivors’ perspective.

“The Maranao, like other tribes and communities, have our own culture, dreams, and lives. Because of the Marawi Siege, we feel as though we have not simply been stripped naked, but forcibly stripped out of our homes that shape our identity,” Madale said. “Marawi is the very heart of the Maranao people. Imagine suddenly losing everything—it is far worse than a nightmare. We never thought something like this could happen to us.”

The Philippine government declared October 17 as Marawi Liberation Day starting in 2017 to mark what it called as a “military victory” against the Islamic State-linked Maute group after a five-month battle.

Madale, who is also part of the board of Ako Bakwit, a group working for the welfare and rights of internally displaced peoples (IDPs), said that there are many more families like hers forced to live in Manila since the siege.

Earlier this year, Bulatlat reported that the displaced families have yet to return to their homes in Marawi. Around 17,000 families or 80,000 individuals are still living in 15 temporary shelters in Marawi and Lanao del Sur, according to Marawi Advocacy Accompaniment.

Read: After 9 years, Marawi displaced families have yet to return to their homes

Under the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act of 2022, any owner of a residential, cultural, or commercial structure, and other properties in Marawi’s 24 MAA and eight barangays considered as other affected areas (OAA) is entitled to monetary compensation subject to verification.

Compensation claims, under the law, shall be filed within one year from the date of commencement of the filing (July 4, 2023) to the date of its termination (July 3, 2024).

Read: Group opposes Marawi Siege compensation planned changes

Data from the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB), the government body that awards monetary compensation to eligible claimants, showed that 3,699 claims were resolved from 2023 to June 30, 2026, amounting to P6.154 billion. This is 25.51 percent of the estimated 14,497 total claims to be resolved by the body by 2028.

Mindanao State University Prof. Sorhalia Latip-Yusoph said that the recovery and return process for the survivors are hurdled by a tedious bureaucratic process.

“The government’s requirements for returning are extremely difficult to meet. Sometimes, we do not understand why the process has to be so difficult. Perhaps they want to be strict,” Latip-Yusoph said. “Our fellow Maranaos (in bakwit) are truly the ones who, if we may put it this way, are the reason our hearts continue to ache. Many of them are still living elsewhere. I hope we will not reach the tenth year without being able to return home.”

Task Force Bangon Marawi was a government inter-agency task force group established by former President Rodrigo Duterte in June 2017 to facilitate rehabilitation, recovery, and reconstruction.

However, Madale said that the four stages of the task force’s process did not align with the needs of the IDPs and survivors of the Marawi siege. The process includes registration, mapping, submission of documents, and biometrics. However, most IDPs lack valid identification and their house/land ownership documents– most of the time– are not recognized by the government implementers.

“The process is inhumane. Even application to the Marawi Compensation Board (MCB) is difficult. They even prioritize illegal claimants,” Madale said. “I hope our government …

title: CABA: Contrafestejo del 12 de octubre
content:
El 12 de octubre, las calles de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires volvieron a ser escenario del contrafestejo, una jornada de lucha y memoria frente a la celebración de la conquista de América. Durante la movilización que partió desde el Congreso, la Policía de la Ciudad intentó impedir que las y los manifestantes marcharan por la calle. Sin embargo, no logró detener la columna, que resistió la imposición policial y sostuvo su derecho a ocupar la calle.
