Мак-Кинли, глава североамериканской олигархии, орудие и защитник крупных капиталистов, предатель кубинцев и филиппинцев, человек, санкционировавший расправу над бастующими в Хэзлтоне, пытки шахтёров Айдахо и тысячу гнусностей, ежедневно совершаемых против рабочих в «образцовой республике», тот, кто воплощал милитаристскую, завоевательную, империалистическую политику, в которую ринулась американская буржуазия, пал жертвой револьвера анархиста.

О чём вы хотите, чтобы мы скорбели, если не о судьбе, уготованной великодушному человеку, который – уместно или неуместно, с хорошей или плохой тактикой – принёс себя в жертву делу равенства и свободы?

Повторим это и в данном случае, как и во всех аналогичных: поскольку мы находимся в обществе волков, где насилие окружает нас и разит со всех сторон, мы, продолжая спокойно бороться за то, чтобы прекратилась эта ужасная необходимость отвечать на насилие насилием, – хотя и желая, чтобы скорее наступил день, когда антагонизмы интересов и страстей между людьми можно будет разрешать человеческими и цивилизованными средствами, – бережём свои слёзы и свои цветы для других жертв, а не для этих людей, которые, становясь во главе эксплуататорских и угнетательских классов, берут на себя ответственность и идут на риск, связанный с их положением.

И всё же нашлись анархисты, которые сочли полезным и прекрасным оскорблять угнетённого, который восстаёт, не имея ни слова осуждения для угнетателя, понёсшего кару за преступления, которые он совершил или позволил совершить!

Это извращение, это нездоровое желание получить одобрение противников, или же неосмотрительная ловкость, которая хотела бы завоевать свободу пропаганды своих идей, добровольно отказываясь от права выражать истинное и глубокое чувство души, – более того, искажая это чувство, притворяясь не тем, что есть?

Я делаю это с сожалением, но не могу не выразить боль и возмущение, которые вызвали во мне и во всех товарищах, каких мне довелось видеть в эти дни, необдуманные слова, посвящённые Agitazione покушению в Буффало.

Чолгош – несознательный человек! Но знают ли они его? Его поступок – обычное преступление, не имеющее ни одного из признаков, необходимых для того, чтобы подобный акт мог считаться политическим!

Полагаю, что ни один государственный обвинитель – королевский или республиканский – не осмелился бы утверждать нечто подобное. В самом деле, есть ли хоть какой-нибудь повод судить о Чолгоше как о человеке, движимом личными интересами или личной злобой? Разве не ясно, что он действовал по мотивам общественного порядка и намеревался – с основанием или без основания, но, несомненно, искренне и самоотверженно – принести себя в жертву ради дела? И разве не эти элементы придают факту наиболее яркий характер политико-социального покушения?

Впрочем, неправильно говорить о преступлении в подобных случаях. Кодекс это делает, но кодекс создан против нас, против угнетённых, и не может служить критерием для наших суждений.

Эти факты – акты войны; и если война есть преступление, то она преступление для тех, кто в ней стоит на стороне несправедливости и угнетения. Преступниками могут быть, являются английские захватчики Трансвааля; ими не являются буры, когда защищают свою свободу, даже если защита была бы безнадёжной.

Поступок Чолгоша (могла бы ответить Agitazione) нисколько не продвинул дело пролетариата и революции: Вместо Мак-Кинли придет Рузвельт, такой же, как и он, и всё останется как прежде, разве что положение анархистов станет немного труднее. И, возможно, Agitazione была бы права; более того, в американской среде, насколько я её знаю, мне это кажется вероятным.

Это значит, что на войне есть ходы удачные и ошибочные, есть бойцы осмотрительные и есть те, кто …

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

author: Unknown
title: Walter Benjamin - The Moon
content:
Author

: Walter Benjamin

Title

: The Moon

Source

:

Berlin Childhood around 1900


 The light streaming down from the moon has no part in the theater of our daily existence. The terrain it illuminates so equivocally seems to belong to some counterearth or alternate earth. It is an earth different from that to which the moon is subject as satellite, for it is itself transformed into a satellite of the moon. Its broad bosom, whose breath was time, stirs no longer; the creation has finally made its way back home, and can again don the widow’s veil which the day had torn off. The pale beam that stole into my room through the blinds gave me to understand this. The course of my sleep was disturbed; the moon cut through it with its coming and going. When it was there in the room and I awoke, I was effectively unhoused, for my room seemed willing to accommodate no one besides the moon.


 The first things that attracted my gaze were the two cream-colored basins on the washstand. By day, it never entered my head to dwell on them. In the moonlight, however, the band of blue that ran around the upper part of the basins was a provocation. It simulated a woven band encircling a skirt-hem. And in fact the brim of each basin was curled like a frill. Between the two basins stood pot-bellied jugs, made of the same porcelain with the same floral pattern. When I climbed out of bed, they clinked, and this elinking was communicated over the washstand’s marble surface to basins and bowls, glasses and carafes. As happy as I was to receive from my nocturnal surroundings a sign of life—be it only the echo of my own—it was nonetheless an unreliable sign, and was waiting, like a false friend, to dupe me at the very moment I least expected it. This was when I lifted the carafe with my hand to pour some water into a glass. The gurgling of the water, the noise with which I put down first the carafe and then the glass—it all struck my ear as repetition. For every spot on this alternate earth to which I was transported appeared wholly occupied by what once had been. Thus, each sound and each moment came toward me as the double of itself. And when I had endured this for a while, I would draw near my bed gripped by the fear of finding myself already stretched out upon it.


 This anxiety did not altogether subside until I once again felt the mattress under my back. Then I fell asleep. The moonlight withdrew slowly from my room. And, often, the room already lay in darkness when I awoke for a second or third time. My hand would necessarily be the first to brave emergence from the trench of sleep, in which it had taken cover before the dream. And just as one sometimes falls prey to a previously unexploded shell even after a battle has ended, so my hand was constantly expecting to be overtaken on its way by a previously delayed dream. When the nightlight, flickering, then brought peace to my hand and me, it appeared that nothing more remained of the world than a single, stubborn question. It may be that this question nested in the folds of the door-curtain that shielded me from noise. It may be that it was nothing but a residue of many past nights. Or, finally, it may be that it was the other side of the feeling of strangeness which the moon had brought on. The question was: Why is there anything at all in the world, why the world? With amazement, I realized that nothing in it could compel me to think the world. Its nonbeing would have struck me as not a whit more problematic than its being, which seemed to wink at nonbeing. The moon had an easy time with this being.“


 My childhood was already nearing its end when, at last, the moon seemed willing to assert its claim to the earth by daylight, a claim which previously it had made only at night.85 High above the horizon-—large, but pale-— it stood, in the sky of a dream, looking down on the streets of Berlin. It was still light outside. Gathered around me were the members of my family, their bearing a little stiff, like that of figures in a daguerreotype. Only my sister was missing. “Where is Dora?”I heard my mother exclaim. Suddenly, the full moon up in the sky began ever more rapidly to expand- Coming nearer and nearer, it tore the planet asunder. The railing of the iron balcony, on which we all had taken our places overlooking the street, broke into a thousand pieces, and the bodies which had been there flew apart in all directions. The funnel created by the moon’s approach sucked everything in …

author: Unknown
title: Seventh denial of release for Nedime Yaklav
content:
In the fourth week of its ongoing protests against the blocking of women prisoners’ releases at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, the Ankara Democratic Institutions Platform made a statement in front of the Ministry of Justice. The protest highlighted the seventh denial of release for Nedime Yaklav, who has been imprisoned for 34 years.


Speaking on behalf of the platform, Nesil Çifçi stated that although there were insufficient social and sporting activities available in the prison, Nedime Yaklav’s failure to participate in these activities had been cited as grounds for denying her release. “Postponing prisoners’ freedom on the basis of facilities that the institution itself fails to provide is not justice; it is oppression,” she said.


Nesil Çifçi stated that, according to data from the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), the release of 90 prisoners had been blocked over the past three months. She called for an end to the arbitrary obstruction of prisoners who have become eligible for release and demanded that sentence enforcement practices be revised in accordance with human rights principles.


Mehmet Sıddık Akın, Co-Chair of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), also drew attention to violations of the right to health in prisons. He called for the release of seriously ill prisoners, for reports from independent healthcare institutions to be taken into account, and for degrading searches to be brought to an end.

Ein Film, der die Unterschiede zwischen der breit gefächerten linken Bewegung im Spanien der 30er Jahre und den Kräften der Reaktion sehr deutlich macht.

title: Bakırhan: 'Peace and Politicisation Council’ must be established immediately
content:
With Abdullah Öcalan’s “Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, the process entered a new phase. The Kurdish Freedom Movement announced its decision to dissolve itself, burned its weapons and withdrew its forces. However, the state’s delays in taking legal and political steps in response to these moves have increased questions and concerns about the future of the process.


Speaking to ANF, DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan said that trust must be established for the process to move forward and called on the government to take concrete steps. He stressed that the verification and assessment report must be published without delay, that the National Security Council (MGK) must adopt a decision, and that implementation of the Framework Law must begin. “Now it is the government’s turn,” he said.


At last week’s parliamentary group meeting, you pointed out that the government was ‘coming up with a new condition every week and a new pretext every month’. Why is the government dragging its feet? What arguments is it putting forward at the moment?


The way to build trust and establish a future through the “Peace and Democratic Society Process” is for both sides to take reciprocal steps. From Mr Öcalan’s call to the statement issued by the Movement’s Leadership on 8 October, very important steps have been taken since the process began. In response, significant steps were also taken, including the establishment of a parliamentary commission and a parliamentary delegation’s visit to İmralı. However, there has been a wait-and-see approach when it comes to taking the steps needed to advance these developments, provide the process with legal guarantees, and ensure Mr Öcalan has the freedom to work and communicate.


This delay is continually justified with various pretexts. That is why we sought to draw public attention to this inaction and the failure to fulfil the necessary responsibilities. The government must respond to each step with a corresponding step. The process should proceed through a “staircase” approach, with each successive stage being crossed through reciprocal steps.


When is the ‘verification and assessment report’ expected to be released?


In my view, there is no longer any reason to wait for the report. Look, the Movement’s Leadership has taken important steps. First, the weapons were burned, followed by the decision to dissolve the organisation. Now they have also evacuated the Metîna Camp, which they had regarded for years as one of their most strategic positions, along with other important bases, and withdrawn their forces from Turkey. No one should underestimate this. When an armed movement voluntarily abandons its own positions, it is the clearest possible way of saying, “We stand by our decision; there is no turning back.”


Now it is the government’s turn. The verification and assessment report must be published without delay, the MGK must adopt its decision, and implementation of the Framework Law must begin. If one side continues taking steps while the other keeps waiting, trust will erode. And trust is what this process needs most.


I want to emphasise one point in particular. It is Mr Öcalan who can accelerate this process and bring it to a conclusion. I am not saying this merely as a hope; I am saying it based on what has happened so far. At every critical juncture, it was his calls that opened the way forward. That is why a “Peace and Politicisation Council” must be established immediately under Mr Öcalan’s coordination. There is no requirement for this to be conditional on the verification and assessment process or on legislation. Let the council be established and meet with Mr Öcalan. The work we refer to as verification and assessment would then proceed much more quickly and on a firmer footing.


What legal reforms are needed to ensure that the process is lasting and irreversible? Specifically, what concrete steps do you expect the government to take to provide legal guarantees that will open the way for democratic politics?


To make the process lasting and irreversible, implementation of the Framework Law must be the starting point. Establishing the bodies envisaged under the law and beginning their work is important for overcoming this critical threshold. We must also reinforce the Framework Law with legislation on freedoms and democratisation to make peace permanent.


Legal guarantees are an indispensable foundation for democratic political activity. A legal framework must be …

title: HPG and YJA-Star guerrillas: Bêrîtan embodies the truth of struggle
content:
People's Defence Forces (HPG) and Free Women's Units (YJA-Star) guerrillas commemorated commander Bêrîtan Hêvî (Gülnaz Karataş) on the anniversary of her martyrdom.


YJA-Star guerrilla Agirî Efrîn spoke about Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom, saying: “I was inspired by comrade Bêrîtan, and it was on this basis that I joined the movement. Today marks the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Comrade Bêrîtan was a commander of the women's army, and Abdullah Öcalan developed the women's military organisation following her martyrdom. Her personality is like a light for us women. I had the opportunity to visit the Martyr Bêrîtan Academy myself, which was a great privilege. As a woman, comrade Bêrîtan showed me the right path. She understood Abdullah Öcalan and put his ideas into practice, and for this we owe her a great deal.


 


Comrade Bêrîtan made history through her resistance against the occupiers. No one would knowingly throw themselves off a cliff, but comrade Bêrîtan did so for a cause. In a short period of time, she had embraced and embodied the idea of the free woman. The position of women in society and within the party is different, and we can see this very clearly. The women's army belongs to all women. Women from every nation have a place in our military organisation. Every woman who recognises the importance of her freedom joins the ranks of the women's army. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of the free woman, and this is also reflected in her struggle.


As women, we believe that we will follow comrade Bêrîtan's path and protect women against all attacks by the system. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of resistance against the system of capitalist modernity, and she sacrificed her life for this cause. Our aim is to uphold the path she established.


Dozens of women sacrificed their lives during the development of the women's military organisation. Comrades Zîlan and Bêrîtan are among the women who have become symbols of the struggle for women's freedom. Patriotism and love for one's homeland were also embodied in comrade Bêrîtan. We renew our pledge to continue her struggle and intensify the struggle for the freedom of women and society.”


‘Bêrîtan represents the Kurdish people's struggle for national unity’


HPG guerrilla Mordem Amed commemorated all martyrs through the memory of Bêrîtan and said: “Comrade Bêrîtan was a woman with a purpose and a quest. Through her action and the message she conveyed, she became a historical figure. She wanted to write a novel about Abdullah Öcalan, which also reflects the depth of her understanding. Historical figures make history through their actions, and the meaning of their stance becomes clearer with the passage of time.


 


Comrade Bêrîtan embodies the true path of patriotism and national consciousness. She stood against all forms of reactionary forces and defended her homeland and her struggle. We can see this in both her life and her action. The attacks by the Turkish state, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the United States are aimed at destroying the Kurds. The year 1992 was extremely important for the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), with many significant developments taking place. Comrades like Bêrîtan understood this period correctly and acted accordingly. The resistance of that time ensured that the Kurdish people's struggle and values would endure.


As fighters following comrade Bêrîtan's path, it is extremely important for us to understand the current period correctly and act accordingly. The process we are going through today is also a historic one in which we must fulfil our role. All Kurdish forces must unite. The KDP's position on this issue is not right. This must change, and Kurdish unity must be built. As fighters following comrade Bêrîtan's path, we must defend Kurdish unity and continue the struggle.


Through comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, thousands of Bêrîtans emerged. Thousands of comrades made following her path the goal of their struggle. Her stance also became a symbol of the free and militant woman. It serves as a guide to struggle for all women. For male comrades, Bêrîtan's stance also represents the spirit of leadership.”


‘Comrade Bêrîtan's dreams will come true’

author: Westsahara Solidarität Berlin
title: 6.11.2026 | DEMO: Freiheit für die Westsahara. Schluss mit der kolonialen Besatzung!
content:
06.11.2026 (Fr), 16:00 Marokkanische Botschaft, Niederwallstr. 39, 10117 Berlin


Kundgebung vor der Botschaft, danach Protestlauf zum Auswärtigen Amt mit Abschlusskundgebung


Die Westsahara ist die letzte Kolonie Afrikas. Nachdem Spanien das Land 1975 verlassen hatte, wurde es von Marokko entgegen aller Beschlüsse der UNO unrechtmäßig besetzt.


Am 6.11.2026 jährt sich zum 51. Mal der sog. „Grüne Marsch“ – ein von Marokko staatlich inszenierter und von der Armee abgesicherter Siedlungsmarsch zur Besetzung der Westsahara. Tausende Saharauis waren damals waren gezwungen ihr Land zu verlassen und als Geflüchtete in Camps in Algerien zu leben.


Der Jahrestag der kolonialen Besatzung der Westsahara gilt in Marokko infamer Weise als Feiertag — doch wir lassen den seit 51 Jahren andauernden Widerstand der sahrauischen Befreiungsbewegung hochleben!


Die Besatzungsmacht in der Westsahara ist repressiv und brutal. Menschen verschwinden in Knästen ohne Kontakt zu ihren Familien. Journalisten werden auf offenere Straße zusammengeschlagen. Angehörige, die Mahnwachen für die Gefangenen abhalten werden verprügelt und festgenommen. Menschenrechtsbeobachter*innen bekommen Einreiseverbot.


Augenblicklich befinden sich Saharauis, die 2010 an einem friedlichen Protestcamp in Gdeim Izik teilnahmen in den marokkanischen Knästen im Hungerstreik gegen ihre unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen.


Wegen all dem wollen wir uns auch dieses Jahr wieder mit einem lautstarken Protest vor der Marokkanischen Botschaft versammeln.


Beim anschließenden Protestlauf zum Auswärtigen Amt werden wir auf die Komplizenschaft der deutschen Bundesregierung und der deutschen Konzerne aufmerksam machen, die sich in den besetzten Gebieten völkerrechtswidrig bereichern und zur Aufrechterhaltung der Besatzung beitragen. Beteiligte Konzerne, die Profit aus dem Status Quo der Besatzung schlagen, sind unter anderen ThyssenKrupp, Siemens, DHL International GmbH, HeidelbergCement, Continental AG und Köster Marine Proteins GmbH und auch die Allianz-Versicherung.


Anlässlich des andauernden Genozids Israels an der palästinensischen Bevölkerung prangern wir zugleich die militärische, ökonomische und politische Zusammenarbeit Deutschlands mit Israel und Marokko an – Komplizenschaft auf Kosten von Freiheit und Selbstbestimmung in Palästina wie in der Westsahara.


Wir fordern: Die sofortiger Freilassung der sahrauischen Gefangenen aus Marokkos Folterknästen! Ein Ende jeglicher Komplizenschaft mit dem marokkanischen Besatzungsregime!


Unsere Solidarität gilt allen, die gegen Kolonialismus, Besatzung und Unterdrückung kämpfen – in der Westsahara und weltweit.


Freiheit, Gerechtigkeit und Selbstbestimmung – jetzt!


Westsahara Solidarität Berlin

author: Kodao Productions
title: The risks journalists face
content:
When police from Davao arrested tabloid columnist Philip Lustre on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, right at the venue of the Saturday News Forum at Dapo Restaurant in Quezon City, serious questions were raised: That it was a Saturday and the cops should have given Lustre some slack on the pretext that weekend arrests are avoided to allow suspects the chance to post bail. Sad to say, this rule is not set in stone but written on murky water.


There used to be another deal between the National Press Club of the Philippines (NPC) and the government that arrests or investigations of journalists on libel, cyberlibel and other charges have to be formally relayed to the club to protect press freedom and the right of suspects to due process. Press freedom was upheld during martial law when imprisoned Satur Ocampo escaped from the clutches of a security detail when he voted during an NPC election. That exercise of press freedom happened during the incumbency of the late NPC president Tony Nieva.


Fair comment is fair comment and it is the task of the accuser to prove that there was malice in reporting, there was ill motive in the commentary and that some AC-DC operation was involved. In one interesting case, a correspondent of an Intramuros-based newspaper was mauled right outside the editorial offices by a businessman who insisted the correspondent was doing a hit job and ruining his trade and reputation. It brought to mind the witty adage of some wag that “press freedom ends where my nose begins.” No reporter, editor or copy boy intervened to save him from being beaten black and blue. His reputation preceded him. The sad story? He is back in business in a purportedly reputable online outlet.

   


In Lustre’s case, his lawyer, Atty. Dino de Leon, was completely aback when the warrant of arrest issued by Judge Retrina Espe Fuentes of Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 10 for cyberlibel did not say who filed the case, Lustre’s address was listed as the editorial office of the Philippine Daily Inquirer (PDI) and Lustre was not even aware that a complaint was filed against him. Defective warrants of arrest can be questioned and the service held in abeyance. Since he was not afforded the right to question the complaint in the first place, de Leon may very well question the in camera proceedings. Where is due process here?


Lustre may complain to high heavens about the raw deal that he got but he might as well cite the even rawer deals done by other courts, as in the case of Ocampo and France Castro and the Talaingod 13, in which those who gave succor to beleaguered students from indigenous groups were found guilty of child trafficking, or Leyte journalist Frenchie Mae Cumpio who got convicted for funding terrorism by a lower court on a matter that the Court of Appeals (CA) had already dismissed. Are these Davao and Leyte courts operating on the basis of Duterte’s iron law? Surely, the people would remember how ex-president and current Scheveningen Prison detainee Rodrigo Duterte bragged about manufacturing evidence to convict suspects in criminal cases but he didn’t talk a wee bit how murderers and smugglers got off the hook when he was still a Davao City fiscal who was as tough as nails.

 


The law cited to convict Cumpio, who has been imprisoned for six years, was not even enacted when the alleged act of terrorism funding was committed. Cumpio was given short shrift by the court, which turned deaf and blind to testimonies and documentary evidence that demolished the charges supported by a script read by professional military informers. Convicted on Jan. 22, 2026, Cumpio and former roommate Mariel Domequil appealed but Judge Georgina Uy Perez of Tacloban RTC reaffirmed her decision to send to the Correctional Institute for Women (CIW) and languish there for 18 years. The court believed the professional military informers who claimed that Cumpio and Domequil delivered P100,000 in cash as well as ammunition to members of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army in Catbalogan City in March 2019.


Prosecutors claimed that Cumpio and Domequil funded the NPA but the narrative of their star witnesses was that they brought the P100,000 to Cumpio and Domequil, ordered them to travel to Catbalogan and were seen arriving at an NPA camp

.

This is standard military narrative. As the defense argued, the military witnesses admitted they brought the money and ammunition to Cumpio and Domequil for delivery to the NPA in time …

title: Rönesans Rezidans davası: Dönemin belediye başkanı ve fen işleri müdürü de yargılanacak
content:
Hatay'da depremin ardından Rönesans Rezidans enkazı | Fotoğraf: DHA

Hatay'da 6 Şubat depremlerinde Rönesans Rezidans'ın yıkılması sonucu 275 kişinin yaşamını yitirmesine ilişkin davaya, hakkında iddianame hazırlanarak dava açılan dönemin Ekinci Belediye Başkanı Seyfettin Yeral ile Fen İşleri Müdürü Mehmet Ezer de dahil edildi. Hatay 3’üncü Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'nde dün görülen duruşmada, 3 tutuklu sanığın tutukluluk halinin devamına karar verilerek dava 30 Kasım'a erteledi.

ANTİS Yapı tarafından inşa edilen ve "Cennetten bir köşe" sloganıyla satılan, Hatay'ın Antakya ilçesinde bulunan Rönesans Rezidans'ın 6 Şubat depremlerinde yıkılması sonucu Hataysporlu futbolcu Christian Atsu, Hatayspor Sportif Direktörü Taner Savut ve milli hentbolcu Cemal Kütahya'nın da aralarında olduğu 275 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, 13 kişi yaralandı. Dışişleri Bakanlığı Hatay Temsilcisi Devrim Öztürk ile bazı yurttaşların cenazelerine enkazda ulaşılamadı.

Hatay Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, sanıklar Mehmet Yaşar Coşkun, Hüseyin Yalçın Coşkun, Ayhan Karan, Mehmet Haşim Eraslan, Bülent Seküçoğlu, Önder Artun, Bayram Mansuroğlu ve İbrahim Dahıroğlu hakkında "bilinçli taksirle birden fazla kişinin ölümüne neden olma" suçundan dava açtı. Geçen yıl 11 Temmuz'daki duruşmada, sanıklar Önder Artun ve Hüseyin Yalçın Coşkun'un vefat ettiği bilgisi paylaşılmış, sanık sayısı 6'ya düşmüştü.

3'ü tutuklu olmak üzere 6 sanığın yargılandığı davaya Hatay 3’üncü Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'nde devam edildi. Bugünkü duruşmada, binanın yıkılmasıyla ilgili haklarında "taksirle ölüme ve yaralanmaya neden olma" suçundan dava açılan dönemin Ekinci Belediye Başkanı Seyfettin Yeral ile Fen İşleri Müdürü Mehmet Ezer'in dosyalarının da görülen davayla birleştirildiği açıklandı.

Duruşmaya, tutuklu sanıklar Mehmet Yaşar Coşkun, Mehmet Haşim Eraslan ve Bülent Seküçoğlu bulundukları cezaevlerinden, tutuksuz sanık Ayhan Karan ise bulunduğu ilden SEGBİS aracılığıyla katıldı. Tutuksuz sanık İbrahim Dahıroğlu ve iki kamu görevlisi, depremde yakınlarını kaybedenler ile taraf avukatları salonda hazır bulundu.

Duruşmada ilk olarak birleşen dosya kapsamında tutuksuz sanıklar Seyfettin Yeral ile Fen İşleri Müdürü Mehmet Ezer'in savunmaları alındı.

Sanık Yeral, 1999 ile 2014 yılları arasında belediye başkanlığı yaptığını belirterek, görev süresi boyunca statik projelerde incelemelerde bulunmadığını, ruhsat vermeden önce teknik personelden destek ve görüş aldıklarını söyledi. Problemli veya sıkıntılı inşaatlara ruhsat onayı vermediklerini ifade eden Yeral, proje ve yapım aşamasındaki denetimleri Fen İşleri Müdürü'nün yaptığını, belediye başkanı olarak projeler üzerinde herhangi bir görevinin bulunmadığını savundu. Yeral, binanın yıkılmasında herhangi bir hatasının olmadığını öne sürerek suçlamaları kabul etmedi.

Dönemin Ekinci Belediyesi Fen İşleri Müdürü Mehmet Ezer ise iddianamenin kendisine ulaşmadığını öne sürerek, savunma için mahkeme heyetinden süre istedi.

Depremde yakınlarını kaybedenler de sanıkların en ağır cezayı almalarını talep etti. Müşteki avukatları, sanıklarından "olası kast" suçlaması yönünden ek savunma alınmasını talep etti.

Tutuklu sanık Mehmet Yaşar Coşkun, 3 yılı aşkın süredir cezaevinde bulunduğunu ve mağdur olduğunu öne sürerek yapıda kusuru olmadığını iddia edip tahliyesini isterken, diğer sanıklar da haklarındaki suçlamaları reddetti.

Mahkeme heyeti, sanıkların mevcut hallerinin devamına ve diğer eksikliklerin giderilmesine karar vererek duruşmayı 30 Kasım'a erteledi.

title: Bakırköy Belediyesine operasyon: 5 başkan yardımcısı dahil 37 kişi gözaltına alındı
content:

İstanbul - Bakırköy Belediyesinin ihale süreçlerinde kamu zararına yol açıldığı ve ruhsat almak isteyen işletmelerden hukuka aykırı para talep edildiği iddiaları üzerine yürütülen soruşturmada, aralarında belediye yöneticileri ve firma temsilcilerinin de bulunduğu 68 kişi hakkında gözaltı kararı verildi. Sabah saatlerinde düzenlenen operasyonda 5 başkan yardımcısı ve 2 meclis üyesinin de aralarında bulunduğu 37 kişi gözaltına alındı.

Bakırköy Belediyesinin ihale ve ruhsat işlemlerine ilişkin usulsüzlük iddiaları üzerine soruşturma başlatıldı. Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının yürüttüğü soruşturma kapsamında, 68 kişi hakkında gözaltına alma, arama ve el koyma işlemlerinin yapılması için talimat verildi. Başsavcılığın açıklamasına göre soruşturma, belediyenin mal ve hizmet alımlarına ilişkin ihale dosyalarında usulsüzlük yapılarak kamu zararına yol açıldığı ve iş yeri çalışma ruhsatı almak isteyen işletme sahiplerinden hukuka aykırı şekilde para talep edildiği yönündeki ihbarlar üzerine başlatıldı.

author: Leanne Sanders
title: Former CEO sues Métis Nation-Saskatchewan, secretariat
content:
Richard Quintal, the former CEO of the Métis Nation-Saskatchewan (MN-S) is suing the organization for wrongful dismissal and breaching his employment contract. Quintal was let go in the spring of 2026.

According to the statement of claim filed Sept. 21 in the Court of King’s Bench in Saskatoon, Quintal is also alleging bad-faith conduct in the way he was dismissed, including the public termination, reversal, suspension, and subsequent investigations the claim alleges were intended to help MN-S avoid its contractual severance obligation.

“The Plaintiff states that the Defendants failed to uphold the obligation of good faith and fair dealing in the manner of dismissal, particularly with respect to the public without cause termination of the Plaintiff…,” the claim alleges.

At the heart of Quintal’s claim is the terms of his employment contract with MN-S.

“The Plaintiff commenced employment with the Defendants on January 8, 2018, through the federal government Interchange Program. The Plaintiff was then offered employment by the Defendants as MNS’s Chief of Staff through a fixed-term contract of employment dated July 20, 2019,” the claim says.

“The contract was then replaced and superseded by a fixed-term extension contract dated December 1, 2022, which, among other things, appointed the Plaintiff Chief of Staff/Chief Executive Officer of MNS, and extended the Plaintiff’s employment with the Defendants to November 30, 2027.”

The claim goes on to allege that “this extension contract was further amended by the Defendants on or about May 9, 2024, and included an extension of the Plaintiff’s employment with the Defendants to July 31, 2030.”

The statement of claim says “significantly, the Contract stated the employment relationship may be terminated without cause upon the Defendants’ providing the Plaintiff with a lump-sum payment…”

According to the claim, the payment is to be equal to whichever is greater: “the minimum notice or pay in lieu of notice and severance pay,” or “the remainder of the Annual Base Salary which would have been payable over the term of the Agreement if the Plaintiff’s employment had not been terminated…”

Quintal is also seeking aggravated or moral damages, punitive damages, special damages, interest, legal costs, and “any further relief the court permits,” according to the claim.

Quintal alleges in the claim he received a letter dated May 13, explaining he was being placed on paid administrative leave while a review was conducted “into the circumstances that led to the extension of his contract to July 2030.”

“The letter stated that the PMC was not aware of (Quintal’s)Contract extension. This claim was made in spite of the fact that at least three members of the PMC at the time…” President Glen McCallum, Marg Friesen, and Brennan Merasty had “full knowledge of the Contract extension at the time the Contract was amended and were in communication regarding the said extension,” Quintal’s claim alleges.

Allegations and accusations dogged Quintal as far back as 2020, according to reports in the media.

Quintal claims he experienced bullying and harassment by certain Provincial Métis Council (PMC) members, and was “publicly discredited and humiliated.”

Several members of MN-S were “suspended pending an apology to the Plaintiff,” however a negotiated resolution followed in April 2025.

The elected members were invited to rejoin the PMC and the Métis Nation Legislative Assembly (MNLA) on May 20, 2026.

“We’ve pushed the reset button to be able to start a new journey…[so]that the obligations of your government [are] not put on the sidelines,” President Glen McCallum said at the time.

The MN-S also lifted the bans against 12 Métis citizens who also had received cease and desist letters last fall.

In a letter sent to the citizens in April, 2026, the Nation’s legal counsel said the rescinding of the letters is not an admission of “liability or wrongdoing by MN-S or the PMC.”

According to Quintal’s statement of claim, he says MNS advised him on April 23 that it would terminate him without cause. The Provincial Métis Council then passed a resolution making the termination effective May 15, publicly announced the change, and began planning a transition.

Quintal alleges in the claim that after he cooperated with the transition, MNS allegedly rescinded the termination decision on May 11, placed him on paid administrative leave, and said it would review how his contract had been extended to 2030 …

author: APTN National News
title: Carney open to conversations around ‘moving beyond’ the Indian Act
content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney says he’s open to discussions around getting rid of the Indian Act.


Passed in 1876, the controversial legislation governs people who have status under the act, reserve lands and issues related to band councils.


Carney was responding to comments made by Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew earlier in the day during the First Nations-First Ministers Meeting in Ottawa.


“Participants in the meeting raised the desirability,” Carney told reporters at the end of the meeting. “Not everybody, but other participants raised a desirability, so it’s already starting from the right place.


“And it’s not the federal government deciding something should be done.”


At the noon break, Kinew held up his First Nations status card, which he said identifies him as an “Indian within the meaning of the Indian Act.”


“It’s time to abolish the Indian Act,” Kinew said. “It’s long overdue that we have a relationship with Indigenous Peoples in Canada that reflects who we are as Canadians today.”


This isn’t the first time First Nations have called for the act to be scrapped – or a government saying it would move towards it.


At the news conference, Carney said that he’d instruct his ministers to work with First Nations to move Canada beyond the Indian Act, which could mean reforming it or abolishing it altogether.


The prime minister said the government is addressing a number of issues contained in the law, including consultations around the second-generation cutoff. That’s where the law strips a person of their legal Indian status after two consecutive generations of parenting with a partner who doesn’t have “status” under the Indian Act.


Cindy Woodhouse-Nepinak, the national chief of the Assembly of First Nations, said at the same news conference that consultations would have to be extensive.


“There is a diversity of First Nations from coast to coast to coast. We’re in every province and territory in this beautiful country that we all share,” she said. “And that question is going to be up to them to decide right, and they’re going to have to decide for themselves.”


It’s not clear when this process will start.


“I am committed to a process that moves Canada beyond the Indian Act,” Carney said.


Tensions between Ottawa and First Nations spiked soon after Carney was elected in 2025 when his government passed legislation to create a new office tasked with streamlining major project developments and approving projects within one year.


First Nations leaders warned the compressed timelines would interfere with their rights and lead to court challenges. Provincial governments have enacted similar legislation.


But tensions are boiling over for a number of other reasons as well, including the lands claim process in British Columbia, the newly announced Pacific Link pipeline project in Alberta and development of the mineral-rich Ring of Fire in Ontario. In many cases, it’s youth who are pushing back on First Nations leaders, the premiers and prime minister.


Carney said Monday it’s “sobering” to consider that this is the first meeting to bring together federal, provincial and First Nations leaders in two decades.


“Our task is twofold. First is to work together to create opportunities for all our peoples, while building a country that is stronger, more sovereign and more independent,” he said.


“And secondly, our task is to live our values fully of a fair and inclusive Canada.”


While some First Nations are opposed to Carney’s development agenda and those of the provinces, others are open to the idea of increasing economic activity in their territories.


Nisga’a Nation President Eva Clayton told reporters ahead of the meeting she supports Carney’s plans and that she and other modern treaty holders are at the meeting to support Canada.


With files from the Canadian Press.

Carney open to conversations around ‘moving beyond’ the Indian Act

 appeared first on

APTN News

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Netanyahu Extends Assault on Hebron Ahead of Israel’s Elections
content:
Israeli forces have displaced over 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in the West Bank city of Hebron since Friday.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Over 3,000 Palestinians have been displaced from their homes in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron (Al-Khalil) since Friday, as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu carries out collective punishment in a bid to shore up support ahead of Israel’s elections on Tuesday.

On Friday, after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire on an Israeli military checkpoint in Hebron, killing two Israeli soldiers, Netanyahu stated that he would “prepare for a full lockdown across all of Judea and Samaria,” using the Israeli term to encompass the West Bank.

The Israeli military quickly locked down the city of Hebron — the largest city in the West Bank and its economic capital — and destroyed the Farsh al-Hawa neighborhood, where the checkpoint was located. Israel’s Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he ordered the destruction in the neighborhood, and filmed himself in front of a building being demolished. The army went on to convert some Palestinian homes into military posts for its operation, and forced families in the Ein Deir Baha neighborhood to leave their homes at night on foot.

Israeli soldiers also besieged the Fawwar refugee camp in Hebron, blocking the camp’s entrance on Saturday to prevent any Palestinians from entering or leaving.

Nearly half of those displaced are babies and children under the age of 18, along with elderly people and pregnant women.

According to Haaretz, Israeli military Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir moved to end the military raid of Hebron on Saturday, stating that its objectives had been met. But Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz insisted that the military operation continue, expanding the displacement of residents and preventing those who had been displaced from returning home.

“These actions by the Israeli occupation are driven by the elections,” Hebron’s mayor, Yousef al-Jabari, told Democracy Now! on Monday. “We are days, or even hours, away from the Israeli elections. Netanyahu and the radical ministers in his government are trying to win as many votes as possible from the settlers. The Israeli response is disproportionate, and there is no justification for these actions.”

Al-Jabari also said that Israel’s actions constituted collective punishment — a statement echoed by the UN.

On Tuesday, Israelis will head to the polls in the first Israeli election since before October 7, 2023 — and one that polls show is an extremely tight race between Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot. Though Netanyahu is the longest-standing Israeli prime minister, his candidacy has been shaken by his corruption trial and his failures on and after October 7.

Netanyahu’s disproportionate response is likely fueled by his desire to demonstrate his ability to wage violence against Palestinians ahead of the election, and to shore up additional votes.

Netanyahu has also reportedly been considering renewed attacks against Iran, likely for the same reason. On Sunday, he published a video warning Iran “and its allies” against interfering with Israel’s elections, saying: “You will suffer blows far stronger than you can imagine.”

Tamir Sorek, professor of Middle East History at Pennsylvania State University, told Truthout that Netanyahu’s actions are consistent with Israel’s long-standing settler-colonial violence and dispossession of Palestinians.

“But at the same time, in these particular circumstances, Netanyahu needs to put what is called the ‘security situation’ at the heart of public discussion,” he said.

Netanyahu “knows that if there are discussions about corruption, for example, or about the economic situation, he is vulnerable,” Sorek went on. But if he can create the feeling of “a security emergency … then he has a better chance to succeed in the elections.”

“So for him, escalating the dynamics everywhere — in the West Bank, in the Gaza Strip, in Iran — for him, it is an electoral advantage,” Sorek said.

The escalations are not likely to end on Tuesday, either — particularly given the fact that Israel’s political parties will need to form alliances to create a ruling coalition, which could take weeks.

“We are likely to see him pushing toward more escalations,” Sorek said. This is for two reasons, he explained: The first is to show the …

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: Protest outside First Nations–First Ministers Meeting decry closed doors and ‘economic coercion’
content:
Grassroots organizers staged a visible presence outside the building where First Nations leaders,

Prime Minister Mark Carney

 and premiers were meeting on Monday, arguing that limited access, narrow representation and a push for major projects amount to consultation in name only.


Wet’suwet’en Hereditary Chief Na’Moks, who was able to enter the building after discussions with the Assembly of First Nations, said the decision to keep most media outside undercut basic democratic norms.


“I have a problem with them not allowing media in to cover this. Because we live in a democratic country. We’re supposed to have free access to information and the press allowed everywhere. We’re being treated like we live in a communist country,” Na’Moks said.


He credited British Columbia Assembly of First Nations Regional Chief Terry Teegee with helping him get inside to hear what was going on during the meeting.


“We got to go inside through AFN. We had a conversation with them and we got to go inside and listen to them. We just came outside from that,” he said. “But I will say my main part was to listen to the chiefs and the opening remarks that they had. And I loved the fact that some went off script and said, you know what? We’re not here just for a photo op. We’re not here just to make a comment. We’re here to tell you the truth.


“That really stood out to me and I was so glad I was there in the room to listen to it.”


Ramon Kataquapit outside the meeting in Ottawa. Photo: Keelan Jacobs/APTN.


Ramon Kataquapit, who sits on the Chiefs of Ontario’s Youth Council, spoke to APTN News outside about the meeting and framed the gathering as another step in a longer pattern of inadequate representation and coercive policy.


“We haven’t had adequate representation from our First Nations and our people in there,” he said. “The main issue that I’m here standing against is what the prime minister and the first ministers have been doing with trying to use this meeting as consultation for our people. And when it comes to what they’re pushing forward right now with these major projects and these bills like Bill C-5, Bill C-37, and Bill C-39, these are really big pieces of authoritarian legislation that’s trying to put our First Nations between a rock and a hard place, forcing us into economic coercion.”


He rejected the idea that a single high-level meeting, or a short series of follow-ups, could meet the standard of free, prior and informed consent.


“When it comes to this meeting, I believe that it’s another part of the process of the Mark Carney government, but also the history of governments, believe that having consultation with First Nations just ends with one meeting and maybe establishing another set of a few meetings.”


Russell Diabo, spokesperson for the Truth Before Reconciliation Education & Advocacy Network, which helped organize the outside presence, expressed low expectations for concrete results.


“I don’t expect much to come out of this meeting,” Diabo said.


Read More:


Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew calls on prime minister to abolish the Indian Act at meeting with chiefs 


Diplomats and disruptors: First Nations get set for a meeting with Canada’s leaders with ceremony 


The Monday session brought Carney, provincial and territorial premiers, and a limited First Nations delegation together on unceded Algonquin territory.


A day of ceremony was held Sunday. Public details about the agenda and speaking arrangements remained sparse in the days leading up to the meeting, and media access to the main discussions was tightly controlled.


Inside the process, different First Nations voices have taken different approaches.


Part of the protest in Ottawa. Photo: Keelan Jacobs/APTN.


Modern-treaty and self-governing nations represented by the Land Claims Agreements Coalition issued a statement Sunday welcoming participation and pointing to their jurisdiction over roughly 40 per cent of Canada’s land base and more than two-thirds of its coastline.


Outside the building, organizers and hereditary leaders argued that the meeting’s structure — with limited seats, restricted media, and an emphasis on economic partnerships tied to major projects—risks treating attendance as a substitute for consent.


The presence outside included flags and banners from Treaty 6 nations, including Onion Lake Cree Nation, which had earlier issued a cease-and-desist notice asserting that the AFN does not speak or consent on its behalf …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Calls for Metal Detector in Senate for El-Sayed in New Islamophobic Remark
content:
Trump called El-Sayed a “jihadist” and said people like him should never be allowed in the Senate.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Republicans’ Islamophobia reached new lows this weekend at a Michigan rally hosted by Donald Trump, where the president repeatedly labelled Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as a “jihadist” and one speaker condemned El-Sayed’s “blood.”

Trump, invoking post-9/11 airport security guidelines, said that El-Sayed would be “unable to get a seat on an airplane” for his supposed “record of support for jihadists” and that “they certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate.”

“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector!” Trump went on. Metal detectors are not currently in use in the Senate, but were temporarily put in place for the House after the January 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol.

Nearly all of Trump’s remarks on El-Sayed at the rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday focused on the latter’s Muslim identity — with many Islamophobic remarks being met with cheers from the crowd.

Trump said that El-Sayed is “on the side of the terrorists,” wants to implement “Sharia law,” and is a “jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member,” a complete fabrication. He also invoked anti-immigrant sentiment, saying that El-Sayed will “invite hordes of jihadists to our shores” who will make it so that “you cannot even have a Christmas,” and likening El-Sayed to Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), who the administration is reportedly trying to deport.

By contrast, Trump spoke very little of the GOP’s Senate candidate, Mike Rogers, who he simply said is “apple pie.” Trump said that Rogers, who is white, is “what your state is all about.”

The president introduced another speaker at the rally, the father of a Flight 93 victim, who spewed white supremacist rhetoric about El-Sayed’s blood.

“Mike Rogers is an American. Abdul has a birth certificate. The birth certificate says he’s a citizen of America. You know what? A birth certificate doesn’t make you an American,” said the speaker, David Beamer.

“[El-Sayed] had the choice to be an American or not. He has chosen otherwise,” Beamer went on. “He has blood that’s red. However, he has chosen to remove any strain of the white and blue part in his blood. We cannot, cannot allow this man to invade and occupy our country.”

The remarks were an escalation of Trump and the GOP’s Islamophobic rhetoric against El-Sayed and were condemned by critics. They come as far right Islamophobic agitator Jake Lang has been protesting El-Sayed and Muslims in Michigan across the state.

El-Sayed hit back at Trump and his Islamophobic rhetoric at his own rally on Sunday, addressing Trump for calling him “Mohamed” as an attempt to highlight and attack his Muslim background.

“I don’t care how he pronounces my name. I don’t even care that he remembers my whole name,” said El-Sayed in a rally in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Sunday. “Because he can just go on and call me ‘senator’ after November. I will be Senator Mohamed to you, bro.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Serbia’s Student-Led Movement Sweeps Strongman Aleksander Vučić Out of Power
content:
Students “changed our understanding of what’s politically possible for all of us,” says journalist Lela Vujanić.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Serbia’s longtime leader Aleksander Vučić has been swept out of power by a historic student-led opposition movement against Vučić’s right-wing Serbian Progressive Party. Candidates from the Student List, who are not students themselves but largely first-time politicians selected by student-led popular assemblies, won a majority of seats in Sunday’s parliamentary elections, marking a seismic shift in Serbian politics. Their victory comes two years into a student-led movement sparked by the collapse of a roof at a train station in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. The disaster became a focal point for anti-government protests over corruption, cronyism, political violence and democratic backsliding.

“Students really changed the whole political landscape of the country, and maybe even more important, they changed political imagination. They changed our understanding of what’s politically possible for all of us,” says journalist Lela Vujanić, who speaks to us from Belgrade about the groundbreaking elections. “This was a great democratic opening and democratic awakening, not only for the students, but for the rest of the country also.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman in Colorado, with Juan González in Chicago.

In Serbia, longtime nationalist leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat following elections Sunday in a contest that pitted Vučić and his right-wing party against a student-led movement that had weakened his hold on power after two years of anti-government protests. The student-led movement first rose up in November 2024 following the collapse of a roof at a train station in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. The disaster became a focal point for protests over government corruption, cronyism, political violence and democratic backsliding. President Vučić conceded defeat after early results showed the Student List poised to win more than 135 seats in the 250-member parliament, compared with only 105 for Vučić’s party. The historic defeat marks the end of a 14-year rule and a seismic shift in Serbian politics.

Tens of thousands of residents flooded into the streets to celebrate following the concession.

SEJLA KIPIC: The feeling is surreal. I laughed. I cried. I screamed. I jumped. It’s just unbelievable. After so many years of this tyranny and dictatorship, we are finally free. And that’s — you cannot put it in words.

AMY GOODMAN: The candidates on the newly formed Student List aren’t students, but political newcomers including farmers, athletes, artists and little-known experts. Students traveled through rural areas on foot and on bicycle to speak directly with voters in rural areas — traditional strongholds of Vučić. This is Student List candidate Radomir Saičić.

RADOMIR SAIČIĆ: [translated] This is a victory of courage over fear, a victory over unrest. Serbia can and must be different. Thank you for every step, every hour, every sacrifice and for every moment you chose not to give up. Thank you to everyone who raised their voice, stood by one another and showed that the future of this country does not belong to a select few, but to all its citizens.

AMY GOODMAN: For more, we go to Belgrade, Serbia, where we’re joined by Lela Vujanić. She’s a journalist and media researcher covering both media and social movements.

Lela, welcome to Democracy Now! If you can talk about this stunning victory of the Student List movement and what Vučić represented, and the changes you think will happen as a result of something we’re seeing not only in Serbia, but student-led movements across Europe right now?

LELA VUJANIĆ: Hi, Amy. Thank you for having me. I was listening the Brazilian segment, and I’m super happy for Lula’s victory and for Brazilian people voting this way.

But, yes, we have something quite historic and extraordinary happening in Serbia, as you said. Yesterday, it was Election Day, parliamentary elections. And our mass civic, social movement, that’s led by Serbian students, was able — that lasts already for two years — was able not only to challenge Vučić and his ruling SNS party, but to win popular vote in a landslide victory, winning 52% of the votes.

author: Kim Sullivan
title: 72 ans après sa mort, la dépouille du bébé Maxime retourne à Manawan
content:
Après un moment pour reprendre son souffle, Manon Ottawa s’exprime devant les médias. « Aujourd’hui, je suis profondément émue de pouvoir annoncer officiellement la date de son retour. »


Elle fait référence au retour de la dépouille de son oncle Maxime. Soixante-douze ans après sa mort, presqu’au jour le jour, le bébé Maxime revient enfin parmi les siens. « Bébé Maxime reviendra à Manawan, sur la terre de nos ancêtres, auprès de sa famille et de son peuple atikamekw. »


C’est un témoignage parmi tant d’autres de l’histoire des enfants autochtones disparus. À l’âge de six mois, bébé Maxime a dû être transporter en hydro-avion à l’hôpital de La Tuque. Seul. « Imaginer la douleur d’une mère qui voit partir son enfant sans pouvoir l’accompagner », dit Manon. Il a ensuite été transféré vers l’hôpital de Québec sans qu’on en avise ses parents. Après 43 jours à l’hôpital, bébé Maxime est mort le 5 octobre 1954.


Conférence de presse du 22 octobre, 2026.


 


Lors de la conférence de presse, l’avocate de la famille Ottawa, Olivia Malenfant, continue à raconter l’histoire du bébé Maxime : « Ses parents n’apprennent de son décès que 2 ans plus tard. Pendant tout ce temps, ils ignorent ce qui est advenu de leur enfant. Ils ne peuvent ni lui dire adieu, ni lui offrir des funérailles, ni lui offrir une sépulture conforme à leurs traditions. Pendant des décennies, la famille est demeurée sans réponses qu’en aux circonstances du décès de bébé Maxime et l’endroit où il a été inhumé. Cette absence d’information concernant le sort d’un proche, la plupart du temps un enfant, est une réalité à laquelle de nombreuses familles autochtones ont été confrontés. »


En 2014, pour honorer la dernière volonté de son père, Manon Ottawa a entrepris les recherches pour retrouver son oncle – le bébé maxime. « Ce parcours n’a pas été facile. Il y a eu des obstacles, des moments de découragement, des longues attentes et beaucoup d’émotions. Mais je n’ai jamais abandonné. »


En octobre 2025, la cour supérieure du Québec accepte une exhumation d’un lot où se trouvaient 5 personnes au total. Maître Malenfant explique que l’exhumation fût complexe, non seulement à cause du nombre de personnes dans le lot creusé, mais aussi parce que « les lots adjacents complétaient 4 défunts d’un côté et 5 de l’autre. Toutes des personnes autochtones. »


À ce moment, un corps présumé d’être celui du bébé Maxime a été envoyé pour identification au Laboratoire de sciences judiciaires et de médecine légale. « Des analyses et des tests d’ADN ont ensuite été effectués afin de confirmer son identité. Le 30 septembre 2026, lors de la Journée nationale de la vérité et de la réconciliation, nous avons reçu la confirmation tant attendue. Les résultats étaient concluants », précise Manon. « Je ne m’attendais pas à ça. J’ai pleuré parce que c’était un soulagement. »


Bébé Maxime a été retrouvé.


Manon a pris un instant pour « remercier sincèrement le Conseil des Atikamekw de Manawan, ainsi que l’association Awacak, Petits êtres de lumière. » Constant Awashish, Grand chef du Conseil de la nation Atikamekw était présent. « La famille, finalement, avoir des réponses à leurs questionnements qui a duré 72 ans quand même. C’est long. Il y a des gens qui sont décédés, des membres de la famille qui sont décédés au courant des années, sans savoir qu’est-ce qui était passé avec bébé maxime. Puis aujourd’hui, je pense que c’est grâce au travail acharné de l’équipe à Awacak, de la communauté, de la famille qui n’ont pas abandonné leur recherche. On peut trouver un dénouement à toute cette période sombre qui a pu affecter de la famille. »


Cette démarche, affirme Manon, est devenue beaucoup plus grande que leur seule histoire familiale. « En cherchant bébé maxime, d’autres enfants ont également été retrouvé. » Le grand chef Awashish précise que « le chemin est tracé. C’est parmi les premiers qui ont réussi à faire l’exercice. Je sais qu’il y en a d’autres dans la Nation atikamekw qui recherchent des membres de leur famille, en espérant que ça peut apporter de l’espoir et de l’encouragement. »


Photo d’archives. 16 décembre, 2019 : une des premières rencontres d’APTN avec Manon Ottawa, où elle nous montre le tikinan.


 


Sur la table de la conférence de presse, un tikinan décoré. Le même type de porte-bébé dans lequel ses grands-parents avaient déposé le petit Maxime lors de son départ vers l’hôpital. Manon l’avait acheté au début de ses recherche, se promettant que tant que bébé …

title: Two Kurdish women missing after being detained
content:
The Voice of Iranian Prisoners Organisation issued a statement concerning two Kurdish women detained in Rojhilatê Kurdistan (East Kurdistan).


The statement said that 17-year-old Perya Nasirî was detained by Iranian intelligence forces at her school in Nexede on 21 October. Six days after her disappearance, her fate and whereabouts remained unknown.


It also stated that Sedrî Bexşî, 43, from the village of Weştape in Bokan, had been held at the Urmiye Intelligence Directorate since her detention a month earlier and was facing serious security-related threats.


After being detained over posts shared on digital media platforms, Sedrî Bexşî had been allowed only one brief telephone conversation with her family, according to the statement. According to the report, Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces raided Sedrî Bexşî’s home in the village of Weştape a month ago, using eight armoured vehicles. Following a search of the house, they seized her phone.

author: Daron Letts
title: Nunavut athletes honoured in Ottawa
content:
Two Nunavut athletes were honoured on Saturday night in Ottawa during the Aboriginal Sports Circle’s National Indigenous Sports Gala.


Rankin Inlet hockey player Lana Lindell and Sanikiluaq multisport athlete Andrew Kavik were named as Nunavut’s recipients of the Tom Longboat Award, established in 1951 in memory of the late Onondaga distance runner from the Six Nations Reserve, near Brantford, Ont.


“It was a great night filled with celebration,” said Aboriginal Sport Circle spokesperson Julie Hawrishok, in an email. “The main ballroom was transformed with lights and a digital background that displayed images of the recipients and images from their home province or territory.”


Lindell accepted her award onstage at the Ottawa Conference Centre 

from former Aboriginal Sport Circle board member Brendon Smithson. Jeff Seeteenak, f

ormer chef de mission for Team Nunavut, accepted Kavik’s award on his behalf because the athlete was unable to attend.


Kavik was recognized for excelling in badminton and for helping his team earn bronze in volleyball during the 2026 Arctic Winter Games.


At the same event, Lindell captained Team Nunavut’s U19 female hockey team to a bronze.

She also captained Saskatchewan’s U18AA Notre Dame Hounds while attending Athol Murray College of Notre Dame.


Alongside hockey, she has participated in volleyball, basketball rugby, and ultimate frisbee during four years at the sports development high school.


“Anything that they provided I played at least a year of,” she said in a phone interview.


She is active in student leadership and volunteer initiatives while studying engineering at the University of Saskatchewan.


Although the Professional Women’s Hockey League remains a dream, Lindell’s plan is to return home to help build infrastructure in Rankin Inlet, she said.

title: Panel discussion on Jineolojî and self-defense in Marseille
content:
A panel discussion and commemoration event focusing on Jineolojî and the formation of women’s armed forces was held in Marseille, France, organized by the Association of Martyrs’ Families (KOMAW), the Marseille Arîn Mîrkan Women’s Council, and members of Jineolojî Provence. The event, held at the Marseille Kurdish Democratic Community Center, was attended by numerous Kurdish women from the region, as well as representatives of French internationalist women’s movements.


The event began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the Kurdistan freedom struggle, represented by Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), described as an immortal commander of the Kurdish women’s struggle, as well as international women revolutionaries who lost their lives defending life.


This was followed by a video presentation highlighting Bêrîtan’s commitment to the principles of women’s freedom and the resistance of Kurdish women in their struggle for liberation. During the screening, chants of “Şehîd namirin” (“Martyrs are immortal) frequently echoed through the hall.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/c389a11c_20261025174114_2026-10-25-marsilya-jineoloji-paneli-1.mp4


‘The formation of women’s armed forces and Jineolojî in the pursuit of women’s freedom’


Speaking at a seminar titled “The Formation of Armed Forces within the Kurdistan Women’s Movement and Jineolojî,” Sîdar Feraşîn, a member of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E), discussed the historical development of the Kurdish women’s movement, awareness of self-defense, and the importance of organizing women’s armed forces.


Feraşîn emphasized that Jineolojî should play a greater role in women’s gatherings and areas of struggle, not merely as an institutional identity but also as a guiding perspective. She also highlighted the importance of the principles of women’s freedom.


Feraşîn stated that Kurdish women continue their organizing efforts in various fields, particularly politics, diplomacy, culture, and the arts, while work on Jineolojî is also ongoing. She noted that educational activities conducted across Europe through camps, seminars, workshops, and conferences have encouraged women to develop new ways of questioning and critical thinking. She emphasized the need to adapt organizational structures to the existing potential.


Discussions focused on the role of Jineolojî, as the science of women, in social transformation. Participants emphasized that strengthening the principles of women’s freedom is essential to building an alternative way of life. They also highlighted the resistance of Bêrîtan, who lost her life in the struggle, as one of the symbols of the Kurdish people’s and Kurdish women’s struggle for a free life.


Message of solidarity from internationalist women


In a statement issued by members of Jineolojî Provence and representatives of international women’s movements, violence against women and femicide were described as being linked to the persistence of the patriarchal system and fascism. The statement emphasized women’s determination to strengthen their struggle for freedom in different parts of the world.


The statement also stressed that keeping the memory of women revolutionaries alive provides strength and courage to continue the struggle, concluding with the message “Berxwedan Jiyan e” (“Resistance is life”).


Elefteria Hambi and Nagihan Akarsel commemorated


The event also commemorated Elefteria Hambi, an internationalist revolutionary who lost her life in Rojava, and Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Academy who was killed in Sulaymaniyah in an assassination carried out by the Turkish state.


A speech honoring Elefteria Hambi (Eva Maria Steiger) recalled that she traveled to Rojava in 2018 and fought against ISIS in the ranks of the YPJ before joining the guerrilla struggle in the Garê and Qandil regions. A tribute written in memory of the German revolutionary was read aloud.


The portraits prepared jointly by Jineolojî Provence and the Third District Neighborhood Committee were described as symbols of remembrance and internationalist solidarity.


In the final part of the program, a poem written in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, the Kurdish journalist and academic who was killed, was recited.


The event concluded with a performance by a choir formed under the Arîn Mîrkan Women’s Council.

title: Girê Spî Committee calls for the protection of families trapped in Regional Directorate building
content:
A group of Kurdish residents from Girê Spî, who were returning to their homes at the invitation of the Girê Spî Regional Directorate, were attacked while entering the building earlier today.


The Girê Spî Committee for the Forcibly Displaced reported that more than 100 Kurdish families were under siege inside the Regional Directorate building.


The committee described the attack against Kurds as an assault on their safety and their legitimate right to return. It called for the protection of the families and for an immediate investigation into those responsible.


The committee stated that it had been coordinating with relevant parties and following up on efforts to enable forcibly displaced families to return to their homes and properties. These efforts have so far yielded no results, it added.


The committee emphasized that the Regional Directorate officials must fulfill their responsibilities to protect the residents against such attacks.


Drawing attention to the plight of more than 100 Kurdish families, including women and children, trapped inside the Girê Spî Regional Directorate building, the committee called on the relevant authorities to intervene immediately to protect the residents from further attacks.


The committee stated that anyone wishing to return to Girê Spî should contact and coordinate with the committee so that their return can be organized, followed up with the relevant parties, and appropriate conditions can be established to ensure their safety.


The committee called on the relevant authorities to launch a thorough and transparent investigation into the attacks, hold all those responsible accountable, take appropriate measures to ensure residents’ safety and prevent further violations, facilitate the safe return of families, and protect their legitimate rights.

title: Temelli: Steps toward democratizing the Republic must not be delayed
content:
At a press conference held in Parliament, DEM Party Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli addressed the peace and democratic society process. He called for the opportunity presented by the process to be seized and for the necessary steps to be taken without delay.


“The democratic resolution to the Kurdish question is the most important step toward comprehensive democratization and the democratization of the Republic,” Temelli said.


Temelli pointed out that the Kurdish question has remained unresolved throughout the Republic’s 100-year history, and that its democratic resolution is of critical importance for the democratization of the Republic.


He emphasized the need to guarantee freedom of the press and expression, protect human rights, and end political bans.


Drawing attention to the continued imprisonment of political figures in Turkey, Temelli cited Figen Yüksekdağ and Selahattin Demirtaş, who are imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial, as well as Can Atalay.


Criticizing the Turkish state’s failure to implement rulings of the European Court of Human Rights, Temelli stated that the Republic must embrace democracy and freedoms.


“The Republic must be at peace with democracy. The path to lasting social peace lies through a democratic state governed by the rule of law, based on equal citizenship. It is therefore essential that we establish such a state governed by the rule of law as soon as possible,” Sezai Temelli said.


Emphasizing that democracy is not limited to political institutions, Temelli stated that prison conditions, freedom of expression, trade union rights, women’s participation in politics, and the fight against poverty are also fundamental indicators of democratization.
