author: The Canadian Press
title: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew calls on prime minister to abolish the Indian Act at meeting with chiefs
content:
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew says he told Prime Minister Mark Carney that Canada should abolish the Indian Act during a historic meeting with premiers and First Nations leaders.


Speaking with reporters during a midday break in the meeting Monday, Kinew held up his First Nations status card, which he said identifies him as an “Indian within the meaning of the Indian Act.”


“It’s time to abolish the Indian Act,” Kinew said. “It’s long overdue that we have a relationship with Indigenous Peoples in Canada that reflects who we are as Canadians today.”


Carney and most of the premiers sat down with chiefs from the Assembly of First Nations in Ottawa for a discussion AFN National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak said is intended to help build prosperity for coming generations.


AFN National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak and Prime Minister Mark Carney listen to opening remarks in Ottawa on Monday. Photo: Raven Brascoupe/APTN.


Monday’s closed-door meeting is the first such gathering since the Kelowna Accord talks of 2005, which brought premiers and then-prime minister Paul Martin together with Indigenous leaders to discuss ways to close the socioeconomic gaps in Indigenous communities.


The Kelowna agreement was not implemented after the Conservative government under former prime minister Stephen Harper took office just a few months later.


This meeting comes as Carney’s government works to speed up major project approvals and development — efforts some First Nations chiefs say threaten their rights.


Jeronimo Kataquapit, who was protesting the major projects push outside the meeting venue in Ottawa, chided the federal government and the Assembly of First Nations over the lack of youth representation at the meeting.


“These major projects cannot move forward without our free, prior and informed consent, and it’s the youth that stand to be the most impacted by the decisions made today by all leadership, both Indigenous and non-Indigenous alike,” Kataquapit said from the sidewalk in front of the Diefenbaker Building.


Protester Katisha Paul, an advocate for youth and women, questioned the Assembly of First Nations’ mandate to negotiate on First Nations’ behalf.


“I’m not in that room today but I can imagine and speculate that the voices of our ancestors are not being heard, they’re not being voiced and they’re not being amplified because many of those elected band council chiefs have lost their ways,” Paul said.


The protest outside 111 Sussex Dr., in Ottawa where the First Nations-First Ministers Meeting was taking place. Photo: Keelan Jacobs/APTN.


Tensions between Ottawa and First Nations spiked soon after Carney was elected in 2025 when his government passed legislation to create a new office tasked with streamlining major project developments and approving projects within one year.


First Nations leaders warned the compressed timelines would interfere with their rights and lead to court challenges. Provincial governments have enacted similar legislation.


But tensions are boiling over for a number of other reasons as well, including the lands claim process in British Columbia, the newly announced Pacific Link pipeline project in Alberta and development of the mineral-rich Ring of Fire in Ontario. In many cases, it’s youth who are pushing back on First Nations leaders, the premiers and prime minister.


Carney said Monday it’s “sobering” to consider that this is the first meeting to bring together federal, provincial and First Nations leaders in two decades.


“Our task is twofold. First is to work together to create opportunities for all our peoples, while building a country that is stronger, more sovereign and more independent,” he said.


“And secondly, our task is to live our values fully of a fair and inclusive Canada.”


While some First Nations are opposed to Carney’s development agenda and those of the provinces, others are open to the idea of increasing economic activity in their territories.


Nisga’a Nation President Eva Clayton told reporters ahead of the meeting she supports Carney’s plans and that she and other modern treaty holders are at the meeting to support Canada.


Story by Alessia Passafiume and Kyle Duggan

author: Jake Johnson
title: US Urged to Recognize Lula’s Presidential Victory as Bolsonaro Demands Annulment
content:
Trump ally Flávio Bolsonaro’s refusal to accept the results sparks fears of political violence and another coup attempt.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Pro-democracy campaigners urged governments around the world, including in the U.S., to formally recognize Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva victory in Sunday’s runoff election as his far-right challenger, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, refused to accept the results, sparking fears of political violence and another coup attempt.

“It is impossible to recognize the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections,” said Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted last year over a plot to violently maintain power following Lula’s 2022 election win. On Sunday, the younger Bolsonaro pointed to the Brazilian Supreme Court’s decision to keep polls open for two hours past the scheduled deadline as a reason to dispute the results — even though both Lula and Bolsonaro pushed for the extension, for different reasons.

Numerous world leaders, including Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, congratulated Lula on his reelection win over Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump. The U.S.-based Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR), which sounded the alarm about the Trump administration’s attempts to interfere in the Brazilian elections ahead of Sunday’s runoff, said in a statement on Sunday that “governments — including the Trump administration — should immediately recognize the outcome, to prevent a possible coup or further violence.”

“It’s likely that Flávio Bolsonaro will, like his father in late 2022, encourage his supporters to mobilize in order to try to overturn the election results, which could trigger a new wave of political violence,” said Alex Main, CEPR’s director of international policy who was in Brazil for the elections. “The Trump administration, which has close relations with the Bolsonaro family, could help defuse this threat by joining other governments in recognizing the election outcome.”

Trump, who hosted Bolsonaro at the White House in May, has yet to comment on the Brazilian election results, as of this writing. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose department led the effort to tilt the election in Bolsonaro’s favor, has also not publicly commented on Sunday’s results.

Mark Weisbrot, CEPR’s co-director, called Lula’s win “a victory for democracy and independence in the Americas against the massive intervention from the Trump administration in favor of the Bolsonaro team.”

“This included politically driven tariffs and other efforts to influence the campaign,” said Weisbrot. “Trump also tried to stop the trial of Jair Bolsonaro, who — like Trump — refused to accept his defeat in a presidential election, and was convicted of attempting a coup d’état and attempted violent abolition of the democratic rule of law.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Wendi C. Thomas
title: Man Who Spent Years Undermining Voters’ Interests May Win Newly Drawn District
content:
Tennessee congressional candidate Brent Taylor has taken steps to strip authority from elected local officials.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Not two weeks after the Tennessee legislature carved Memphis into three congressional districts this spring, in a move designed to eliminate Democratic representation, Republican state Sen. Brent Taylor made his electoral expectations clear in a photo posted on social media.

Taylor and U.S. Rep. Tim Burchett, a fellow Republican, sat side by side on the U.S. Capitol steps. “My friend Tim Burchett showing me the dadgum ropes,” Taylor wrote in a Facebook post.

On May 7, the same day that the new districts were approved, Taylor had announced his bid to represent the redrawn Congressional District 9, which for more than four decades had stood as the state’s sole majority Black district. During that time, it covered mostly the Memphis area; it now stretches across half the state and is majority white.

Taylor, 58, already has a track record with many of the voters he is now seeking to represent in Washington, D. C.: In his nearly four years as a state senator, he has taken steps to strip authority from local officials elected by many of those same voters. With the backing of a Republican supermajority, Taylor, who is white, pushed through half a dozen laws that superseded the power and priorities of local politicians.

Around the country, state legislatures from both parties have used preemption laws to control local governments. That tactic has been embraced by Republican-dominated statehouses in recent years as a way to restrict the ability of Democratic-led cities to enact policies state leaders disagree with, including protections for civil rights, public health and workers.

Memphis has long struggled with high rates of violent crime that have begun to fall only in the last couple of years. This is where Taylor focused his legislative efforts. He led the charge to prohibit judges from considering a defendant’s ability to pay when making bail decisions. He has tried to oust Steve Mulroy, the first Democrat elected as Shelby County district attorney in 25 years, and pushed through legislation authorizing the state to review every decision made by his office. And he co-sponsored a law that voided the Memphis City Council’s ban on police stops for minor traffic infractions, which had been passed after the 2023 beating death of Black motorist Tyré Nichols.

The question of how to keep communities safe has drawn divergent political approaches in Memphis — from Mulroy’s focus on rehabilitation as part of his effort to lower violent crime, to Taylor’s emphasis on aggressive prosecution and incarceration. Those approaches can mean very different experiences for the people of Memphis, which makes up most of Shelby County. Some elected officials and criminal justice experts warn that the laws Taylor has championed will embolden police to detain drivers without justification and the criminal justice system to lock up more people for longer periods in the already overcrowded county jail, where more than 65 people have died since 2018.

“I think he’s very dangerous for Shelby County, and he’s going to be very dangerous for the Ninth District if he gets elected,” said former Shelby County General Sessions Court Judge Bill Anderson, referring to how Taylor’s policies could especially harm Black men. Anderson retired in May 2025 after clashing publicly with Taylor over bail reform measures. (Anderson supported them; Taylor opposed them.)

Taylor is favored to win because of redistricting by Tennessee Republicans after a U.S. Supreme Court ruling in April made it harder to challenge gerrymandering that dilutes the Black vote. The Mississippi native, who lives in an antebellum-style mansion in a tiny and heavily white community east of Memphis, has loaned his congressional campaign $1.5 million. The candidate made millions after selling his funeral home businesses to a private equity firm.

Taylor’s opponent is state Rep. Justin J. Pearson, a 31-year-old Black Democrat who has taken a very different approach to what the district needs. Pearson has called for addressing the root causes of crime by improving schools and economic opportunities instead of a singular focus on incarceration. title: Un saut du tigre dans le passé
content:
« Quelle horrrreueur ! » - propos transi d'un bourgeois des beaux quartiers de Limoges, au soir du 17 octobre 2026, face au panache flamboyant de l'Hôtel de Ville en train de partir en fumée, au terme d'un assaut mémorable de la plèbe insurgée – refrain de la Marseillaise en prime – contre ce monument


d'arrogance autant que de vanité, héritage infâme d'une III

e

 République ayant piétiné les cadavres de la Commune, foulé le sang des colonies, adoubé le régime de la Collaboration.


De cris d'orfraie en hurlements, de boursouflures outragées en petites vertus effarouchées, de condamnations morales en compulsions de haine,

la France a peur

 : c'est que l'Histoire n'a pas dit son dernier mot, dont cet octobre en flammes figure déjà comme un retour ardent.


Car c'est bien à Limoges que les émeutes du pain de septembre 1791, qui ont aussi lieu dans d'autres villes, préludent au soulèvement local du 27 février 1792, au cours duquel les ouvriers en armes envahissent la salle du conseil municipal. Accusé à raison d'affamer la population, par un détournement calculé du blé destiné aux habitants, Naurissart, le maire de l'époque, prend bientôt la fuite.


C'est à Limoges, dans le contexte consécutif aux journées révolutionnaires de février 1848 (qui mettent fin à la Monarchie de Juillet et portent au pouvoir une bourgeoisie républicaine s'empressant d'écraser les révoltes ouvrières de juin), qu'une Garde populaire, appuyée par une foule d'ouvriers rejoints pour l'occasion par le peuple insoumis des ponts de Vienne (les Ponticauds), marche le 27 avril sur la mairie, défendue par une Garde bourgeoise finalement désarmée par la foule au corps-à-corps. Le matin même, ses canons avaient été renversés au Champ de Juillet. À la faveur du pillage bienvenu de plusieurs armureries de la ville, la Préfecture est également envahie. Préfiguration éphémère d'un véritable pouvoir ouvrier, un Comité provisoire est constitué. Prise de panique, la bourgeoise se fait la malle.


Après celle de Paris, en vigueur depuis le 18 mars 1871, mais aussi celles de Marseille ou de Lyon, c'est encore à Limoges, le 4 avril, que la Commune est proclamée. Commune d'un jour, qui débute par l'insoumission de soldats refusant de rejoindre les troupes versaillaises qui assiègent Paris. Une mutinerie éclate, qu'amplifie et prolonge une révolte ouvrière au cours de laquelle s'enchaînent la prise de l'hôtel de ville, la mort de Billet (colonel qui avait eu l'outrecuidance d'ordonner à la troupe de dégainer le sabre) et l'assaut nocturne sur la Préfecture, dont le locataire s'enfuit, déguisé en… ouvrier !


C'est toujours à Limoges, en avril-mai 1905, que le prolétariat en lutte (bas salaires, mauvaises conditions de travail, arbitraire et sexisme des contremaîtres) déclenche une grève générale insurrectionnelle d'ampleur. Outre de nombreuses barricades et le pillage désormais traditionnel de quelques armureries, une bombe est posée devant la résidence du grand patron local de l'industrie porcelainière d'alors, Théodore Haviland, dont l'automobile est bientôt incendiée tandis que les usines sont prises d'assaut, leurs portes enfoncées, les ateliers saccagés. Le 17 avril, les insurgé.es affrontent avec détermination les charges meurtrières de la cavalerie – au cours desquelles le jeune Camille Vardelle, ouvrier porcelainier de 20 ans, est tué par balles – suite à l'attaque de la prison où sont enfermés plusieurs grévistes que le préfet refuse de libérer.


À l'époque enfoncée à l'aide d'un bélier improvisé, la porte d'entrée ainsi qu'un pan non négligeable du mur d'enceinte de la prison de Limoges se verront à nouveau célébrés comme il se doit sous les coups de boutoir généreux d'une tractopelle, dérobée sur un chantier voisin, dans la nuit de Noël 1974...

author: Mitch Stoltz
title: Anti-Circumvention Laws Raise the Cost of Knowledge
content:
The vast amount of information on the open web requires researchers and journalists to adapt with new tools to make sense of it all. Checking facts, gauging public opinion, and other lines of inquiry depend on being able to analyze the overwhelming amount of material posted online every day. Unfortunately, responding to the AI industry’s voracious appetite for data, companies stewarding this public data are looking to cash in and block access to the open web. This makes the web harder to navigate, and threatens all kinds of important research.


Reddit’s

lawsuit

 against SerpAPI and Perplexity threatens to do exactly that.


Reddit was once a very open platform, fostering a community of alternative apps and extensions putting users in control of their experience. Since the rise of AI however, it changed tack. Over the last three years Reddit has

closed APIs to users

, limited

UI features

, and otherwise restrained access

without login

. By making the voices on the platform harder to access, the company has positioned itself as a gatekeeper, and has since struck a lucrative data-sharing arrangement with Google.


SerpAPI, in contrast, is a tool which offers automated access to Google’s search engine results pages. It’s used by Perplexity, an AI-based search tool. Reddit sued to stop SerpAPI and Perplexity from bypassing Reddit’s own arrangement with Google. (Google brought a similar suit, which was dismissed by another court.)


It comes as little surprise that the legal weapon Reddit employed in this case is Section 1201 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, the same “anti-circumvention” law that has caused so much trouble for artists, innovators, and researchers over the years—and that EFF has fought against from the beginning. Reddit’s suit claimed that SerpAPI’s use of widely used techniques to access Google search results amounted to “circumventing” access controls on copyrighted works. 


There are major problems with this argument. 


First, Reddit doesn’t own the copyright in its users’ posts—the users do, and they grant Reddit the right to distribute the posted content freely.


Second, there’s no meaningful copyright infringement going on here. Perplexity functions like a search engine, responding to users’ queries with relevant links and optionally an AI-generated summary. Crawling and indexing the web to create a search engine was long ago ruled a fair use under copyright law.


And third, Google’s efforts to put rate limits on search queries and block some kinds of automated querying aren’t the sort of “access controls” that Section 1201 was written for. The law was passed in 1998 and targeted things like breaking the encryption on DVDs and other digital media. In contrast to physical or paywalled media, Reddit posts are visible to everyone, without a paywall and generally without a login. 


Unfortunately, a federal district judge

ruled

 in July that the suit could proceed, concluding that Section 1201 applied. That’s a dangerous ruling, because it casts a cloud of legal uncertainty over lots of important research, including efforts to study public sentiment through social media and to preserve records of historical events. Without tools that can look at the web at scale, many kinds of research are simply impossible today. But if employing those tools risks Section 1201 liability, only the wealthiest institutions will be able to use them.


We cannot let the internet be rebuilt such that information is divided up among a handful of gatekeepers and sold back to us like cable subscription packages. If our knowledge of the online world comes only through wealthy institutions, the cost of knowledge will only increase and access to unbiased answers diminishes.

title: Familias desplazadas en Cisjordania bajo un escenario idéntico al de Gaza: 260 hogares evacuados en una noche
content:
Según nos informan miembros del Sindicato de Trabajadores Postales de Palestina, las autoridades han iniciado el desplazamiento forzoso de familias replicando el modus operandi empleado en Gaza, según denuncian los afectados. En la última noche, 260 familias fueron obligadas a abandonar sus hogares sin destino conocido, mientras continúan las demoliciones de viviendas, empresas, industrias y edificios.


Desde ayer, se han comenzado a desplazar familias en Cisjordania utilizando el mismo método brutal aplicado anteriormente en Gaza. Los afectados advierten de que podrían quedarse sin ningún refugio en muy poco tiempo.


Las demoliciones han comenzado: casas, empresas, industrias y edificios están siendo derribados. En la noche del sábado, 260 familias fueron desplazadas tras recibir la instrucción de abandonar sus viviendas, sin que se les haya comunicado cuál será su destino final, que permanece completamente incierto.


Los afectados denuncian que la situación se agrava por el contexto electoral: las elecciones en Israel se celebran en pocos días y los políticos estarían explotando el sufrimiento de la población para obtener rédito electoral.


Ante esta situación, los desplazados hacen un llamamiento urgente a los medios de comunicación para que cubran la crisis antes de que la ciudad se convierta en la próxima Gaza.


Sin moral. Sin piedad. No dejan nada en pie, concluyen.


Desde CNT llamamos a todo el mundo a difundir esta noticia.

author: Rubén Morvolution
title: No son solo disturbios: escuchar a la juventud de Barcelona
content:
No son solo disturbios: escuchar a la juventud de Barcelona


La protesta juvenil del 24 de octubre revela un malestar que no puede reducirse al vandalismo. Detrás de algunas de sus expresiones aparecen la crisis educativa, la precariedad laboral y la pérdida de confianza en el futuro.


Rubén Morvolution — Trabajador industrial


El pasado 24 de octubre, una convocatoria juvenil difundida a través de las redes sociales reunió a un gran número de estudiantes, principalmente de instituto, en el centro de Barcelona. Bajo referencias como

Instituts Indignats

 y

Blocus

, inspiradas en las movilizaciones estudiantiles francesas, la jornada terminó con enfrentamientos con la policía, incendios, destrozos y saqueos de comercios. La respuesta institucional no tardó en situar los acontecimientos en el terreno del orden público.


Los hechos no necesitan ser minimizados. Pero reducir lo sucedido a una gamberrada colectiva tampoco permite comprenderlo. Entre las imágenes de los disturbios han circulado entrevistas a participantes que expresan preocupaciones bastante más concretas que el simple deseo de provocar altercados. La presencia de chicas entre quienes participaron en los acontecimientos y entre las personas detenidas recuerda, además, que no estamos hablando de un fenómeno exclusivamente masculino.


Preguntadas por sus motivos, algunas de estas personas jóvenes denuncian el estado de las aulas, critican al profesorado y al Gobierno y hablan de la falta de futuro. Cuando una periodista les pregunta si están allí por la educación, responden afirmativamente. Una de las intervenciones resume la frustración con una frase especialmente significativa: para conseguir trabajo necesitas un título, pero después puedes acabar cobrando 1.500 euros. La conclusión es un rechazo airado al valor de esa titulación.


La cifra no es casual. Los 1.500 euros se han convertido en una referencia habitual al hablar de los salarios modestos en España. Un sueldo que puede parecer aceptable sobre el papel, pero que, una vez descontados el alquiler, los suministros, la alimentación y el transporte, difícilmente permite a muchas personas jóvenes emanciparse y construir una vida independiente. La cuestión no es únicamente cuánto se cobra, sino qué condiciones de vida permite sostener ese salario.


No estamos ante un análisis económico elaborado, pero tampoco ante palabras carentes de contenido social.


Una promesa que pierde credibilidad


Durante décadas, estudiar, obtener una titulación y acceder al empleo se presentó como el camino hacia una vida mejor. La educación debía permitir el ascenso social; el trabajo, proporcionar independencia económica; y el salario, abrir la puerta a una vivienda y cierta estabilidad.


Esa promesa nunca se cumplió por igual para toda la población, pero desempeñó un papel fundamental en la integración de amplios sectores de la clase trabajadora.


Lo que expresan estas voces juveniles es la pérdida de confianza en esa relación entre esfuerzo y recompensa. Se les exige prepararse, competir y acumular credenciales, mientras anticipan empleos precarios, salarios insuficientes y dificultades para emanciparse.


Los 1.500 euros mencionados en la entrevista no constituyen una predicción sobre el futuro de quienes protestan ni un cálculo preciso de sus necesidades. Expresan una percepción social reconocible: incluso cumpliendo las exigencias del sistema educativo y consiguiendo un empleo, puede resultar imposible alcanzar la autonomía material que se les había prometido.


Y quizá lo más significativo sea su edad. Buena parte de esta juventud todavía no ha tenido una experiencia laboral prolongada, pero ya imagina su futuro dentro del mundo del trabajo en términos de precariedad. La inseguridad no aparece únicamente después de incorporarse al empleo: comienza a formar parte de sus expectativas durante la adolescencia.


Una rabia que también contiene contradicciones


El malestar no se expresa necesariamente de manera coherente. Quienes denuncian las condiciones de la educación pública pueden dirigir también su enfado contra el profesorado, que padece problemas laborales y organizativos dentro del propio sistema educativo.


Esa contradicción merece ser comprendida, no utilizada para desacreditar a quienes protestan.


Desde la posición del alumnado, el profesorado puede representar la autoridad inmediata, las exigencias académicas y una institución que no responde a sus expectativas. Desde la posición de las …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Brasil y cómo romper la estadística: Una victoria contra los pronósticos
content:
El domingo 25 de octubre se llevó a cabo la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales en Brasil. El escenario era complejo para Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva: había quedado segundo en la primera vuelta, con casi dos puntos porcentuales menos que su adversario, Flávio Bolsonaro.


Desde Brasil, Lucrecia Fernández para Red Eco Alternativo


Sin embargo, el pueblo brasileño hizo historia. Lula revirtió el resultado y obtuvo el 51,79 % de los votos válidos, frente al 48,21 % de Bolsonaro. Una diferencia de 3,58 puntos porcentuales que le permitió acceder a su cuarto mandato presidencial, en una elección que rompió una tendencia histórica de casi cuatro décadas.


El resultado fue más que una victoria electoral. En las calles, en las redes sociales y en las urnas, millones de brasileños participaron de una disputa que excedió los nombres de los candidatos: estaba en juego el modelo político de país y su lugar en América Latina. Pero una remontada de estas características no se construye en soledad. Reducir la figura de Lula sería dejar afuera uno de los aspectos más significativos de esta elección: la movilización popular que se desplegó durante las semanas previas al balotaje.


Un logro histórico: dar vuelta la estadística


Los números permiten dimensionar la magnitud de la remontada. En la primera vuelta, celebrada el 4 de octubre, Flávio Bolsonaro había obtenido el 47,03 % de los votos válidos, frente al 45,16 % de Lula. La diferencia era de 1,87 puntos porcentuales, equivalente a más de 2,2 millones de votos.


Tres semanas después, el resultado se invirtió. Lula alcanzó el 51,79 % y Bolsonaro quedó en el 48,21 %. El presidente reelecto no solo recuperó la diferencia inicial: terminó imponiéndose por más de cuatro millones de votos.


La relevancia histórica es indiscutible. Desde el retorno de las elecciones presidenciales directas en 1989, ningún candidato que hubiera terminado segundo en la primera vuelta había conseguido ganar el balotaje. Lula se convirtió en el primero en lograrlo.


Pero una remontada de estas características no se construye en soledad. Y reducirla a la figura de Lula sería dejar afuera uno de los aspectos más significativos de esta elección: que el pueblo brasilero se movilizó en las calles desde que se conoció que el 25 de octubre habría segunda vuelta.


Unidos frente al horror


El pueblo brasileño salió a las calles con banderas, remeras, carteles y consignas. Personas de distintas edades, sectores sociales y expresiones de género se hicieron presentes en los espacios públicos, manifestaron su apoyo a Lula y expresaron, al mismo tiempo, su rechazo a lo que representaba la candidatura de Bolsonaro.


La movilización tuvo una dimensión que excedió los actos partidarios. Hubo quienes organizaron concentraciones, quienes compartieron mensajes en las redes sociales, quienes impulsaron campañas digitales y quienes buscaron convencer a familiares, amigos y vecinos de la importancia de acudir a las urnas. La elección se convirtió en una conversación colectiva que atravesó la vida cotidiana.


En ese escenario, el voto dejó de ser únicamente una adhesión a un candidato para convertirse, también, en una forma de expresar qué país no se quería.


No se trataba simplemente de una disputa binaria entre Lula y Bolsonaro. Para una parte de quienes se movilizaron, la elección representaba la posibilidad de poner un límite al avance de una derecha que identificaban con el retroceso de derechos, el cuestionamiento de las políticas sociales, el racismo, la violencia contra las mujeres y los ataques a la educación y la salud públicas.


La consigna de no permitir el regreso del bolsonarismo funcionó como un punto de encuentro entre sectores que no necesariamente compartían todas sus posiciones políticas. La defensa de la democracia, de los derechos conquistados y de la soberanía nacional fue capaz de articular demandas diversas alrededor de un objetivo común.


El sur de Brasil: salir a la calle donde parecía imposible


El sur de Brasil fue uno de los territorios más desafiantes para la campaña de Lula. En estados como Santa Catarina y Paraná, Flávio Bolsonaro había conseguido ventajas importantes en la primera vuelta. Sin embargo, esa correlación electoral no impidió que sectores de la población salieran a las calles para expresar su apoyo al presidente Lula y defender el proyecto político que representaba.


La movilización tuvo un valor particular en una región donde el bolsonarismo conserva una …

author: Rob Smith
title: The Horror: The history of smallpox in B.C.
content:
What would it take to do something so evil as to spread a deadly disease on purpose? For descendants of survivors of a catastrophic smallpox epidemic it’s an easy answer. Greed.


“If they took out the occupying nation, then they could do what they wanted with the land. They could own the land,” Skip Gregg told APTN Investigates.


Gregg knows the story. It’s been passed down through the generation in Tsilhqot’in territory.


“Oral history of our people is like, yes, it was threatened to us. If you don’t give us our land or do what we want you to do, we’ll bring in smallpox,” he said.


In the 1860s, officials in a brand-new colonial government in Victoria had visions of connecting two roads from British Columbia’s coast to its interior. Gold had been discovered. There had also been various proposals for a rail link to the pacific as early as the 1840s.


Author Tom Swanky puts it this way.


“Doing the Bentinck Arm Road and the people doing the Bute Inlet Road, they have in mind they’re going to make fortunes from being the first people on the ground in the great Northwest Passage by land,” he said.


In his book The True Story of Canada’s War of Extermination on the Pacific, Swanky wrote that Bentinck Arm company director Ranald McDonald was on the Brother Jonathan when it docked in Victoria in March 1862.


The same ship carried passengers sick with smallpox. A coincidence perhaps. But Swanky pointed out, McDonald met the Francis Poole expedition in Bella Coola.


More on Poole in a moment, but first Swanky told APTN this about McDonald.


“He would have been one of the greatest beneficiaries, private beneficiaries, for his partnership in the Bentick Arm Road,” Swanky said.


In Victoria, the disease quickly spread amongst the surrounding First Nation encampments and villages. The city was known for racial strife, informal segregation and discrimination.


How did a single passenger just off the boat come into contact with anyone in the encampments?


“We have the record of a diarist with the Tsimshian. And he said that it was a big snowstorm on the day that smallpox arrived,” he said.


“The Tsimshian and the Haida, they were engaged in a series of drunken brawls. You have to imagine that this innocent man from San Francisco got off the boat, and on his way to Victoria, wandered into a native village where there’s violence going on.”


Dr. John Helmken was the colony’s top physician as well as the speaker of the Legislative Assembly. He was also married to governor Douglas’ daughter. Helmken claimed to have vaccinated over 500 Indigenous people


“The American newspapers immediately reported that those people broke out with the disease. They had smallpox, so that’s evidence of an inoculation program,” said Swanky.


Smallpox spread through the encampments. Up to 1,500 people died. The sick, along with the healthy, were expelled from Victoriam forced to go home to infect their communities.


This is an unexplained departure from previous epidemic responses. In the coastal communities, 20, 000 people died.


The Nuxalk from Bella Coola and the Tsilhqot’in were not present in Victoria.


In May of 1862, Francis Poole left Victoria on a mining expedition. He left with 25 men, many carrying the disease. Along the way, it was reported that Poole left sick men behind, two at a time, in Nanaimo, Fort Rupert, Bella Coola, and then into Tsilhqot’in territory at the villages of Nautileff and Chilcotin Lake


Gregg said the party left a trail of death along the way.


“At Chilcotin Lake, all but an Elder and a small child [died].”


There is no official death toll, but the Tsilhqot’in estimate it’s in the thousands. At least 500 died at Chilcotin Lake alone.


Poole would return to Victoria in July. Apparently having not visited any mining sites. He would have a private meeting with governor Douglas.


During his research for his books, Swanky found the official record during the time period had been altered. The minutes are missing.


“It implicates every member of Douglas’s executive council. None of them can break ranks, because they’re all implicated,” he said.


Swanky said his books lay out the case for mass murder.


But is his evidence compelling? There is not much support in academic circles.


“The issue of how the Crown came to govern British Columbia is never addressed. The academic community’s interest is in creating a narrative to justify the Crown’s presence. You have this phenomenon of colonialism, where you …

author: dev
title: Cinéastes de notre temps
content:
Le 17 octobre, on a vu refleurir des barricades sur les Champs-Elysées et des groupes d'insurgés portant le gilet fluo ont à nouveau envahi le pays. La France a été marqué par ce soulèvement légendaire et le mouvement en cours s'inspire de ces codes et de ces pratiques pour se renforcer. Les Gilets Jaunes, qui ont su faire trembler le pouvoir, hantent les consciences et les imaginaires de la jeunesse qui prend aujourd'hui la rue et la parole. Pour ce deuxième épisode de

Cinéastes de notre temps

 nous passerons

BoumBoum

 de Laurie Lassalle (2022).


Il est parfois difficile d'extraire ce qui mérite d'être vu parmi les milliers de productions cinématographiques dont nous sommes abreuvés. Les films sont jetables comme n'importe quelles autres marchandises. Le cinéma peut être une place forte contre le spectacle seulement si nous sommes en mesure de défendre une culture critique.


« Je voudrais que

Cinéastes de notre temps

 soit une émission de laboratoire pour la création d'un nouveau langage ... Pour moi, cette émission poursuit un ensemble de réflexions sur le matériau filmique et sur la manière dont le sens peut ou non s'en emparer ».


(André S. Labarthe.

Cinéma 69

, 140, novembre 1969.)


Régulièrement, nous proposerons sur

lundimatin

des films


gratuits et en streaming pendant une semaine,


accompagnés d'un entretien avec leurs cinéastes.


« L'idée était de mettre un réalisateur face à un autre réalisateur, qu'il soit mort ou vivant – même si on s'est vite aperçus que la rencontre avec les vivants présentait un plus vif intérêt. » (

Entretiens avec André S. Labarthe,

Thierry Lounas, 2011)


Notre époque est riche en soulèvements, en bouleversements, en évènements. Elle se caractérise par la mise en images et en sons, en cinéma, de ceux-ci. Nous irons à la rencontre des cinéastes qui ont été fidèles à un événement et qui ont fait du cinéma un lieu de son expression. Nous chercherons des films qui vont vers la rencontre et le dehors. Un cinéma dans lequel la vie se multiplie et qui invente de nouveaux désirs.


A rebours de la tyrannie de l'actualité et de la publicité, mais aussi contre toute nostalgie, nous essayerons de proposer ici une sélection de films « actuels » qui font l'épreuve du temps. C'est à dire que par leur puissance visionnaire, nous parions qu'ils ne s'useront pas.


Episode 2 : BoumBoum de Laurie Lassalle (2022)


Pendant les Gilets Jaunes à Paris, Laurie et Pierrot tombent amoureux. Ils filment ensemble la révolte populaire et les personnes qui, comme eux, y sont engagés. «


Nos corps se mêlent à des milliers d'autres qui expriment leur colère dans la rue tous les samedis, des mois durant. » Le film est fait de ce tissu-là : des inconnus fédérés autour d'un désir de l'autre, d'un désir des autres et autour d'un désir de changement, d'une ouverture des possibles. Le tout entremêlé et sous une pluie de grenades. Boum, Boum : comment vivre l'amour libre et comment faire la révolution ? Réinventer l'amour, changer le régime, surmonter les blessures aussi bien psychiques que physiques. Leur histoire va se construire au cœur d'un soulèvement, leur entente en suivre l'intensité et les remous.

BoumBoum

 c'est l'histoire d'un amour et d'une insurrection.


Episode 1 : L'Époque, toujours en ligne

A venir lundi prochain :


Entretien croisé - Matthieu Bareyre & Laurie Lassalle


Pour toutes propositions, écrire à

dimanchepm@riseup.net

author: dev
title: « Cher·es collègues, il va falloir cesser d'être respectables... »
content:
En attendant le « reprise des cours », des professeurs du secondaire ont réuni ces quelques réflexions quant à l'ambiguïté à laquelle les accule leur "statut" et au chantage exercé par l'institution qui les retourne

de facto

 contre le mouvement.


« L'agent public doit se conformer aux instructions de son supérieur hiérarchique, sauf dans le cas où l'ordre donné est manifestement illégal et de nature à compromettre gravement un intérêt public. »


Code général de la fonction publique (article L121-10)


1.

Non, ce n'est pas « leur » mouvement : le mouvement des lycéens, en ce qu'il concorde précisément avec nos revendications, est aussi le nôtre. Il faut donc s'en sentir partie intégrante et se demander : que nous faut-il faire pour contribuer à faire triompher notre mouvement ?


2.

 D'abord, reconnaitre une chose : les lycéen

·

nes ont réussi là où les professeur

·

es ont échoué. Notre profession, corporatiste et « bonne élève » est si soucieuse d'être constructive et respectable qu'il y a bien longtemps qu'elle n'est plus prise au sérieux. Après des années de mobilisations de personnels de l'éducation, qui se sont révélées pour la plupart perdantes, car elles cherchaient à rester crédibles aux yeux du gouvernement, le mouvement lycéen nous met face à nous-mêmes : allons-nous, cette fois encore, rester respectables ?


3.

Rester « respectables », c'est persister à « remplir notre mission » comme si de rien n'était. Ne surtout pas déroger à nos « obligations légales » : la place d'un

·

e professeur

·

e est dans sa salle de classe, n'est-ce pas ? et puisque certain

·

es élèves veulent faire cours, quel

·

le professeur

·

e serais-je si je ne les prenais pas ? C'est se persuader que sa place n'est pas dehors, avec les élèves qui bloquent, mais bien dedans, derrière la vitre, derrière la grille – il ne s'agirait pas de cautionner, par notre présence, des tirs de mortier ou des poubelles brûlées. C'est recommencer à placer des évaluations dès que l'occasion se présente parce qu'il faut bien les évaluer, les élèves…


4.

 Si nous sommes autant à être tenté

·

es par la respectabilité, c'est que, au-delà de la position de supériorité morale qu'elle semble nous conférer, le chantage de l'institution est fort. Cette période révèle en effet avec cruauté ce que cette dernière attend réellement de nous, ce pour quoi nous sommes réellement payé

·

es : mettre des notes. Au-delà de nos envies si légitimes de retrouver nos élèves, de faire cours, de leur transmettre nos savoirs, telle est, in fine, notre crainte : ne pas pouvoir les évaluer. Même si nous savons qu'y procéder sans faire cours, sans passer du temps avec elleux, sans les préparer n'a pas de sens, nous persistons à vouloir le faire ; car l'absence de sens nous semble encore moins pire que le sentiment de les abandonner. Pris

·

es en tenaille par ces injonctions absurdes et culpabilisantes, dès lors que nous glissons dans un soutien marqué au mouvement, nous voilà réduit

·

es par les discours des proviseur

·

es, des médias des milliardaires, de certains parents et du gouvernement à la position intenable d'être des traîtres à la mission de l'école. Professeur

·

es soutenant les blocus, nous serions des opportunistes ou bien des fainéant

·

es, des gauchistes cherchant à « manipuler les élèves ». Tous les jours où nous déciderons de débrayer, de nous mettre en grève, de soutenir les élèves face à la police, quelque bon serviteur zélé de l'institution sera là pour nous rappeler quelle est notre place, sans se gêner de nous rendre moralement responsables des « débordements ».


5.

 Reconnaissons-le : l'institution, par le biais de ses directions d'établissement, exploite notre attachement à notre travail pour faire de nous, malgré nous, derrière la police, des agent

·

es de la casse du mouvement.


6.

 Mais la vérité, c'est que, si nous soulageons temporairement notre conscience professorale en programmant des évaluations ou en donnant du travail aux élèves pour « rattraper le temps perdu », ce même geste ne viendra jamais soulager notre conscience d'avoir vu nos élèves se faire gazer, matraquer, se faire mettre en joue, courser, charger, renverser, mutiler, interpeler, enfermer, insulter, brutaliser par la police de l'État. Il ne viendra pas effacer dans nos mémoires l'image des visages de nos élèves, de 14 ans, 15 ans, 16 ans, en pleurs, en rage, décontenancés, choqués, tout rouges et boursouflés du gaz, les bleus, les doigts, pieds …

author: Daron Letts
title: Horror writer Jamesie Fournier shares scares in print and on screen
content:
Horror author Jamesie Fournier says he enjoys scaring children almost as much as they enjoy being scared.


“It’s very entertaining to be terrified,” he said Saturday in an interview in his Inhabit Media office in Iqaluit. “That’s why we love horror.”


The Inuktitut and English writer had just launched his latest children’s book,

 Lemming’s First Halloween

, earlier that day at Nunatta Sunakkutaangit Museum.


Dozens of costumed children and their families dropped by the event to create creepy crafts and hear spooky stories.


The book is Fournier’s second in the series. He published

Lemming’s First Christmas

 in English and Inuktitut in 2024.

Lemming’s First Halloween

marks Fournier’s first collaboration with Toronto-based Pakistani-Canadian illustrator Faiza Khan.


The tale follows Lemming and her pup as they cross paths with a qallupilluk, a monster known to drag children into the ocean.


Overcoming fear is an important life skill that Inuit horror stories tap into, Fournier said.


“When you’re afraid you’re aware of your surroundings. You’re taking everything in. You’re being very cautious. Survivalism has kicked in,” he said. “To be brave we have to first know what scares us.”


Scary fiction help children remember life lessons that can help keep them safe, such as to stay away from sea ice when a trusted adult is not near.


“Once we’re afraid and we’re informed of how we can be safe, we are able to problem-solve,” Fournier said. “That skill translates to every facet of life.”


Children enjoy repeating memorable nightmarish narratives as well, Fournier has noticed.


“Whenever I read to children, they all want to tell me their stories, too,” he said.


Fournier added he can relate to that urge, as he was the same way as a child in Yellowknife.


He would devour

Batman

 comics and

Tales From the Crypt

magazines over breakfast with his dad. He also listened with keen attention at bedtime when his mom shared monstrous Inuit legends.


Throughout his career, Fournier has revisited those childhood frights in print and on the screen.


His work

appeared

 in

Taaqtumi 2:

 An Anthology of Arctic Horror Stories

, released by Inhabit Media in 2025.


This year, his award-winning 2022

novel

 

The Other Ones

 was made into a 19-minute short film by Inhabit Media’s sister company, Taqqut Productions, in collaboration with Toronto-based Stop Motion Department.


That story follows a mother and daughter as they’re pursued by the wrath of an ancient terror, eerily animated by stop-motion and claymation puppets.


An ancient terror stalks a mother and daughter in

The Other Ones

, a new stop-motion short film written and co-directed by Jamesie Fournier. (Image courtesy of Taqqut Productions)


Fournier co-directed the film with Taqqut producer Danny Christopher.


It’s making the rounds of the Canadian film festival circuit this fall and winter after premièring at the Ottawa International Animation Festival last month.


The Other Ones

 is scheduled to screen at Iqaluit’s Astro Theatre at 7:30 p.m. Tuesday as part of Inhabit Media’s

Alianaqtut: A Night of Inuit Horror

 film series, alongside five other Inuktitut films released by Taqqut.


Tickets are free on a first-come basis, and all ages are welcome.


— With files from Lilli Akpaleeapik

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Defender el agua es defender la vida”
content:
Del 21 al 23 de noviembre se realizará en Traslasierra, Córdoba, la 7.ª Cumbre Plurinacional en Defensa del Agua para los Pueblos de Abya Yala, un encuentro que reunirá a asambleas, pueblos originarios y organizaciones de distintos territorios para compartir experiencias y fortalecer las luchas en defensa del agua y los bienes comunes.


Por Adrián Flores para Red Eco


En esta entrevista con Red Eco, Juan Manuel Izzo reconocido activista ambiental de la provincia y uno de los organizadores de la cumbre en Córdoba, analiza los conflictos socioambientales, cuestiona el avance del modelo extractivo y destaca la importancia de la organización colectiva. También convoca a quienes todavía no se han involucrado a acercarse y participar en la defensa de la vida y los territorios.


¿Por qué se eligió Córdoba y, particularmente, Traslasierra para realizar esta nueva cumbre?


La elección del territorio para la siguiente cumbre se realiza al cierre del encuentro anterior, entre quienes participan.


Córdoba forma parte de un territorio avasallado por el modelo extractivo. Aquí confluyen diversas problemáticas: el agronegocio y su contaminación, los desmontes y el desarraigo de las comunidades, el riesgo de que una minería presentada como de bajo impacto se transforme en una actividad de alto impacto cuando la demanda es excesiva, y un territorio castigado por grandes incendios, con los negociados que se esconden detrás.


También hay industrias que ponen en riesgo a la población de la propia capital, como el caso de Porta. A esto se suma la producción destinada a satisfacer la demanda de alimentos para ganado de mercados muy lejanos. Es el caso de Fondo Monte, que propicia una demanda de agua subterránea fuera de control y pone en riesgo los acuíferos.


Tenemos un gobierno que promociona la ecología en la publicidad, pero cuya práctica contradice ese discurso. Córdoba también forma parte del plan IIRSA y hay ciudadanos procesados judicialmente por defender la vida.


Estas y otras problemáticas son parte de los conflictos que se analizan y trabajan desde hace años en las cumbres. Por estos motivos se eligió Córdoba y, puntualmente, Traslasierra: porque estaban dadas las condiciones.


¿Cuáles son las principales problemáticas que tenemos con el agua en Córdoba y en el país? ¿Qué papel juegan los intereses económicos y los gobiernos?


El agua es un elemento fundamental, no solo para la vida, sino también para desarrollar cualquier actividad económica. Por eso está en disputa.


Córdoba está sofocada de conflictos. El negocio inmobiliario, por sí solo, está desbaratando ecosistemas y contaminando cauces y espejos de agua. El país atraviesa una realidad similar, aunque cada territorio tiene sus propios conflictos: minería, agronegocio, hidrocarburos, explotación offshore, litio y otras actividades que multiplican las zonas de sacrificio.


Desde la geopolítica internacional se nos asigna el papel de proveedores de materias primas, es decir, de bienes naturales. Toda la región de Abya Yala carga con ese estigma.


En cuanto a los gobiernos, considero que todos han sido funcionales a este modelo. Se pueden advertir diferencias en la contención social, el acceso al consumo y algunos esbozos de soberanía, pero estamos muy lejos de encontrar soluciones reales.


Frente a esta realidad, los pueblos se organizan y buscan soluciones de forma horizontal y participativa. La cumbre es un ejemplo de ello.


¿Por qué defender el agua es también defender nuestros territorios y los bienes comunes?


La lucha por la protección del agua es, simplemente, la defensa de la vida, de todas las vidas. Pensar el ambiente como algo lejano es un acto de ignorancia terrible. Siempre intentamos plantear que los conflictos no son solamente ambientales, sino socioambientales, porque tienen que ver con las acciones y omisiones de una sociedad.


El agua, además de ser dadora de vida, es necesaria para llevar adelante cualquier actividad productiva. Por eso, la propia demanda genera conflictos. Y si agregamos que el agua es un medio natural de transporte de sustancias, nos encontramos con que gran parte de nuestros espejos de agua están contaminados.


El cuidado del agua debería ser una de las prioridades de la agenda de las políticas públicas.


¿Qué importancia tiene encontrarse con otras asambleas, pueblos originarios y organizaciones para compartir experiencias y fortalecer las luchas?


Más que importante, es fundamental. Cuando en un mismo ámbito …

author: anred
title: Justicia para Cindy: a días del juicio, se pide máxima participación
content:
Bandera desplegada en la Asamblea de Abya Yala en el Encuentro Plurinacional MLTTBI y NB, en Córdoba este año. Foto: Sol Erazo.


El juicio se realizará el 2 y el 4 de noviembre en los Tribunales de Lomas de Zamora. La madre protectora de la niña convoca a personas y organizaciones a estar presentes en ambas jornadas

. Por Movimiento Etiopía para ANRed / Foto: Sol Erazo


Hace 10 años, durante demasiadas tardes en un conurbano silencioso, una niña sufría mientras su madre salía a trabajar. No sabía cómo contar que no le gustaba lo que su padre le hacía mientras la obligaba a guardar el secreto. La aterraba, le daba vergüenza y asco. No lo comprendía.


Cindy lo expresó con relatos, descripciones, cambios de humor abruptos y dibujos. Tenía solo 3 años. En ese escenario nunca antes vivido y sobre el cual nadie le había dicho qué hacer, su madre escuchó los pedidos de auxilio y le creyó a su hija. Confrontó al abusador.


“No lo vas a poder probar”, dijo él antes de ser expulsado del domicilio que compartían.


El recorrido legal comenzó con una denuncia, siguió con citaciones a juzgados, pericias e informes. Un difícil proceso en el que, además de lidiar con las vulneraciones padecidas, tuvieron que sufrir la violencia institucional de juezas y funcionarios.


Cuando una persona pide ayuda y en su lugar recibe más daño y se obstaculiza su derecho a alcanzar justicia, está siendo revictimizada. ¿Por qué el poder judicial tardó 10 años en llevar a juicio a un abusador? ¿Qué ocurre desde que una niña relata abusos sexuales hasta que esos hechos son efectivamente condenados? ¿Quiénes la cuidan?


Entre las acciones juzgadas socialmente como más aberrantes se encuentra el abuso sexual contra la niñez, que en muchos casos se devela luego de una clase de educación sexual integral en la escuela. Las niñas, niños y adolescentes que los padecen suelen ser amenazados con el fin de lograr que guarden silencio y no expongan a quienes los vulneraron.


Cuando el relato ocurre y pueden decir, ponerle palabras a aquello que les pasó, es imprescindible resguardar su integridad, creer, acompañar y actuar para evitar que continúen dañándoles. Quienes realizan estos hechos, de sometimiento sexual y dolor, no son monstruos ni fueron sacados de una película de terror. De acuerdo con el CEPASI (Centro de Prevención y Atención del Abuso Sexual en la Infancia y Adolescencia), en la Argentina, entre el 70 y 80% de los casos de abuso sexual son intrafamiliares y ocurren dentro del hogar. Aquí, como en la mayoría de los casos, se trataba de una persona en la que Cindy confiaba y a quien quería.


Durante los siguientes años, el progenitor acosó legalmente a la niña y a su madre formulando denuncias en las que argumentó impedimento de contacto y exigió la revinculación obligada. En todo momento, Cindy manifestó no querer verlo ni querer tener contacto con él. Pese a eso, a finales de 2017 una jueza de familia de Lomas de Zamora obligó a la niña a revincularse con el progenitor. En dicha ocasión, la niña padeció nuevas violencias sexuales teniendo 5 años de edad.


La jueza de familia, en lugar de atender lo expresado por la niña, la expuso nuevamente al peligro de encontrarse sola con quien la agredió desde su primera infancia. Esta decisión de la magistrada la convierte en responsable necesaria de las nuevas vulneraciones que promovió con su intervención.


Ante el accionar judicial insensible, Cindy y su madre se sostuvieron en el amor fraterno que las une y la red colectiva que las acompaña. Porque creerle a las niñas y niños es responsabilidad de toda la sociedad: debemos velar para que puedan tener una vida libre de violencias. Son sus derechos humanos, consagrados en la Convención de los derechos del niño (CN Art. 75 inc. 22), en la Ley nacional de promoción y protección de niñas, niños y adolescentes (Ley N° 26061/2005) y también en la ley provincial que atañe al presente abordaje, que obliga a un trato respetuoso y digno de niñas, niños y adolescentes (Ley N° 13298/2005).


Si se hubiera dado lugar a su voz, a su interés superior y a su bienestar integral, no hubiera quedado desprovista de protección por parte de las instituciones que debían priorizarla.


Luego de 10 años, llega a juicio oral en el TOC N° 9 de Lomas de Zamora la causa contra el abusador, en la que se espera se lo condene y se deje de torturar a la niña con su revinculación. Este 2 y 4 de noviembre, numerosas organizaciones y personas autoconvocadas estarán junto a Cindy …

author: Jazzy Mason
title: For Child Abuse Survivors Like Me, Prison Reactivates Familiar Trauma
content:
Prisons will continue to retraumatize survivors as long as society accepts control as care and punishment as protection.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The man in blue is yelling at me.

His voice slices the air before my mind can catch up. My body responds first — heart racing, shoulders tightening, breath shallow. I know this reaction intimately. It is older than this moment, older than this uniform. It lives in muscle memory, in skin, in a nervous system trained early to survive authority.

The man in blue is screaming commands, provoking my trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder, though he will never call it that. To him, this is procedure. Policy. Control. To my body, it is a return.

The man in blue is searching me.

His hands do not ask permission. They do not pause when my breath stutters or my knees lock. They move with confidence, backed by the state. I am reminded how I was touched as a child — how adults with power handled my body as if it belonged to them, as if consent were irrelevant. I am reminded how silence was demanded then, too.

The man in blue tells me when to bail, when to move, when to stop, when to stand still. His instructions echo older ones — less formal, more intimate, equally violating. I remember being taught how to perform, how to comply, how to disconnect from myself in order to endure.

The man in blue wakes me up by kicking my bed.

My body jerks awake before my mind does, flooded with fear. This is not the first time I have been startled out of sleep by a man who wanted control. As a child, nights were never safe. In prison, neither are mornings. There is no sanctuary here — only submission or punishment.

Prison does not create trauma in a vacuum. It activates it.

The man in blue is watching me.

Watching as I walk. Watching as I eat. Watching as I exist. Surveillance is constant, normalized, justified. When I was a child, being watched meant danger. In prison, it is framed as safety. My body does not know the difference.

The man in blue roughs me up and cuffs me while I am already down. My sobbing is muffled, ignored, treated as inconvenience. I am told to obey. I am told this is for my own good. I am told this is how order is maintained.

I have heard all of this before.

Prison does not create trauma in a vacuum. It activates it. For survivors of childhood abuse — especially sexual abuse — incarceration is not merely confinement. It is reenactment. Strip searches, body checks, constant surveillance, verbal degradation, forced compliance: These are not neutral practices. They mirror the dynamics of abuse with chilling precision.

The uniform changes, but the power imbalance does not.

In prison, authority is embodied. It has a voice, a posture, a right to touch, restrain, and command. The system does not ask what a body remembers. It does not care how trauma lives in the nervous system. It demands obedience anyway.

I was abused by men who were supposed to protect me — family members, trusted figures, authority disguised as care. They told me I was safe while they harmed me. They told me to be quiet. They told me to obey.

Later, the state told me the same things. The man in blue said he would protect me.

The lie landed the same way every time.

Incarceration relies on compliance. Compliance relies on fear. For trauma survivors, fear is already wired deep. Prison does not rehabilitate us — it exploits what was broken long before we arrived. Women and gender-nonconforming people are especially vulnerable. Many enter prison with extensive histories of physical and sexual violence. Yet carceral systems are not trauma-informed by design. They are trauma-producing.

Incarceration is not just about punishment. It is about power over bodies — especially bodies that have already been violated.

We are told that strip searches are about contraband. That restraints are about safety. That surveillance is about order. But when a system repeatedly violates bodies with known histories of abuse, intent becomes irrelevant. Impact is what matters.

And the impact is devastating. Nightmares intensify. Dissociation becomes survival. Panic attacks are disciplined as defiance. Emotional responses are written up as infractions. Survival instincts are punished.

This is not a failure of individual officers. It is a feature of the system.

The brutality and inhumanity of …

author: Maya Schenwar
title: Announcing the Winners of the 6th Annual Keeley Schenwar Memorial Essay Prize
content:
The prize honors the work of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated authors who are writing toward a more just world.

The prize honors the work of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated authors who are writing toward a more just world.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

As repression has escalated in so many realms of U.S. life over the past year and a half, we cannot allow ourselves to forget that nearly 2 million people in this country experience some of the most constant and brutal state repression, in the form of incarceration. Millions more are on probation, parole, electronic monitoring, or another form of non-institutional confinement that often leads straight back to incarceration. Meanwhile, 79 million people in this country live with a criminal record and all the barriers and obstacles that come with it, and nearly half of U.S. adults have an immediate family member who has been incarcerated. Too often, in moments of crisis and upheaval, attention turns away from the millions behind bars, and the many millions more who’ve been impacted by incarceration. We must uplift the stories of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated writers who are sharing their stories firsthand — and calling us to action.

Today, the Truthout Center for Grassroots Journalism is grateful to announce the winners of the sixth annual Keeley Schenwar Memorial Essay Prize. The prize, awarded to two formerly or currently incarcerated people for essays related to imprisonment or policing, is given in memory of my sister Keeley Schenwar (1990-2020), who was a devoted mother, daughter, sister, friend, writer, and advocate for incarcerated mothers. Each year, the selected essays share some of the spirit in which Keeley Schenwar moved through the world (and wrote her own work): a spirit of empathy, open-heartedness, and resistance. Each winner receives $3,000 and publication in Truthout. This year, we received 614 submissions — more than ever before — and each one shone a powerful light. We wish we could have chosen many more winners; selecting two is a near-impossible endeavor. We’re so grateful to everyone who trusted us to read their work, and to everyone who participated in the selection process. In addition to members of the Truthout team, we are very thankful for Joseph Peterson, who bottom-lined the program and correspondence process, and for our guest judge Colette Payne, a winner of the 2022 prize.

The 2026 winners of the Keeley Schenwar Memorial Essay Prize are Harlow Scott, author of “Cancer in Prison: A Death Sentence?” and Jazzy Mason, author of “For Child Abuse Survivors Like Me, Prison Reactivates Familiar Trauma.”

Harlow’s essay, “Cancer in Prison: A Death Sentence?” chronicles her diagnosis with colon cancer, 14 years into her prison sentence. She describes the medical neglect and abuse to which she’s been subjected — and the long-term deprivation of healthy food, safe conditions, and emotional well-being that makes incarcerated people more vulnerable to cancer. Guards shackled her in the hospital in the days after surgery, rendering it impossible to thoroughly clean her wounds. Returning to prison afterward, she was forced to ride in a vehicle meant for prison dogs. She must regularly drink water that has been deemed essentially unfit for human consumption. And yet, Harlow writes, “If I die today, I don’t want to be remembered as another number forgotten amongst the casualties of the prison system. I want to be remembered as a spontaneous shimmering light, dancing and free.”

Jazzy’s essay, “For Child Abuse Survivors Like Me, Prison Reactivates Familiar Trauma,” points to the way in which prison functions as sexual abuse, especially for those who survived such abuse before prison. She calls us to recognize the impact of this constant trauma reactivation for survivors behind bars. Jazzy writes, “For survivors of childhood abuse — especially sexual abuse — incarceration is not merely confinement. It is reenactment. Strip searches, body checks, constant surveillance, verbal degradation, forced compliance: these are not neutral practices. They mirror the dynamics of abuse with chilling precision.” Her essay also emanates a spirit of persistent resistance, which infuses every step of her struggle against the “man in blue.”

author: dev
title: Quelques notes sur la séquence en cours
content:
1.

 Sous le ciel, l'ordre déborde de cruauté. Il est temps de se lever. En nombre.


2.

 Politiser la plainte. Organiser la colère. Révolutionner la joie.


3.

 À chaque révolution, il y a eu des pillages. Le problème n'est pas de savoir s'il y a des pillages, mais s'il y a, sinon révolution, au moins le désir, l'envie, la passion, d'une révolution. C'est-à-dire quelque chose de l'ordre d'une dynamique émotive qui dépasse l'émeute évanescente et bascule vers une temporalité révolutionnaire. Le peuple est parfois acculé à une violence dont il ne voulait pas, mais qu'il assume.


4.

Entendons par émeute, un soulèvement populaire à parti d'un élan émotionnel partagé : colère, sentiment d'injustice, plainte… Pour l'historienne Sophie Wahnich, les émotions ne sont pas des

instincts


anhistoriques

 mais des

variables historiques

 [

1

]

.

C'est dans ce sens que l'on peut parler de dynamique émotive révolutionnaire. Bien sûr, cette dynamique ne sera pas la même à chaque fois qu'il y a révolution, puisqu'il n'y a pas Une mais des révolutions. Par-delà ou en-deça de la radicalisation ou non des discours, de la dynamique narrative des événements, il y a cet élément émotionnel, irréductible aux discours, mais très lié à la manière dont les gens agissent ou non dans une séquence. Lors de la journée de 24 octobre, plusieurs manifestations ont été interdites partout en France. Sur une pancarte, on pouvait lire : « Je suis en manifestation parce que j'ai peur d'aller en manifestation ».


5.

 Selon une très vieille grille de lecture des moments d'agitation populaire, les êtres humains en foule perdent leur humanité. Les instincts s'emparent d'eux ils agissent comme des bêtes. -

 Ah comme c'est déplorable !Comme c'est dommage ! On comprend bien sûr la colère mais...

 C'est alors le rôle des bergers, des chiens de garde, des éclaireurs de consciences, de ramener tout ce beau monde à la “raison”.


6.

 Depuis le 19

e

 siècle et l'ère des révolutions, il y a une ambivalence fondamentale dans les comportements des foules agitées. Freud qui ne peut nullement être qualifié de révolutionnaire ou d'agitateur public souligne ce double aspect : dans un rassemblement d'individus en foules, les inhibitions individuelles tombent, il est possible d'avoir une exaltation des pulsions mais il est tout aussi possible de voir se déployer un

grands accès de renoncement, de désintéressement, de dévouement à un idéal

 – Dignité, solidarité, égalité, liberté. Dans ce deuxième cas, on peut parler d'une “moralisation de l'individu par la foule”

 [

2

]

. Autrement dit, la foule peut rendre les être humains bestiaux ou inversement capables de participer à quelque chose de plus grand que leur petit Moi, Moi, Moi. Rien ne peut fixer en amont ou en aval l'une des deux directions. Rien ne peut trancher définitivement le triomphe de l'une et l'effacement de l'autre.


7.

 Lors des pillages en temps d'émeute, désinhibés, les individus profitent de l'occasion pour s'en mettre plein les poches. Mais les pillages peuvent être aussi le signe d'un communisme précaire, momentanément réalisé ; désinhibés, les individus se montrent capables de sortir des eaux glacés du calcul égoïste, s'emparant des objets non pas pour leur propre usage mais seulement pour le geste de s'en emparer et/ou de partager. Le 17 octobre, il y a eu des scènes qui attestent tout aussi bien de l'un que de l'autre. La question politique n'est pas statistique : combien de personnes ont pillés pour revendre leur butins, combien pour la simple joie de distribuer gratuitement, quel est leur profil sociologique, leur appartenance religieuse, etc. La question politique est celle des invisibilisations : qu'est-ce qui ne doit pas apparaître ? Qu'est-ce qui a lieu et pourtant est exclu du visible ?


8.

On comprend peut-être mieux pourquoi en ce moment, sur les plateaux télé et dans toute discussion respectable, il y a une condition d'entrée : condamner les pillages. On ne peut parler que si on accepte cete condition minimale : la nécessité du maintien de l'ordre et la défense de la propriété privée. Ce qui s'y joue fondamentalement, c'est l'exclusion des certaines personnes et des certaines pratiques de toute forme de “nous”.


9.

 À entendre les responsables politiques, les journalistes et les experts invités sur les plateaux télé, il existerait trois types de profils : les manifestants légitimes, les casseurs, les pilleurs. Autre nomination aujourd'hui répandue : la gauche …

title: HPG guerrillas: Our decision to join the movement is a commitment to Leader Öcalan’s manifesto
content:
The peace and democratic society process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan on February 27, 2025, has sparked new political debates and discussions about social change within Kurdish society. Young people who have since joined the Kurdish freedom movement also cite the Kurdish leader’s paradigm and his

Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto

 when explaining their decisions.


Two members of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG), Şoreş Botan and Dilsoz Sînornenas, explained their motivations to ANF, speaking about the social circumstances of Kurdish youth, the manifesto’s influence on their political development, and the significance of the peace process for their future path.


Şoreş Botan: The system deliberately targets young people


Şoreş Botan described the social conditions in North Kurdistan as a decisive factor in his decision. His remarks focused on assimilation policies targeting the Kurdish population, the situation of young people, and the political perspectives outlined in the manifesto.


Botan stated the following:


“After the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto reached the Kurdish people and their youth, it sparked extensive discussions. Its publication had a positive impact on society as a whole. Even before we joined the movement, discussions highlighted that the attacks of special warfare against our society had already begun. These attacks deliberately target young people in North Kurdistan in particular.


Young people are deliberately supplied with drugs on the streets to keep them away from the freedom movement. As a result, we become alienated from the social reality of our people. I witnessed this firsthand. Our aim was to avoid being drawn into this dirty system of genocide.


As Kurdish youth, we did not accept this. We had already adopted this stance before joining the movement. Our culture and language are under attack. In fact, the aim is to eradicate Kurdish society. We could not tolerate this. That is why I also decided to join the movement. The publication of the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto generated positive momentum within society.

Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] has been held under severe isolation for 27 years. This system of isolation is unacceptable. Even before joining the movement, we opposed the existing system. Leader Apo initiated a process two years ago. Subsequently, the manifesto was written and made available to the Kurdish people. This had a very positive impact on society. Following its publication, our goal as Kurdish society became to respond appropriately to Leader Apo’s call through our struggle.


When one studies the manifesto in depth, it becomes clear that Leader Apo provides answers to all social problems and develops appropriate solutions. I continue to read his writings to properly understand his ideas and grasp the depth of his perspective. I regard my decision to join the movement as one made following the publication of the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto. My efforts and struggle are aimed at living up to my leader’s expectations and supporting it.


With the publication of the manifesto, the women’s struggle has come even more prominently to the forefront, both as a social issue and in terms of its development. This has also become evident in various areas of the struggle. The manifesto has influenced the women’s struggle and society in many ways. The women’s struggle continues to expand day by day. We are convinced that the struggle and leading role of women will be further strengthened through the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto. Leader Apo wants women to assume a leading role in society and throughout the world. Our struggle is also developing on this basis.


Kurdish youth in particular should engage with the social realities addressed in the Peace and Democratic Society Manifesto and make greater efforts to read and understand it. In this way, it can also have a positive impact on them. We call on Kurdish youth to read the manifesto themselves and engage with Leader Apo’s ideas. This is what we expect from Kurdish youth.”

title: YBŞ and YJŞ: Success of the agreement depends on protecting Yazidi rights
content:
The Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ) have confirmed their agreement with the Iraqi government to integrate a total of 4,165 fighters into the state security forces. At a ceremony in the Shengal Mountains on Monday, the two forces stated that the success of the agreement would depend on whether the rights of the Yazidi population were protected, the consequences of the genocide were addressed, and the agreed commitments were fulfilled.


Alongside YBŞ and YJŞ fighters and commanders, the ceremony was attended by Iraq’s Deputy Prime Minister, the Governor of Mosul, representatives of the Iraqi security authorities, as well as Yazidi mothers and religious dignitaries.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/fc8e17e7_20261026105003_2026-10-26-sengal-ybs-sengaldeki-entegrasyona-dair-aciklama-1.mp4


Independent military status to be terminated


In their joint statement, the YBŞ and YJŞ confirmed that they had reached an agreement with Baghdad to end their independent military status. Their forces will operate within Iraqi security institutions in the future. Control over their weapons will also be transferred to the state in accordance with the agreed arrangements. The decision was made out of a sense of responsibility for Shengal’s security and in recognition of Iraq’s territorial integrity.


At the same time, the YBŞ and YJŞ emphasized that their integration was subject to clear commitments: “The prerequisite is that the agreed provisions are implemented, the rights of our male and female fighters are upheld, the dignity of our fallen fighters is protected, and the security of Shengal, as well as the rights and autonomy of its people, are guaranteed.”


530 fighters martyred and hundreds wounded


The statement recalled the genocide committed by ISIS against the Yazidi population in August 2014. When the terrorist organization occupied large parts of Iraq, including Mosul, the YBŞ and YJŞ emerged from the resistance against the attacks on Shengal. The units emphasized that their establishment was directly linked to the Yazidi people’s struggle for survival. “Our units fought a war of defense and liberation. In protecting our people and our land, we lost 530 fighters and suffered hundreds of injuries. Following the defeat of ISIS, we were the first forces to raise the Iraqi flag in Shengal. We have never abandoned our duty to protect our people.”


During the ceremony, tribute was paid to Ebu Nuri, Mam Zekî, Şêx Xeyri, Bêrîvan, Berfîn, Zerdeşt Şengalî, Mecid Temimi, and Merwan Bedel, as well as all those who lost their lives in the resistance against ISIS.


Investigating the genocide and ensuring the return of displaced people


For the YBŞ and YJŞ, the military agreement represents only one part of the necessary steps. They are calling for the fate of Yazidis who have been missing since the genocide to be clarified and for justice to be delivered to the victims’ families. They also emphasize the need to create conditions for the return of displaced people and to advance the reconstruction of Shengal.


The units are also demanding the strengthening of civilian institutions and local self-governance. Accordingly, all communities in Shengal must be involved in political decision-making. Only in this way, they say, can a democratic system be established that serves the interests of the entire population. In their statement, the YBŞ and YJŞ thanked the Iraqi government and all those who have supported the Yazidis since the genocide. They called for this cooperation to continue during the practical implementation of the agreement.


‘We will continue to fulfill our responsibilities’


In closing, the YBŞ and YJŞ addressed the families of the martyrs, wounded, and missing, as well as the entire Yazidi population. “We have fulfilled our responsibilities on the front lines of the struggle. Today, we will continue to fulfill them in a new phase in which the unity and sovereignty of Iraq, the security of Shengal, the dignity of its people, and the building of a stable and just future for all take precedence.”


They emphasized that their obligation to the martyrs was to protect what they had given their lives for. Ultimately, they said that the success of the resistance against the genocide must be measured by whether the Yazidis can exercise their rights and continue to live freely and in safety.
